the gcd of the row multiplicities is not a complete component invariant.
For the first all-degree-at-least-two source deficit,

```text
remainder=[2^+,2^+,3^-,4^+,5^+],       target=2,
```

the two component sizes are `15,120` and `720`, and again only the first is
loaded.  The strict `gt-bk-single-loaded` sweep passed all `1,868`
support-disjoint source-deficit cases with at most six factors, labels and
targets at most four, and total degree at most sixteen.  This property is
special to the relevant signed sector: the unsigned degree vector
`[2,2,2,2,2,2]` already has two different components containing admissible
cuts.  Hence a proof may use the source-deficit and support-disjoint sign
hypotheses, but cannot assume a universal unique decomposable orbit.

The fibres also admit a matching-theoretic model which exposes where a
non-Boolean syzygy could live.  For a state `(prec,alpha)`, make
`alpha_v` top tokens and `beta_v=d_v-alpha_v` bottom tokens at every vertex.
Join a top token at `u` to a bottom token at `v` precisely when `u` precedes
`v` in `prec`.  This is a Ferrers bipartite graph `H_(prec,alpha)`.

**Lemma 22F5 (Ferrers separation form).**  A cut `T` is admissible for
`(prec,alpha)` if and only if both vertex-induced bipartite graphs

```text
H[T]  and  H[T^c]
```

have perfect matchings, where the target belongs to `T^c`.

**Proof.**  List the top and bottom tokens of one induced graph in
nondecreasing vertex order.  Because its adjacency matrix is Ferrers, it has
a perfect matching if and only if the `j`-th top token precedes the `j`-th
bottom token for every `j`; when this holds, pairing equal ranks is already
a perfect matching.  Equality of the two token counts is the terminal queue
condition, and the rank-by-rank inequalities are exactly the prefix queue
conditions in `(P22.16)`.  Apply this separately to `T` and `T^c`.  QED.

Thus Target 22F3 is an averaged signed uncrossing theorem for balanced
vertex separations of Ferrers graphs which remain perfectly matchable on
both sides.  The failure of the whole-fibre Boolean rule above says that the
standard lattice of membership atoms alone does not prove the required
uncrossing; a successful differential must also use alternating matching
paths, or equivalently the adjacent state transport `(P22.18)`.

The admissible-cut family is not a delta-matroid, so its matching
description cannot be promoted to a symmetric-exchange proof.  Take the
four-block Dyck state

```text
alpha=[1,1,1,0],                 beta=[0,0,0,3].
```

Its complete target-free feasible-cut family is exactly

```text
Fhat={emptyset,{0,1,2,3}}.
```

Indeed every proper nonempty cut gives one colour a nonzero terminal queue
height.  For the two feasible sets, choose `e=0` in their symmetric
difference.  Toggling `e`, either alone or together with any other element
of that difference, gives a nonempty proper cut and is infeasible.  This
violates the symmetric-exchange axiom.  The strict C++ diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_bk_cut_deltamatroid.cpp` reproduces this
minimal obstruction.  Thus even the Ferrers matching formulation retains
the genuinely non-matroidal global allocation problem.

The queue formulation has an exact finite-level analogue.  For an ordered
list `d_1,...,d_m` and a level-`k` fusion path

```text
h_0=0,h_1,...,h_m=0,
```

put

```text
alpha_i=(d_i+h_i-h_(i-1))/2,       beta_i=d_i-alpha_i. (P22.31)
```

**Lemma 22G (two-sided level queue).**  Level-`k` invariant fusion paths are
in bijection with integer vectors in `(P22.31)` satisfying, at every step,

```text
0<=alpha_i,beta_i<=d_i,
beta_i<=h_(i-1),                 alpha_i<=k-h_(i-1),
h_i=h_(i-1)-beta_i+alpha_i.                       (P22.32)
```

Thus `beta_i` consumes the lower queue while `alpha_i` consumes the upper
hole queue.  Omitting the upper inequality recovers the ordinary queue in
Lemma 22F.

**Proof.**  The ordinary Clebsch--Gordan conditions for
`V_(h_(i-1)) tensor V_(d_i)` are equivalent to the integrality in `(P22.31)`,
`0<=alpha_i,beta_i<=d_i`, and `beta_i<=h_(i-1)`.  The extra affine-wall
condition is

```text
h_(i-1)+d_i+h_i<=2k.
```

Substituting `h_i=h_(i-1)+d_i-2beta_i` turns it into
`h_(i-1)+alpha_i<=k`, which is the upper inequality in `(P22.32)`.
Every transformation is reversible.  QED.

Lemma 22G identifies the uniform finite target: construct the required
odd-to-positive matching on pairs of two-sided queue paths using moves that
preserve both inequalities in `(P22.32)`.  Such a matching would prove
`(PCP_k)` simultaneously for every `k`; dropping the upper queue would give
the ordinary matching studied in Targets 22C--22F.

The ordinary Bender--Knuth transport does not preserve this two-sided
state space.  Thus the finite matching cannot be obtained by applying
`(P22.18)` and then checking the upper queue afterwards.

**Proposition 22G1 (affine Bender--Knuth ceiling obstruction).**  At level
`k=2`, take the ordered degree list and finite top vector

```text
d=[1,1,2,2],                 alpha=[1,0,2,0].
```

They give the valid finite height path

```text
0 -> 1 -> 0 -> 2 -> 0.
```

Apply the ordinary Bender--Knuth switch `(P22.18)` at the middle positions
of degrees `1,2`.  Its transfer is zero, and it gives

```text
d'=[1,2,1,2],                alpha'=[1,2,0,0].
```

The new second step would have height three.  Equivalently, its upper queue
condition in `(P22.32)` is

```text
alpha'_2=2 > k-h_1=1.
```

Hence the ordinary switch sends a valid `SU(2)_2` fusion path outside the
finite path set.

**Proof.**  For the original vector, the successive pairs
`(alpha_i,beta_i)` are

```text
(1,0), (0,1), (2,0), (0,2).
```

They satisfy both lower and upper inequalities in `(P22.32)` at heights
`0,1,0,2`, and return to zero.  Before the switched pair the height is one,
while its two bottom entries are one and zero.  Formula `(P22.17)` therefore
gives `z=0`; substitution in `(P22.18)` gives the displayed `d',alpha'`.
At its second step the upper condition fails as stated.  QED.

The strict C++ probe

```text
character_ring_iter/probe_su2_finite_bk_exchange.cpp
```

enumerates finite paths from `(P22.32)`, applies the ordinary switch, and
fails closed on the displayed witness:

```text
SU2_FINITE_BK_ORDINARY_TRANSPORT result=FAIL level=2
degrees=[1,1,2,2] top=[1,0,2,0] position=1
swapped_degrees=[1,2,1,2] swapped_top=[1,2,0,0].
```

Consequently the finite global-payment lemma needs an intrinsically affine
transport--for example a packet-valued `q`-recoupling move which retains the
upper-hole queue--rather than the ordinary BK component graph.

There is nevertheless an exact local *uncoloured* affine transport.  It is
the appropriate replacement for `(P22.18)` at the level of fusion paths.

**Lemma 22G2 (rank-preserving finite path recoupling).**  Consider two
adjacent labels `a,b` in a level-`k` fusion path, with incoming, intermediate,
and outgoing labels `h,r,t`.  Put

```text
I_(a,b)(h,t)=(h star_k a) intersection (t star_k b),
I_(b,a)(h,t)=(h star_k b) intersection (t star_k a).
                                                               (P22.33)
```

Both are increasing parity intervals and have the same cardinality.  Map
the `j`th member of `I_(a,b)(h,t)` to the `j`th member of
`I_(b,a)(h,t)`.  Replacing `r` by this member after interchanging `a,b`
gives a bijection of finite fusion paths; applying it again is the inverse.

**Proof.**  The first interval indexes the multiplicity-free summands in

```text
Hom(V_t,V_h tensor V_a tensor V_b),
```

when `V_a` is fused first, and the second indexes the same space when
`V_b` is fused first.  Associativity gives equality of their cardinalities.
Every finite `SU(2)_k` fusion interval is an increasing step-two interval,
so equal rank is a bijection.  The incoming and outgoing labels are fixed,
and the selected new intermediate label belongs to both required fusion
intervals, hence it gives a valid two-sided-queue path.  Swapping back
uses the same two ordered intervals and restores the original rank.  QED.

For the obstruction in Proposition 22G1, the ordinary invalid intermediate
label three is replaced by the sole finite intermediate label one, producing
the valid swapped path

```text
0 -> 1 -> 1 -> 2 -> 0,
alpha'=[1,1,1,0].
```

The probe's `recoupling` mode checks this bijection and its involutivity
through increasingly nontrivial boxes:

```text
level vertices max label  finite paths  tested swaps  result
  2       4        2               9             27  PASS
  4       5        4             940          3,760  PASS
  6       6        6         117,032        585,160  PASS.
```

The rank correspondence in Lemma 22G2 has an explicit crystal realization.
This supplies the coherence that is needed to organize local moves globally.
Let two adjacent labels be `a,b`, and let their down-counts in the
two-sided queue of Lemma 22G be

```text
u=a-alpha_i,                    v=b-alpha_(i+1).
```

Put

```text
c=min(v,a-u),                   d=u+v-c,
u'=min(d,b-c),                  v'=c+max(0,d-b+c).  (P22.34)
```

After interchanging `a,b`, replace the two top counts by

```text
alpha'_i=b-u',                  alpha'_(i+1)=a-v'. (P22.35)
```

**Lemma 22G3 (finite crystal realization and Coxeter coherence).**  The
map `(P22.34)--(P22.35)` is exactly the rank-preserving finite recoupling of
Lemma 22G2.  In particular, if `s_i` denotes this map at positions
`i,i+1`, then on every level-`k` fusion path

```text
s_i^2=1,
s_i s_j=s_j s_i                    when |i-j|>1,
s_i s_(i+1)s_i=s_(i+1)s_i s_(i+1).              (P22.36)
```

Thus ordered-rank recoupling gives a coherent symmetric-group transport of
finite fusion paths.  This does not yet prove `(PCP_k)`: it does not allocate
the two colours or resolve Plucker collisions.

**Proof.**  Write `h` and `t` for the incoming and outgoing heights.  The
old and new intermediate labels are

```text
r=h+a-2u,                     r'=h+b-2u',
t=h+a+b-2(u+v).                                   (P22.37)
```

The two possible intermediate intervals have lower endpoints

```text
L_(a,b)=max(|h-a|,|t-b|),
L_(b,a)=max(|h-b|,|t-a|).
```

Substituting `(P22.34)` into `(P22.37)` and splitting only according to
which argument realizes each `min` gives

```text
r-L_(a,b)=r'-L_(b,a).                              (P22.38)
```

Both intervals have step two, so `(P22.38)` says precisely that `r` and
`r'` have the same ordinal rank.  Lemma 22G2 therefore identifies
`(P22.34)--(P22.35)` with its finite recoupling map, and in particular
proves preservation of both queue bounds.

Formula `(P22.34)` is the two-letter type-`A_1` crystal `R` rule: pair the
`v` down-tokens of the right factor with the `a-u` up-tokens of the left
factor, then exchange the two residual strings.  For three factors the
noncrossing signature pairing of all down-tokens to the available up-tokens
is independent of whether the left or the right adjacent pair is exchanged
first.  This gives the braid relation in `(P22.36)`; pairing twice restores
the two original residual strings, and disjoint pairs use disjoint strings.
These give involutivity and distant commutation.  QED.

The strict `coherence` mode of
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_finite_bk_exchange.cpp` checks all three
relations in `(P22.36)` and independently checks equality of
`(P22.34)--(P22.35)` with the interval-rank recoupling.  The following
exhaustive boxes pass:

```text
level vertices max_label finite_paths  braid tests  distant tests
  4       5        4             940         2,820          2,820
  6       6        6         117,032       468,128        702,192
  6       7        3          26,635       133,175        266,350
  8       6        4          31,282       125,128        187,692
  8       7        4         336,261     1,681,305      3,362,610.
```

Its independent `crystal-r 20` mode verifies the unrestricted token formula
itself on `53,361` two-token involutions and `12,326,391` three-token braid
instances.  These finite checks audit the formula and its implementation;
the signature-pairing argument above is the uniform proof.

This is a proved local path bijection, not yet the finite global lemma: a
cut is a pair of coloured paths, and the rank map in `(P22.33)` need not
preserve its two factorisations.  The next finite task is therefore to
replace this scalar bijection by a packet/Temperley--Lieb transport whose
boundary terms are injectively paid by even channels.

The scalar recoupling nevertheless extends coherently to the *tickets* of a
fixed two-colour channel.  This removes the affine-wall obstruction from
transport in the order graph; what remains is the allocation of the
transported tickets.

**Lemma 22G4 (coherent two-colour finite-ticket transport).**  Keep a
named remainder list, adjoin a fixed target vertex `star` of label `p`, and
let a channel ticket for a cut `T` consist of a level-`k` invariant fusion
path on the ordered vertices of `T` and one on the ordered vertices of
`T^c union {star}`.  Track the named vertices under an adjacent
transposition of the remainder order.

If the transposed vertices have different cut colours, identify both paths
unchanged.  If they have the same colour, apply the rank-preserving
recoupling of Lemma 22G2 to their adjacent entries in that colour's path,
and leave the other path unchanged.  These maps are bijections of finite
channel tickets.  As the adjacent transposition varies, they satisfy the
Coxeter relations, preserve the cut sign, and preserve both finite queue
bounds.

**Proof.**  When the two colours differ, deleting the vertices of the other
colour leaves the ordered sequence on each side unchanged.  When they
agree, they are adjacent in their common restricted sequence, so Lemma 22G2
gives a bijection of precisely that finite fusion path and fixes its two
external heights.  The path on the other side is untouched.  Thus both
factorisations remain invariant and both two-sided queue bounds hold.

Involutivity and distant commutation follow factorwise from Lemma 22G3.
For a braid on three named vertices, the all-one-colour case is exactly the
braid relation in Lemma 22G3.  Otherwise each colour occurs once or twice.
The singleton-colour path is unchanged, while the two entries of the
repeated colour are reversed exactly once on either side of the braid and
receive the same rank recoupling.  The two composites therefore agree.
Finally the cut is a fixed set of named vertices, so its sign and its odd or
even parity are unchanged.  QED.

Consequently the odd and even finite channel tickets form coherent bundles
over the factor-order graph.  A finite proof may therefore transport a
candidate global Hall allocation through arbitrary reorderings without ever
leaving `SU(2)_k`.  Lemma 22G4 does not itself compare odd demand with even
capacity: multiplication of the two transported paths still has the
Plucker/Temperley--Lieb collisions isolated in Targets 22C2 and 22H3.

The strict `coloured-ticket` mode of
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_finite_bk_exchange.cpp` independently
enumerates both colour-path bases, applies the stated transport, and checks
involutivity, braid coherence, and distant commutation.  It passed the
complete boxes

```text
level vertices max_label degree words tickets swaps braids distant
  4       5        3          243     1,590  6,360  4,770   4,770
  6       6        3          729    18,998 94,990 75,992 113,988.
```

The audit uses two invariant colour paths; adjoining an untouched target
leaf to either colour gives the channel-ticket convention in Lemma 22G4.
These checks certify the finite implementation of the proved transport and
make no claim about the unresolved Plucker/Temperley--Lieb allocation.

Thus the remaining proof cannot be an order-independent polymatroid
exchange, an order-independent pairwise XOR injection, or a fibrewise
parity theorem.  The surviving statement is the adaptive cumulative Hall
matching of Target 22C2, or the weaker rank-plateau statement Target 22F1.

Two still stronger fixed-degeneration shortcuts are also false.  In the squarefree
Stanley--Reisner degeneration of the Plucker ring, crossing products vanish.
For remainder labels `[1,1,1,1]`, target `2`, and minus mask `3`, the odd
source dimension is four, its degenerate rank is one, and the nonempty even
supply is two.  Thus the special-fibre kernel has dimension three and is too
large by one.  In the domain Gelfand--Tsetlin degeneration a fixed vertex
order can also lose too much rank: for support-disjoint labels
`[1,1,2,2,3]`, target `1`, and minus mask `3`, the odd source dimension,
degenerate rank, and nonempty even supply are respectively `8,2,5`.
Reordering the six vertices as `[0,2,4,1,3,5]` raises the rank to six and
makes every tableau fibre satisfy `(P22.9)`.  Hence neither standard fixed
degeneration proves even the aggregate estimate automatically.

The strict exact C++ diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/analyze_su2_plucker_sr_parity.cpp` constructs both
degenerations and the tableau fibres.  Its order-adapted support-disjoint
fibre-order mode passed all 505 cases with at most six factors, remainder labels at most
three, targets at most three, and total degree at most fourteen.  A wider
replay passed all 2,422 support-disjoint cases with at most seven factors,
labels and targets at most four, and total degree at most sixteen.  Proposition
22B first occurs beyond that replay's total-degree cutoff.  Outside the
support-disjoint sector the fibrewise claim itself can fail for every vertex
order: six label-two factors, target two, and three minus copies have a fibre
with six odd and four even cuts.  Proposition 5 removes precisely this type
of mixed-sign equal-label case before Target 22B is invoked.
The earlier bounded replay is recorded in
`certificates/su2_plucker_gt_sd_best_4_7_4_16.log`.

The divided-difference factorization used earlier for the all-minus search
has a useful categorical and finite-level form.  In the ordinary
representation ring, or in `R_k` with `q<=k`, put

```text
Delta=e_1 tensor e_0-e_0 tensor e_1,
S_q=e_q tensor e_0+e_0 tensor e_q,
D_q=sum_(j=0)^(q-1) e_(q-1-j) tensor e_j.               (P23.1)
```

**Proposition 23 (fundamental-difference normal form).**  One has

```text
e_q tensor e_0-e_0 tensor e_q=Delta D_q.                (P23.2)
```

Consequently every signed remainder with `m` minus factors has the exact
form

```text
R=Delta^m H,
H=product_(i minus)D_(q_i) product_(i plus)S_(q_i).      (P23.3)
```

Here `H` is exchange-symmetric and belongs to the nonnegative tensor-product
basis cone.  Thus `(PCP)` and `(PCP_k)` reduce to the single rank-one target

```text
(id tensor tau)(Delta^m H) belongs to the nonnegative cone              (FDC)
```

for `H` in the multiplicative cone generated by the `D_q` and `S_q`.

**Proof.**  Write `e_q=U_q(e_1/2)`.  The divided-difference identity

```text
[U_q(X/2)-U_q(Y/2)]/(X-Y)
   =sum_(j=0)^(q-1)U_(q-1-j)(X/2)U_j(Y/2)               (P23.4)
```

follows by telescoping the recurrence
`XU_j(X/2)=U_(j+1)(X/2)+U_(j-1)(X/2)`.  Substituting
`X=e_1 tensor e_0` and `Y=e_0 tensor e_1` proves `(P23.2)`.
All indices in `D_q` are at most `q-1`; hence the same telescoping uses no
affine wall when `q<=k`, and the identity remains exact in every `R_k`.
Multiplying `(P23.2)` over the minus factors gives `(P23.3)`.  Every `D_q`
and `S_q` is symmetric and coefficientwise nonnegative, proving the final
assertions.  QED.

After the principal specialization used in Proposition 18, `(P23.2)` reads

```text
P_q(t)-t^(q/2)chi_q(y)
 =[1+t-t^(1/2)chi_1(y)]
   sum_(j=0)^(q-1)t^(j/2)P_(q-1-j)(t)chi_j(y).           (P23.5)
```

There is an exact supermodule behind both factors in `(P23.5)`.  Put
`a=t^(1/2)`, let `V=V_1`, and grade

```text
E=exterior^bullet(aV)=1 direct-sum aV direct-sum a^2 1.  (P23.6)
```

Here the displayed expression is the ordinary graded character; its
supercharacter is

```text
B(a,y)=1-a chi_1(y)+a^2.                                (P23.7)
```

**Lemma 23A (exterior--symmetric-power form).**  For every `q>=1`,

```text
Q_q(a,y)=sum_(j=0)^(q-1) a^j P_(q-1-j)(a^2) chi_j(y)
        =character Sym^(q-1)(E),                         (P23.8)

P_q(a^2)-a^q chi_q(y)=B(a,y)Q_q(a,y).                   (P23.9)
```

Consequently the outer polynomial `A_R` is the invariant super-Hilbert
polynomial of the genuine graded supermodule

```text
K_R=
 tensor_(i minus)[exterior^bullet(aV) tensor Sym^(q_i-1)(E)]
 tensor_(i plus)[(direct-sum_(j=0)^q_i a^(2j)1)
                  direct-sum a^(q_i)V_(q_i)],           (P23.10)
```

where parity occurs only in the first exterior factor of each minus
position.

**Proof.**  If `z,z^(-1)` are the weights of `V`, then

```text
sum_(n>=0) character Sym^n(E) u^n
 =1/[(1-u)(1-a^2u)(1-azu)(1-az^(-1)u)].                 (P23.11)
```

The first two denominator factors have coefficient `P_l(a^2)` in degree
`l`, and the last two have coefficient `a^j chi_j(y)` in degree `j`.
Convolution gives `(P23.8)`, while `(P23.9)` is `(P23.5)`.  Multiplying the
supercharacters of the factors in `(P23.10)` and extracting `SU(2)`
invariants gives exactly `(P18.3)`.  QED.

The minus-factor supermodule has a natural Koszul differential, and its
homology is completely explicit.  Write

```text
E=kx direct-sum V direct-sum kz
```

with `a`-degrees `0,1,2`.  For `v in V`, let `A_v(x)=v` and let `A_v`
vanish on `V direct-sum kz`.  The operators `A_v` commute, and they induce
commuting derivations `D_v` on `Sym^n(E)`.  Use the invariant symplectic
form to identify `V` with its dual.

**Lemma 23A1 (factorwise Koszul resolution).**  For `n=q-1`, the operator

```text
d_q=sum_i iota_(v_i) tensor D_(v^i)
```

is an odd `SU(2)`-equivariant differential on

```text
exterior^bullet(aV) tensor Sym^n(E).
```

It preserves total `a`-degree, and its homology is

```text
H_0=direct-sum_(j=0)^(q-1) a^(2j) 1,
H_1=direct-sum_(j=0)^(q-1) a^(q+j) V_(q-j),
H_2=direct-sum_(j=0)^(q-1) a^(q+1+j) V_(q-1-j).       (P23.11a)
```

Consequently its homology Euler character is

```text
P_q(a^2)-a^q chi_q=B(a,y)Q_q(a,y).                   (P23.11b)
```

**Proof.**  The contractions anticommute and the `D_v` commute, so
`d_q^2=0`.  Contraction lowers exterior degree by one, while `D_v` replaces
`x` by a vector of `a`-degree one, so total `a`-degree is preserved.  In
coordinates `y_1,y_2` on `V`, one has `D_i=y_i partial_x`.  Decomposition
first by the power `z^j` and then by
`deg_x-exterior_degree` gives homogeneous strands of the Koszul complex
for the regular sequence `(y_1,y_2)`.  All interiors are exact.  In degree
zero only `x^(n-j)z^j` survives.  In degree two the `x`-degree-zero endpoint
is `z^j Sym^(n-j)(V) tensor exterior^2(V)`.  In degree one, quotienting the
`x`-degree-zero endpoint by the incoming Koszul image leaves
`z^j V_(n-j+1)`.  These are exactly `(P23.11a)`.  The terms `H_1(j)` for
`1<=j<=q-1` equal the graded
characters `H_2(j-1)`.  The unpaired terms are `a^qV_q` in odd degree and
`a^(2q)1` in even degree, which with `H_0` give `(P23.11b)`.  QED.

This factorwise resolution does not make invariant homology even in the
outer range.

The most immediate attempt to couple different minus factors gives no new
homological payment.  This closes the natural ``generic mixed Koszul
differential'' shortcut, but does not restrict operations which also use
plus factors.

**Proposition 23A1B (cross-minus Koszul rigidity).**  Let there be `m`
minus factors in `(P23.10)`.  On their tensor product, for a scalar matrix
`C=(c_(ij))`, define

```text
d_C=sum_(i,j=1)^m c_(ij) sum_(epsilon=+,-)
       iota_(i,epsilon) D_(j,epsilon).                 (P23.11bc)
```

Here `iota_(i,epsilon)` contracts the `epsilon`-weight exterior generator
in the `i`th copy of `exterior^bullet(V)`, while `D_(j,epsilon)` is the
derivation on the `j`th symmetric factor which sends its generator `x_j`
to the corresponding weight vector of `V` and kills all other generators.
The plus factors are left unchanged.  Then `d_C` is an odd,
`SU(2)`-equivariant, outer-degree-preserving differential.  Moreover, in
every fixed outer degree,

```text
dim H_odd(d_C)^SU(2) >= dim H_odd(d_I)^SU(2).          (P23.11bd)
```

Thus cross-minus contractions alone cannot improve on the factorwise
Koszul differential.

**Proof.**  The contractions anticommute and all the derivations commute.
Every pair of summands in `d_C^2` therefore cancels with the reversed pair,
while an individual square is zero.  Each summand removes and creates the
same `SU(2)` weight and changes the total `a`-degree by `-1+1=0`; this
proves the first assertion.

Identify the exterior product of the minus factors with

```text
exterior^bullet(V tensor C^m).                         (P23.11be)
```

If `C` is invertible, a change of the `C^m` exterior generators conjugates
`d_I` to `d_C` (with the inverse transpose on contractions).  Hence the
ranks of both parity maps, and their invariant homology dimensions, are
constant on the nonempty open set `det(C)!=0`.

Fix one outer degree and restrict to `SU(2)` invariants.  The two
differential matrices have entries linear in `C`.  A minor nonzero at any
matrix `C_0` is a nonzero polynomial and is therefore nonzero at some
invertible matrix.  Consequently each parity rank at `C_0` is at most its
common invertible value.  Since

```text
dim H_odd=dim C_odd-rank(d: C_odd -> C_even)
                     -rank(d: C_even -> C_odd),
```

this proves `(P23.11bd)`.  QED.

For the first obstruction of Lemma 23A2, the strict C++ calculation
`character_ring_iter/probe_su2_cross_koszul.cpp` constructs the entire
outer-degree-six invariant complex for
`[3^-,3^-,1^+,2^+,2^+]`.  It obtains

```text
coupling       rank even->odd  rank odd->even  H_even  H_odd
I                         129             133      38     10
[[1,1],[1,2]]             129             133      38     10
[[1,1],[1,1]]             112             112      76     48.
                                                               (P23.11bf)
```

All three differentials square to zero and commute with the raising
operator exactly modulo the prime `1,000,003`.  This is an implementation
check of the uniform rigidity proof, not evidence for a broader global
claim.  A successful global payment differential must contain arrows which
involve plus factors or genuinely higher operations.

**Lemma 23A2 (factorwise-homology obstruction).**  Give every minus factor
of `(P23.10)` its differential `d_q`, give the plus factors zero
differential, and take the tensor-product differential.  For

```text
R=[3^-,3^-,1^+,2^+,2^+],                 p=5,
```

its homology has a nonzero odd invariant in the outer grade `a^6`.

**Proof.**  Here the label sum of `R` is `11`, so the coefficient of
`V_5` occurs in grade `a^(11-5)=a^6`.  Choose the essential odd class
`a^3V_3` from one minus factor, the degree-zero scalar from the other,
`aV_1` from the plus label one, `a^2V_2` from one plus label two, and the
degree-zero scalar from the other.  Their tensor product has grade six and

```text
dim Hom_SU(2)(1,V_3 tensor V_1 tensor V_2)=1,
```

because `V_1 tensor V_2` contains `V_3`.  The indexed choices give at least
four such odd classes.  Kunneth's theorem makes them genuine homology
classes of the factorwise differential.  QED.

The obstruction in Lemma 23A2 has a unique lowest-degree binary correction,
but its local chain lift is curved.

**Lemma 23A3 (first cross-factor transvectant and curvature).**  For the
outer class in Lemma 23A2, the only lowest-degree binary
`SU(2)`-equivariant channel which can map it to an even invariant is

```text
V_3 tensor V_1 -> V_2.                               (P23.11c)
```

It sends the odd `a^3V_3` class of a minus factor, together with the
`aV_1` state of the plus-one factor, to the even `a^4V_2=H_2(j=0)` class.
No binary channel using a plus-two state works.

On chains, exterior multiplication by the plus vector `w` is the natural
order-zero lift:

```text
delta_w(alpha tensor f tensor w)
 =(w wedge alpha) tensor f tensor 1.
```

It satisfies

```text
delta_w^2=0,             {d,delta_w}=D_w.              (P23.11d)
```

In particular it does not extend the factorwise differential to a
bicomplex.  This curvature is unavoidable among order-zero binary lifts.

**Proof.**  Clebsch--Gordan gives
`V_3 tensor V_1=V_2 direct-sum V_4`, and the required even homology target
is `V_2`; hence `(P23.11c)` is unique up to scalar.  In contrast,
`V_3 tensor V_2=V_1 direct-sum V_3 direct-sum V_5` contains no `V_2`.
The Cartan identity between contraction and exterior multiplication gives
`(P23.11d)`.  It is nonzero already on
`x Sym^(q-2)(E)`.  Finally, the relevant equivariant Hom-space into
`exterior^2(V)` is one-dimensional, so every order-zero lift is a scalar
multiple of this one and has the same curvature.  QED.

There is an exact nonlocal lift for this first obstruction.  Choose the
`SU(2)`-invariant orthogonal deformation retract `(p,i,h)` of the
factorwise complex onto its homology, let `delta_H` be the map
`V_3 tensor V_1 -> V_2` from `H_1(j=0)` to `H_2(j=0)`, and put

```text
tilde_delta=i delta_H p.                              (P23.11e)
```

Then `{d,tilde_delta}=0` and `tilde_delta^2=0`.  Summing `(P23.11e)` over
the two minus factors in Lemma 23A2 pairs all four indexed odd invariants
with the corresponding even `V_2 tensor V_2` invariants at the reduced
essential-source level.  This does not yet remove them in the full homology
complex, because the same `H_2` classes are paired characterwise with
`H_1(j=1)` classes; Lemma 23A6B below gives the resulting Schur-complement
condition.  What remains is to redistribute those paired odd columns while
making the harmonic projections compatible across arbitrary factors and
grades, or to cancel the curvature `D_w` by higher-order terms satisfying
the resulting Maurer--Cartan equations.

The characterwise cancellations inside `(P23.11a)` cannot be performed
before constructing the cross-factor arrows.  If they are, the effective
minus and plus factors are

```text
M_q^eff=(direct-sum_(i=0)^q a^(2i)1)
          direct-sum Pi(a^q V_q),

P_r=(direct-sum_(j=0)^r a^(2j)1) direct-sum a^r V_r.  (P23.11f)
```

Here `Pi` denotes odd parity.

**Lemma 23A4 (effective binary-map classification).**  Every
degree-preserving equivariant binary odd map from the odd summand of
`M_q^eff tensor P_r` to its even part is a linear combination of the
following channels:

```text
a^qV_q tensor a^(2s)1 -> a^(2s)1 tensor a^rV_r,
    possible exactly when q=r;

a^qV_q tensor a^rV_r -> a^(2i)1 tensor a^(2t)1,
    possible exactly when q=r and i+t=q;

a^qV_q tensor a^rV_r -> a^q1 tensor a^rV_r,
    possible exactly when q is even and q<=2r.         (P23.11g)
```

In particular, if `q` is odd and support-disjoint from the plus labels,
every such effective binary map is zero.

**Proof.**  The target in the minus coordinate is scalar, while the only
plus-coordinate types are `1` and `V_r`.  Thus the relevant Hom-spaces are

```text
Hom(V_q,V_r),       Hom(V_q tensor V_r,1),
Hom(V_q tensor V_r,V_r).
```

The first two are nonzero exactly when `q=r`.  Clebsch--Gordan makes the
third one-dimensional exactly when `q` is even and `q<=2r`.  Equality of
the displayed `a`-degrees forces respectively `i=s`, `i+t=q`, and
`i=q/2`, giving `(P23.11g)`.  QED.

For the word of Lemma 23A2, all effective binary channels vanish:
`q=3` is odd and differs from the plus labels `1,2`.  The required
invariant is already ternary,

```text
V_3 tensor V_1 tensor V_2 -> 1.                       (P23.11h)
```

Retaining the characterwise cancellable `a^4V_2=H_2(j=0)` carrier instead
allows the binary transvectant `(P23.11c)`.  Therefore the paired
`H_1/H_2` summands are essential Hall capacity, despite cancelling in the
Euler character.  A derived proof must either retain them and solve the
overlapping-arrow relations, or use genuinely higher-arity operations on
the minimal effective object.

The higher-arity evaluation maps on the minimal object have a simple
classification and no square-zero obstruction.  For an odd minus summand
`Pi(a^qV_q)` and two nontrivial plus summands `a^rV_r,a^sV_s`, put

```text
alpha=(q+r-s)/2,       beta=(r+s-q)/2,
gamma=(s+q-r)/2.
```

**Lemma 23A5 (ternary evaluation differential).**  An invariant evaluation

```text
V_q tensor V_r tensor V_s -> 1                      (P23.11i)
```

exists exactly when

```text
|r-s|<=q<=r+s,                 q+r+s even.
```

It is unique up to scalar.  For every

```text
0<=i<=q, 0<=j<=r, 0<=l<=s,
i+j+l=(q+r+s)/2,
```

it gives a degree-preserving odd map

```text
Pi(a^qV_q) tensor a^rV_r tensor a^sV_s
 -> a^(2i)1 tensor a^(2j)1 tensor a^(2l)1.            (P23.11j)
```

The allocation `(i,j,l)=(alpha,beta,gamma)` is always available.
Any linear combination of such indexed ternary evaluations, extended by
the identity on untouched factors with Koszul signs, squares to zero.

**Proof.**  Clebsch--Gordan gives the stated admissibility and
one-dimensional Hom-space.  Equivalently, `(P23.11i)` contracts
`alpha,beta,gamma` pairs of fundamental indices between the three symmetric
powers.  Degree equality is exactly the displayed sum condition.  If two
ternary operations overlap, the first replaces every active summand on its
support by scalars, so the second composition is zero in either order.  If
their supports are disjoint, the two odd operations anticommute.  Hence the
square of their sum is zero.  QED.

For `(q,r,s)=(3,1,2)`, the canonical allocation is `(1,0,2)`.  On the word
of Lemma 23A2 it maps

```text
Pi(a^3V_3) tensor aV_1 tensor a^2V_2
 -> a^2 1 tensor 1 tensor a^4 1.
```

The choices of one of the two minus factors and one of the two plus-two
factors give four distinct outputs, so this ternary differential pairs all
four offending odd invariants with even ones.

The remaining obstruction is unbounded arity rather than the
Maurer--Cartan equation.  For example, in

```text
R=[5^-,3^-,1^+,2^+,2^+,2^+,2^+],          p=7,
```

the outer grade is `a^(17-7)=a^10` and contains the odd invariant

```text
a^5V_5 tensor aV_1 tensor a^2V_2 tensor a^2V_2,
```

because `V_1 tensor V_2 tensor V_2` contains `V_5`.  No pair among
`V_1,V_2,V_2` contains `V_5`, so every ternary evaluation vanishes on this
class; an arity-four evaluation is necessary.

More generally, take `q=2m+1` and

```text
R_m=[q^-,3^-,1^+,(2^+)^(2m)],              p=q+2.
```

The outer grade contains a class using `V_q`, `V_1`, and `m` of the
`V_2` factors.  Their highest weights sum to `q`, while every proper
subcollection has highest weight below `q`.  Thus killing this class on the
minimal effective object requires an operation involving the odd factor and
all `m+1` active plus factors.  The necessary arity is unbounded.  This
leads to an unbounded-hyperedge rank problem, even though the pure
evaluation operations themselves satisfy square zero automatically.

For exactly two minus factors, that rank problem has an exact bipartite
form.  Fix an outer `a`-degree.  A left vertex consists of

```text
(i,A,lambda, scalar grades off A),                    (P23.11k)
```

where minus factor `i` contributes its odd `a^(q_i)V_(q_i)` summand, `A`
is the indexed set of plus factors in their nontrivial `a^(r_j)V_(r_j)`
summands, `lambda` is a fusion-path basis vector in

```text
Inv(V_(q_i) tensor tensor_(j in A)V_(r_j)),
```

and every untouched factor has a specified scalar grade.  A right vertex
is an all-scalar allocation of the same total degree.  Join a left vertex
to a right vertex when the untouched scalar grades agree and the active
coordinates can be assigned

```text
0<=t_i<=q_i,              0<=t_j<=r_j,
sum_(i union A)t=(q_i+sum_(j in A)r_j)/2.             (P23.11l)
```

The edge map is the dual invariant `lambda^*` followed by insertion into
those scalar summands.

**Lemma 23A6 (pure-evaluation Hall reduction).**  A pure-evaluation
differential can be chosen injective on the outer odd subspace with exactly
one essential minus summand if and only if the bipartite graph
`(P23.11k)--(P23.11l)` satisfies

```text
|X|<=|N(X)|                         for every left set X. (P23.11m)
```

For every fixed active support `i union A`, these inequalities hold
automatically.

**Proof.**  The independent dual path functionals make the allowed
differential entries arbitrary scalars on precisely the displayed
bipartite support.  Full column rank is therefore equivalent to a matching,
which is `(P23.11m)`.  For the fixed-support assertion, order the active
labels `d_1,...,d_n` and write a fusion path as

```text
h_0=0, h_1,...,h_n=0.
```

Set

```text
alpha_k=(d_k+h_k-h_(k-1))/2.                          (P23.11n)
```

Fusion admissibility gives `0<=alpha_k<=d_k`, and telescoping gives
`sum_k alpha_k=sum_k d_k/2`.  Thus `(alpha_k)` is a neighboring scalar
allocation.  Conversely,
`h_k=h_(k-1)+2alpha_k-d_k`, so this map is injective on fusion paths.
QED.

Consequently the remaining theorem is not path capacity inside one support;
it is simultaneous assignment of scalar-grade markers across different
active supports and pre-existing scalar allocations.  The Hall condition is
a structured strengthening of aggregate dimension positivity, so it is not
equivalent to `(PCP)` merely from total dimensions.

There is a simultaneous injection for arbitrary top-path supports.  Fix the
selected minus factor and suppose

```text
q=sum_(j in A)r_j.
```

The invariant on that active support is the unique top fusion path.  Assign

```text
t_q=q-|A|,       t_j=1 for j in A,       t_j=0 off A. (P23.11o)
```

This is admissible because every `r_j>=1`; its index sum is `q`, half the
active label sum.  The coordinates equal to one recover `A`, so
`(P23.11o)` is collision-free across any family of top supports.

The family `R_m` above illustrates that unbounded arity need not cause a
rank failure.  For every `m`-subset `A` of the `2m` indexed plus-two
positions, the top fusion path

```text
V_(2m+1) subset V_1 tensor tensor_(j in A)V_2
```

is unique.  Send it to the scalar allocation having index `m+1` on the
selected minus factor, index zero on the plus-one factor, index one on
each selected plus-two factor, and index zero elsewhere.  The index sum is
`(m+1)+m=2m+1`, exactly half the active label sum.  The positions carrying
index one recover `A`, and the positive minus index records which equal
minus factor was selected when `m=1`.  Hence these
`binom(2m,m)` outer odd classes have a collision-free matching for every
`m`.

The universal scalar-output Hall theorem is nevertheless false.

**False Target 23A6A (cross-support scalar-marker theorem).**  Consider the
remainder

```text
R=[3^-,1^+,5^+,(2^+)^5]
```

at outer target `p=7`.  Its relevant `a`-degree is
`19-7=12`, or scalar-index sum six.  Fix the plus-five factor in scalar
grade zero.  Let `X` contain every state whose active support consists of
the plus-one factor and a `k`-subset `B` of the five indexed plus-two
factors, for `1<=k<=4`; give the inactive plus-two factors scalar indices
summing to `4-k`, and include every fusion path.

The four fusion multiplicities are

```text
dim Inv(V_3 tensor V_1 tensor V_2^k)=1,2,5,12,
                                             k=1,2,3,4,
```

while the numbers of inactive scalar assignments are respectively

```text
[x^(4-k)](1+x+x^2)^(5-k)=16,6,2,1.
```

Therefore

```text
|X|=5*1*16+10*2*6+10*5*2+5*12*1=360.               (P23.11p)
```

On the right, the scalar caps are `(3,1,2,2,2,2,2)` and their indices sum
to six, giving

```text
[x^6](1+x+x^2+x^3)(1+x)(1+x+x^2)^5=312
```

ambient allocations.  Write `C` for the inactive subset of plus-two
positions.  The edge condition is

```text
sum_(j in C)t_j=|C|-1,
```

or equivalently `#zeros in C=#twos in C+1`.  A nonempty proper `C` exists
exactly when at least one of the five indices is zero, by taking a singleton
zero.  Hence the only excluded allocations have no zero: five permutations
of `(2,1,1,1,1)` with the minus and plus-one indices both zero, and the two
allocations with all five indices one and those two remaining indices
`(1,0)` or `(0,1)`.  Thus

```text
|N(X)|=312-7=305<360=|X|.                            (P23.11q)
```

This exact Hall deficit of `55` proves that no scalar-marker choice,
including `(P23.11n)`, complements, rotations, or zero-sum transfers, can
give the universal injection.

The strict exact C++ verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_fdc_evaluation_hall.cpp` recomputes the
four fusion multiplicities, both bounded-composition counts, and the full
neighbor enumeration.  Its replay is recorded in
`certificates/su2_fdc_evaluation_hall.log`.

At the level of the reduced essential-source block, retaining the first
non-scalar carrier appears to repair this failure.  For `q=3`, the
essential odd class is `a^3V_3=H_1(j=0)` and the carrier is
`a^4V_2=H_2(j=0)`.  On a support containing the plus-one factor and `k`
plus-two factors, use

```text
pi_2:V_3 tensor V_1 -> V_2
```

and retain the active `V_2^k` tensor.  Since

```text
V_3 tensor V_1=V_2 direct-sum V_4,
```

the original, carrier, and residual multiplicities for `k=1,2,3,4` are

```text
m_k=(1,2,5,12),       c_k=(1,1,3,6),       d_k=(0,1,2,6). (P23.11r)
```

The carrier outputs remember the indexed active support and inactive scalar
grades, so they are collision-free.  Their total rank is

```text
5*16*1+10*6*1+10*2*3+5*1*6=230.                    (P23.11s)
```

The residual `V_4` blocks have `130` directions.  Their exact bipartite
graph against the `312` scalar allocations has matching rank `130`.
Consequently

```text
230+130=360,                                          (P23.11t)
```

for that reduced block.  This count is not the rank of a differential on
the full `H_1/H_2` space, because `H_2(j)` is already paired with the odd
column `H_1(j+1)`.

**Lemma 23A6B (carrier Schur-complement criterion).**  Let `C` be a paired
odd `H_1` block, `C'` its isomorphic even `H_2` block, `E` the essential
odd block, and `S` the remaining even block.  After normalizing the
pairing `C -> C'` to the identity, any proposed differential has block
matrix

```text
             C   E
partial = [  I   A  ] : C direct-sum E -> C' direct-sum S.
          [  D   B  ]
```

Its rank is

```text
rank(partial)=dim(C)+rank(B-DA).                      (P23.11t1)
```

In particular, if the paired columns have no redistribution map `D`, the
carrier block `A:E -> C'` contributes no rank beyond the identity pairing.

**Proof.**  Subtract from each column of `E` the corresponding linear
combination, prescribed by `A`, of the columns of `C`.  This invertible
column operation changes the matrix to

```text
[ I    0   ]
[ D  B-DA ],
```

which proves `(P23.11t1)`.  QED.

Therefore `(P23.11s)--(P23.11t)` prove only that the essential block embeds
after the paired `H_1` columns have been suppressed.  They do not repair
the full Hall deficit.  The same strict verifier and certificate recompute
the reduced carrier and residual ranks; they do not construct `D` or check
the Schur complement.  A valid carrier proof must redistribute the paired
odd columns and prove full rank of `B-DA`.

There is a uniform carrier hierarchy for every fixed active support in
ordinary `SU(2)`.  The carrier types in `(P23.11a)` can be rewritten as

```text
H_2(j)=a^(q+1+j)V_(q-1-j)
      =a^(2q-h)V_h,             0<=h<q.              (P23.11u)
```

For a chosen plus label `r`, every channel `h in q star r` with `h<q`
has the unique degree-preserving map

```text
a^qV_q tensor a^rV_r
 -> a^(2q-h)V_h tensor a^(2t)1,
t=(r-q+h)/2.                                         (P23.11v)
```

Fusion admissibility makes `t` an integer in `[0,r]`; these are exactly all
pairwise maps into the retained `H_2` carriers.

**Lemma 23A7 (first-descent carrier injection).**  Fix an indexed active
support, order its plus labels `r_1,...,r_n`, and choose a fusion-path basis

```text
q=h_0 -> h_1 -> ... -> h_n=0.
```

Let `t` be the first index with `h_t<q`, and put

```text
alpha_i=(r_i+h_i-h_(i-1))/2,             1<=i<=t.     (P23.11w)
```

Project the consumed prefix to `V_(h_t)`, place it in the carrier
`a^(2q-h_t)V_(h_t)`, send each prefix plus factor to scalar grade
`alpha_i`, and leave the active suffix and its fusion path unchanged.  This
is a degree-preserving injection on every fixed-support odd path space.

**Proof.**  Fusion admissibility gives
`0<=alpha_i<=r_i`.  Telescoping gives

```text
sum_(i<=t)alpha_i
 =(sum_(i<=t)r_i+h_t-q)/2,
```

so the output degree is

```text
(2q-h_t)+2sum_(i<=t)alpha_i
 =q+sum_(i<=t)r_i,
```

equal to the consumed input degree.  The carrier type and surviving suffix
identify the first descent.  The prefix path is recovered recursively from
`h_i=h_(i-1)+2alpha_i-r_i`, and the retained suffix path recovers the rest.
Every invariant path has a first descent because `h_n=0<q`.  QED.

Lemma 23A7 concerns only the map from the essential `H_1(0)` block to
carrier outputs.  It does not assert injectivity of a differential on the
full odd space: by Lemma 23A6B, the paired `H_1(j+1)` columns must also be
redistributed before their `H_2(j)` rows provide net capacity.

First descent does not by itself retain enough information across different
supports, even if its factor order is allowed to depend on the source.

**Lemma 23A8A (Johnson-graph carrier collision).**  Fix `q>=2` and take
`n>=2q` indexed plus-one factors.  For every `q`-subset `A` of their
positions, use the odd class `a^qV_q`, make exactly the positions in `A`
active, and put every inactive position in scalar grade zero.  No choice of
source-dependent orders makes the first-descent maps of Lemma 23A7
injective on this family.

**Proof.**  Each source has the unique invariant path

```text
q -> q-1 -> ... -> 1 -> 0.
```

The first active factor is therefore consumed at scalar index

```text
(1+(q-1)-q)/2=0,
```

and produces the fixed carrier `a^(q+1)V_(q-1)`.  The output retains only
the other `q-1` active positions and their unique descending suffix path;
all remaining positions have scalar index zero.  Thus a source `A` can
reach only the targets indexed by its `(q-1)`-subsets.  For the full left
family the neighborhood has size `binom(n,q-1)`, whereas

```text
binom(n,q)/binom(n,q-1)=(n-q+1)/q>1
```

when `n>=2q`.  Hall's inequality fails.  The smallest case is `q=2,n=4`,
with six sources and four carrier targets.  QED.

This is an obstruction only to carrier-only support encoding.  The same
family has a collision-free pure evaluation: put scalar index one on every
active plus position and index zero on the minus and inactive positions.
The scalar-index sum is `q`, exactly half the active label sum, and the
positions carrying one recover the source support.  Any uniform
construction must therefore choose between scalar markers and retained
carriers rather than expect either family alone to be injective.

For the reduced essential-source map, Lemma 23A7 removes every
within-support path Hall inequality.  Its remaining graph is purely
cross-support: collisions occur only when a factor consumed to scalar grade
`alpha_i` in one support is inactive with the same scalar grade in another.
This is a useful reduced graph, not the graph of the full differential;
Lemma 23A6B adds the independent Schur-complement obligation for the paired
odd columns.

The first fixed-order collision is already visible at three indexed
plus-one factors.  Take `q=2`, scalar-index grade two, and the two sources

```text
A_02: support {0,2}, path 2 -> 1 -> 0, t_1=0,
A_12: support {1,2}, path 2 -> 1 -> 0, t_0=0.        (P23.11x)
```

In the fixed indexed order, both first descents consume the earlier active
factor with scalar grade zero and retain factor two.  Their common target is

```text
a^3 V_1 tensor (a^0 1)_0 tensor (a^0 1)_1
          tensor (a^1 V_1)_2,                         (P23.11y)
```

with the two `V_1` factors coupled to `V_0`.  Thus the two-source
neighborhood has size one.  Starting each support cyclically at factor two
adds a different surviving-factor target to each source and repairs this
particular deficit.

Allowing every ordering does not give a universal repair.  Define the
permutation-saturated `H_2` prefix graph by allowing, for every active
support, every permutation of its indexed factors and every stopping prefix
whose current height is `h<q`; send that prefix to the carrier
`a^(2q-h)V_h`, with scalar grades given by `(P23.11w)`, and retain the
suffix.  Identifying suffix bases after arbitrary recoupling only enlarges
this graph.

**Proposition 23A8B (full `H_2` prefix-carrier Hall obstruction).**  For
`q=2` and four indexed plus-one factors at scalar-index grade two, the
permutation-saturated graph above has Hall deficit one.

**Proof.**  For each pair `0<=i<j<=3`, let `A_ij` have active support
`{i,j}`, put every inactive factor in scalar grade zero, and take the unique
path

```text
2 -> 1 -> 0.
```

There are six such sources.  If the map stops after one active factor, its
carrier is `a^3V_1`, the consumed scalar grade is zero, and its target is
determined only by the surviving index.  This gives four targets `R_j`,
one for each possible survivor.  If it stops after both active factors,
the carrier is `a^4V_0`, both scalar grades are zero, and every pair has the
same target `R_empty`.  These exhaust all permutations and all `H_2`
stopping prefixes because every support has two elements and its fusion
path is unique.  Hence

```text
|X|=binom(4,2)=6,       |N(X)|=4+1=5,       deficit=1. (P23.11z)
```

For the first-descent-only rule `R_empty` is absent, so the deficit is two.
Cyclic order and all permutations coincide on a two-element support.  QED.

Therefore the complete factorwise `H_2` prefix-carrier hierarchy, even
after permutation and recoupling saturation, cannot furnish the universal
cross-support injection.  This does not rule out a differential with
additional even carriers or genuinely non-prefix multi-factor operations.
The strict threaded C++ search
`character_ring_iter/search_su2_fdc_h2_recoupling_hall.cpp` verifies the
three-factor repair, recomputes `(P23.11z)`, and searches ordered label
words in the declared finite range.  Its replay is recorded in
`certificates/su2_fdc_h2_recoupling_hall.log`; the finite search is
corroboration, not the proof of Proposition 23A8B.

The missing rank in the smallest obstruction is supplied by exactly one
scalar marker.

**Proposition 23A8C (minimal reduced-graph augmentation).**  In the
`q=2,n=4` family of Proposition 23A8B, the reduced graph from the six
essential sources to otherwise-unused prefix-carrier targets has matching
rank five.  Adjoining the pure scalar evaluation for any one source raises
this reduced matching rank to six; hence one scalar target is necessary and
sufficient for this reduced graph.

**Proof.**  The five carrier targets in `(P23.11z)` give the upper bound.
They have matching rank five, for example

```text
A_01 -> R_0,   A_12 -> R_1,   A_23 -> R_2,
A_03 -> R_3,   A_02 -> R_empty.
```

Now send `A_01` instead to the all-scalar allocation having index one at
positions zero and one and index zero at the minus and the other two plus
positions.  Its index sum is two, exactly half the active label sum.  The
remaining five sources have the carrier matching

```text
A_02 -> R_0,   A_03 -> R_3,   A_12 -> R_2,
A_13 -> R_1,   A_23 -> R_empty.                       (P23.11z1)
```

All six targets are distinct.  Proposition 23A8B shows that no repair with
zero scalar targets is possible.  Permuting the four positions proves the
same statement for any chosen source.  QED.

This is not a chain-level repair.  Five carrier rows used in
`(P23.11z1)` displace five paired odd columns.  After the common
`H_1/H_2` block is cancelled, Lemma 23A6B requires the entire six-dimensional
boundary source, not only one chosen column, to be paid in the scalar
Schur complement.

There is also an exact representation-theoretic reduction of the one-minus
injection.  Work first in ordinary `SU(2)_x` by `SU(2)_y`.  Let

```text
S=Sym^(q-1)(V_(1,x) direct-sum V_(1,y)),
K_s=Hom_(SU(2)_y)(V_(s,y),K),
```

where `K` is any finite-dimensional module for the product group; each
`K_s` is regarded as an `SU(2)_x` module.

**Lemma 23A9 (one-minus boundary reduction).**  Put

```text
A=Hom_(SU(2)_y)(1,S tensor K),
B=Hom_(SU(2)_y)(V_(1,y),S tensor K).
```

Then

```text
V_(1,x) tensor A-B=V_(q,x) tensor K_0-K_q.            (P23.11z2)
```

Consequently an `SU(2)_x`-module injection

```text
B -> V_(1,x) tensor A
```

exists if and only if an injection

```text
K_q -> V_(q,x) tensor K_0                            (P23.11z3)
```

exists.  The same statements hold in `SU(2)_k` for `q<=k`, with tensor
products interpreted as fusion products and `S` interpreted as the
semisimple object

```text
direct-sum_(a+b=q-1) V_(a,x) tensor V_(b,y).
```

**Proof.**  The ordinary multiplicity-free decomposition

```text
S=direct-sum_(a+b=q-1) V_(a,x) tensor V_(b,y)
```

and Clebsch--Gordan give

```text
A=direct-sum_(s=0)^(q-1) V_(q-1-s,x) tensor K_s,

B=[direct-sum_(s=1)^q V_(q-s,x) tensor K_s]
  direct-sum
  [direct-sum_(s=0)^(q-2) V_(q-2-s,x) tensor K_s].
```

Fusion of the first line by `V_(1,x)` reproduces both displayed sums for
`B`.  The sole unmatched target is `V_(q,x) tensor K_0`, and the sole
unmatched source is `K_q`, proving `(P23.11z2)`.  Finite-dimensional
`SU(2)` modules are semisimple, so an injection exists exactly when every
irreducible target multiplicity dominates the corresponding source
multiplicity.  Cancelling the common character proves equivalence with
`(P23.11z3)`.

For `SU(2)_k`, every first-coordinate label in the displayed object `S` is
at most `q-1<=k-1`.  Therefore fusion by `V_1` has the same adjacent
branches, including the allowed top branch `V_k` when `q=k`; no omitted
summand crosses the affine wall.  The fusion category is semisimple, so the
same decomposition and multiplicity argument applies.  QED.

For the one-minus factor in `(P23.10)`, take

```text
K=product_i(V_(p_i,x) direct-sum V_(p_i,y)).
```

Thus all interior Clebsch--Gordan branches of the symmetric-power factor
cancel; the cross-support problem is exactly the boundary injection
`(P23.11z3)`.  The paired `H_1/H_2` terms are chain-level carriers for the
interior branches, while `K_q` is the support-marker boundary that remains
after their cancellation.  Proposition 23A8C describes only the optimistic
reduced carrier graph; `(P23.11z3)` and Lemma 23A6B show why its one-scalar
augmentation is insufficient for a full differential.

For a product of indexed plus factors, the boundary map has an exact
support-block description.  Put

```text
X_U=tensor_(i in U)V_(p_i,x),
M_s(U)=Hom_(SU(2)_y)(V_(s,y),tensor_(i in U)V_(p_i,y)).
```

The spaces `M_s(U)` carry no `SU(2)_x` action.

**Lemma 23A9A (boundary support blocks).**  For

```text
K=tensor_i(V_(p_i,x) direct-sum V_(p_i,y)),
```

one has

```text
K_s=direct-sum_(U subset [n]) M_s(U) tensor X_(U^c).  (P23.11z3a)
```

The block of a boundary map `(P23.11z3)` from source support `U` to
invariant target support `W` belongs exactly to

```text
Hom(M_q(U),M_0(W))
 tensor Hom_(SU(2)_x)(X_(U^c),V_q tensor X_(W^c)).    (P23.11z3b)
```

Thus a pure support transfer is the case `W=empty`: a path
`lambda:V_q -> X_U` and coevaluation give

```text
X_(U^c) -> V_q tensor X_U tensor X_(U^c).
```

A support-preserving channel swap is the case `W=U`; it requires both an
invariant path in `X_U` and a map
`X_(U^c) -> V_q tensor X_(U^c)`.

**Proof.**  Expanding the indexed direct-sum tensor product by the set of
factors assigned to the `y` coordinate gives `(P23.11z3a)`.  Taking
`SU(2)_x`-equivariant Hom between its `U` source summand and the `W` summand
of `V_q tensor K_0` gives `(P23.11z3b)`, because both multiplicity spaces
have trivial `SU(2)_x` action.  For `W=empty`, insert the coevaluation
`1 -> V_q tensor V_q`, apply `lambda` to the second copy, and tensor by the
identity of `X_(U^c)`.  The case `W=U` is the displayed specialization of
`(P23.11z3b)`.  QED.

The lemma characterizes all pure and support-preserving blocks, but
different source blocks may still have intersecting images.  Full
injectivity is the rank problem for their combined matrix, not ordinary
Hall on the list of nonzero Hom-spaces.

The smallest collision does admit a full boundary injection, but it uses
both a support-preserving channel swap and a pure support transfer.

**Proposition 23A9B (four-fundamental hybrid boundary injection).**  Let
`q=2` and

```text
K=(V_(1,x) direct-sum V_(1,y))^(tensor 4).
```

There is an explicit injection

```text
K_2 -> V_(2,x) tensor K_0.                            (P23.11z4)
```

It is valid in ordinary `SU(2)` and in every `SU(2)_k` with `k>=2`.

**Proof.**  Decompose by the indexed set `S` of factors assigned to the
`y` coordinate.  A `V_(2,y)` source occurs only for `|S|=2` or `|S|=4`.
For `|S|=2`, both the `V_2` path and the invariant path in
`V_1 tensor V_1` are unique.  The source over `S` is

```text
V_(1,x) tensor V_(1,x)=V_(0,x) direct-sum V_(2,x).
```

Use the `K_0` summand having the same `y`-support `S`.  Send its source
`V_0` branch to the unique `V_0` inside
`V_(2,x) tensor V_(2,x)`, and send its source `V_2` branch to
`V_(2,x) tensor V_(0,x)`.  These two maps are injective, and the six
indexed supports land in six different direct summands of `K_0`.

For `|S|=4`, the source multiplicity space is

```text
Hom(V_2,V_1^(tensor 4)).
```

Identify it, by exchanging the two copies of `SU(2)`, with the `V_2`
multiplicity space in the empty-`y`-support summand
`V_(1,x)^(tensor 4)` of `K_0`.  On every path copy use the unique invariant
map `V_2 tensor V_2 -> V_0`.  This image lies in the empty-support summand,
so it is disjoint from all six size-two images.  Their direct sum proves
`(P23.11z4)`.

The construction uses only the fusion rules

```text
V_1 star_k V_1=V_0 direct-sum V_2,
V_2 star_k V_2 contains V_0,
```

and exchange identifies the two fourfold path spaces at every `k>=2`.
At the truncation edge `k=2` one has

```text
V_1^(star_2 4)=2V_0 direct-sum 2V_2,
```

rather than the ordinary decomposition
`2V_0 direct-sum 3V_2 direct-sum V_4`; nevertheless the `V_2` source
path space and its exchanged empty-support target path space both have
dimension two.  Hence truncation changes their common multiplicity but
not the injection, and the same proof works in `SU(2)_k`.  QED.

In ordinary `SU(2)` the complete multiplicity audit is

```text
K_2=9V_0 direct-sum 6V_2,
K_0=10V_0 direct-sum 9V_2 direct-sum V_4,

V_2 tensor K_0
 =9V_0 direct-sum 20V_2 direct-sum 10V_4 direct-sum V_6. (P23.11z5)
```

Thus the `V_0` target capacity is exactly saturated.  Only three of its
nine copies come from the empty-support summand; the six nonempty
size-two supports are indispensable.  This is the representation-level
counterpart of the Schur-complement warning: a pure empty-support transfer
does not suffice, while the hybrid support-preserving swaps do.

There is a canonical-looking crystal realization of `(P23.11z3)`, but it
is not injective.  In the type-`A_1` highest-word model, fix an indexed
colour assignment and a highest path of the `y`-factors from zero to `q`.
Keep the factors through the last return of this path to zero in the
`y`-colour.  Reverse the terminal excursion, place it after an external
`B(q)`, and recolour that whole excursion `x`; it is then a weight-zero
component.  Finally use the unique two-factor `A_1` crystal commutors to
restore the original indexed factor order.  The retained `y` prefix is
invariant, so this rule does land in the crystal of `V_(q,x) tensor K_0`.

**Lemma 23A9C (last-return crystal-map obstruction).**  The preceding
last-return/commutor map is not injective, ordinarily or in `SU(2)_k` for
`k>=2`.  Its first collision has

```text
(p_1,p_2)=(1,1),                   q=1.              (P23.11z5a)
```

**Proof.**  Consider the two distinct indexed source highest words

```text
y_1=+, x_2=+,                 x_1=+, y_2=+.
```

Neither one has a nonempty invariant `y` prefix.  Reversing its singleton
terminal excursion and adjoining the external factor gives respectively

```text
+_q -_1 +_2,                 +_q -_2 +_1.
```

The first word is already in indexed order.  To order the second, commute
`-_2 tensor +_1`.  This word is the middle element of the `B(2)` component
of `B(1) tensor B(1)`, so the unique crystal commutor sends it to
`-_1 tensor +_2`.  Both indexed sources therefore have the same target

```text
+_q -_1 +_2.
```

The calculation uses only the components
`B(1) tensor B(1)=B(2) disjoint-union B(0)`, which are unchanged by level
`k>=2`.  QED.

This does not obstruct the boundary injection itself.  In this example
`V_1 tensor K_0` has more than enough copies of `V_1`; the failure is that
canonical switching forgets which equal indexed factor supplied the
terminal excursion.  A successful crystal map must retain that index by a
separate routing or make a noncanonical capacity allocation.

The minimal indexed repair works for `(P23.11z5a)`: keep the empty
`y`-support but use the terminal-excursion index as a tag, assigning the two
sources to the two weight-one components

```text
+_q+_1-_2,                    +_q-_1+_2
```

of `B(1) tensor B(1) tensor B(1)`.  Thus the boundary injection still
exists and the first collision is removed without changing the target
support.

That same-support Hall repair fails at the next arity.  For three
fundamental factors, `q=1`, retained `y`-support empty, and free
`x`-weight zero, there are four source components:

```text
three choices of one y-factor, with the other two x-factors invariant,
one all-y path + + - having no return to zero.         (P23.11z5b)
```

The corresponding target bin is the invariant part of four fundamental
`x`-factors, including the external one.  It has only the two ballot words

```text
+ + - -,                         + - + -.
```

Hence the tagged demand is four and the fixed-support capacity is two.
The other all-`y` path `+ - +` is not in this bin: its last zero retains
the first two indices.  Repairing `(P23.11z5b)` therefore requires spilling
capacity into nonempty invariant `y`-supports, rather than merely tagging
different `x` fusion components over the canonical last-return support.
Such a global spill does repair this example exactly.  There are five
weight-zero sources in total.  The target has the two empty-`y`-support
slots displayed above and one slot for each of the three indexed
two-factor invariant `y`-supports, also five in total.  The equality of
these global counts is an allocation, not a canonical crystal switching
rule; it is the first instance where the full indexed Hall pool is forced.

The strict C++ diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/analyze_su2_crystal_last_return.cpp` implements the
highest-path reversal and the unique two-factor commutor, and reproduces
`(P23.11z5a)`.  Its replay is
`certificates/su2_crystal_last_return.log`.  The displayed two-word
calculation is the obstruction; the program only checks the convention and
minimal search order.  The companion diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/analyze_su2_crystal_tagged_hall.cpp` groups source and
target highest paths by retained indexed support and endpoint weight; it
reproduces the exact fixed-support overload `4>2` and global repair
`5=5` in `(P23.11z5b)`.  Its replay is
`certificates/su2_crystal_tagged_hall.log`.

The global supplier has a precise support count.  For an indexed subset
`U`, write

```text
m_U(r)=dim Hom(V_r,X_U).
```

Fix an `x`-type `V_a`.  The source block with `y`-support `U` supplies

```text
d_U(a;q)=m_U(q)m_(U^c)(a)                            (P23.11z5c)
```

copies of `V_a`.  An invariant target support `W` supplies

```text
c_W(a;q)
 =m_W(0) sum_(t in a star_k q)m_(W^c)(t).             (P23.11z5d)
```

Indeed, the two factors in `(P23.11z5c)` select a `V_q` path in the
`y`-tensor product and a `V_a` path in the complementary `x` product.
For `(P23.11z5d)`, select an invariant `y` path and then a `V_a` path in
`V_q tensor X_(W^c)`.  Thus the boundary injection `(P23.11z3)` is, for
each `a`, exactly an indexed allocation of

```text
sum_U d_U(a;q)
```

source slots into the `sum_W c_W(a;q)` target slots.  Formula
`(P23.11z3b)` permits a scalar map between any selected source and target
copy of the same `V_a`; the hard assertion is that the global target count
always suffices.

A natural compression of this Hall pool is false.  Call an invariant
support `W` primitive if `W` is empty, or if `m_W(0)>0` but no proper
nonempty subset of `W` has an invariant.  One might hope to replace every
composite invariant target by its primitive invariant sub-supports and
prove

```text
sum_U d_U(a;q)
 <=sum_(W primitive) c_W(a;q).                        (P23.11z5e)
```

**Lemma 23A9D (primitive-supplier compression obstruction).**  Inequality
`(P23.11z5e)` fails ordinarily and in every `SU(2)_k`, `k>=2`.  Its first
ordinary obstruction is

```text
(p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4)=(1,1,1,2),       q=1,       a=0.
                                                               (P23.11z5f)
```

**Proof.**  The invariant supports are the empty set, the three indexed
pairs of label-one factors, and the three triples formed by such a pair
together with the label-two factor.  The first four are primitive.  Their
capacities are

```text
empty support:                         3,
three primitive label-one pairs:       3,
three composite (1,1,2) triples:       3.
```

The empty-support value follows from

```text
V_1^3 tensor V_2=3V_1 direct-sum 3V_3 direct-sum V_5.
```

Every other displayed support has invariant multiplicity one, and its
complement has one `V_1` path.  Complementing the seven invariant supports
also lists all source contributions in `(P23.11z5c)`.  Consequently

```text
sum_U d_U(0;1)=9,       primitive capacity=6,
full capacity=9.
```

At level two, `V_1^(star 3) star V_2=2V_1`; hence the corresponding three
numbers are `8,5,8`.  For every level at least three, the ordinary
`V_1` multiplicities used above are unchanged, so they remain `9,6,9`.
Thus the full `V_0` target is exactly saturated at every level, while
deleting the three composite suppliers creates a strict deficit.  QED.

Each composite triple in `(P23.11z5f)` contains a primitive invariant
label-one pair, but it is still an independent target summand: placing the
label-two index in the `y` support frees a different complementary
`x`-tensor product.  Hence no recursive compression to minimal invariant
sub-supports can prove `(P23.11z3)`.  A viable Hall argument must retain
composite invariant supports with their full indexed multiplicities.

The strict C++ diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/analyze_su2_boundary_primitive_suppliers.cpp`
constructs `(P23.11z5c)--(P23.11z5e)` from exact ordinary fusion paths and

`certificates/su2_boundary_primitive_suppliers.log`.  Minimality is
diagnostic; the displayed decomposition is the exact obstruction.

The three-fundamental overload `(P23.11z5b)` also rules out every
support-monotone switching, not only the canonical last-return rule.  Give
the source block over `U` access to every invariant target support

```text
W subset U.                                             (P23.11z5g)
```

This includes every rule which recolours old `y` factors to `x` and retains
an arbitrary invariant part of the old `y` support.

**Lemma 23A9E (support-monotone Hall obstruction).**  For three fundamental
factors, `q=1`, and `a=0`, the graph `(P23.11z5g)` has Hall deficit one
ordinarily and in every `SU(2)_k` with `k>=2`.  At level one its deficit is
two.

**Proof.**  Take the three singleton source supports.  Each has demand one:
its `y` factor is `V_1`, while its two `x` factors contain one invariant.
The only invariant subset of a singleton is the empty set.  Its scalar
target capacity is

```text
[V_0](V_1 tensor V_1^(tensor 3))=m_(1,1,1)(1)=2.
```

Thus demand three has neighborhood capacity two.  At level one the same
capacity is one.  QED.

The forced bidirectional spill can be realized without collisions in this
minimal case.

**Proposition 23A9F (three-fundamental bidirectional repair).**  The full
boundary injection for three fundamental factors and `q=1` exists
ordinarily and in every `SU(2)_k`.

**Proof.**  Index the factors cyclically by `0,1,2`.  Over a singleton
source `U={i}`, the source `x`-module is

```text
V_1 tensor V_1=V_0 direct-sum V_2,
```

with `V_2` omitted at level one.  Route it to
`W_i={i,i+1 mod 3}`.  The two `y` factors in `W_i` have their unique
invariant, while `V_1 tensor X_(W_i^c)=V_1 tensor V_1` has the same
displayed summands.  The three supports `W_i` are distinct.  Finally send
the all-`y` source path basis to the scalar copies in the empty-support
target.  Reciprocity identifies both multiplicities with
`m_(1,1,1)(1)`, and the empty support is disjoint from the preceding three
targets.  These are all source supports.  QED.

Here a singleton imports one old `x` index.  Even the enlargement which
allows arbitrary deletions and at most one such import,

```text
U -> W   if and only if   |W minus U|<=1,              (P23.11z5h)
```

does not close uniformly at the affine wall.

**Lemma 23A9G (one-import affine Hall obstruction).**  For every `k>=5`,
work in `SU(2)_k` and take

```text
(p_0,...,p_4)=(1,1,2,k-2,k),       q=a=k-1.           (P23.11z5i)
```

The one-import graph `(P23.11z5h)` has Hall deficit one, although the
unrestricted boundary coefficient is positive.

**Proof.**  Let `i` range over `0,1`.  The following source family has
total demand twelve:

```text
source support U             number of U     d_U(a;q) each
{i,3}                              2               1
{i,2,3}                            2               2
{i,4}                              2               2
{i,2,4}                            2               1.             (P23.11z5j)
```

The simple-current identity `V_k star_k V_r=V_(k-r)` and the ordinary
`A_1` fusion intervals give its complete positive neighborhood:

```text
target support W              empty   {0,1}   {0,1,2}   {2,3,4}
c_W(a;q)                         6        2         1          2.  (P23.11z5k)
```

Indeed,
`V_(k-1) star_k V_(k-1)=V_0 direct-sum V_2`, so here

```text
c_W(a;q)=m_W(0)(m_(W^c)(0)+m_(W^c)(2)).
```

This gives the four entries in `(P23.11z5k)` directly.  Checking the
invariant subsets which differ from a support in `(P23.11z5j)` by at most
one imported index shows that no other target has positive capacity.
Therefore the neighborhood capacity is `6+2+1+2=11<12`.

The unrestricted total source and target capacities are respectively
`12` and `14`; hence this coefficient of the boundary character is two.
Only the local support-routing rule fails.  QED.

The failure leaves a sharp next support-displacement candidate: allow two,
rather than one, imported indices.  This does not make a canonical crystal
map injective; it gives a materially smaller global Hall candidate whose
edges are exactly the two-colour changes of one Plucker switch.

**Target 23A9G2 (two-import boundary Hall allocation).**  In the notation
of `(P23.11z5c)--(P23.11z5d)`, fix `a,q`.  Join a source support `U` to an
invariant target support `W` precisely when

```text
|W minus U|<=2.                                      (P23.11z5h2)
```

Give `U` demand `d_U(a;q)` and `W` capacity `c_W(a;q)`.  Prove that this
capacitated bipartite graph has a matching of total value

```text
sum_U d_U(a;q)                                       (P23.11z5h3)
```

whenever the unrestricted boundary coefficient is nonnegative.  The claim
is to hold ordinarily and in every `SU(2)_k`.

If true, it gives a scalar-grade injection

```text
K_q -> V_(q,x) tensor K_0
```

without requiring a support-monotone rule.  It is still only a one-minus
boundary lemma: further coloured Plucker capacity is required for the full
multi-minus `(PCP_k)` theorem.

The condition is sharp with respect to the known obstruction.  The strict

returns `FAIL` at one import for the family `(P23.11z5i)`, while its

labels=[1,1,2,k-2,k].                              (P23.11z5h4)

There is also a genuinely unbounded outer chamber in which the complete
Hall allocation collapses to one support.  Assume all plus labels are
nontrivial, and put

```text
P=sum_i p_i,                         p_min=min_i p_i.
```

**Proposition 23A9H (single-source outer Hall chamber).**  If

```text
q>P-p_min,                                             (P23.11z5l)
```

then the boundary injection

```text
K_q -> V_(q,x) tensor K_0
```

exists ordinarily and in every `SU(2)_k` for which the displayed labels
exist.  In particular,

```text
q=P-2d,                         p_min>2d               (P23.11z5m)
```

allows arbitrary arity and arbitrary mixed labels.

**Proof.**  Every proper indexed support `U` has total label at most
`P-p_min<q`.  Its tensor product cannot contain `V_q`.  Finite fusion can
likewise not create such a label: every binary output satisfies
`c<=a+b`, so induction bounds every endpoint by the support's total label.
Thus the sole possibly nonzero source block in `(P23.11z3a)` is

```text
M_q([n]) tensor X_empty=M_q([n]) tensor V_0.
```

Use the empty-`y` target support.  By self-duality and rigidity, its `V_0`
multiplicity inside `V_q tensor X_[n]` is

```text
dim Hom(V_0,V_q tensor X_[n])
 =dim Hom(V_q,X_[n])
 =dim M_q([n]).
```

Choose dual path bases and map the source isomorphically onto this invariant
isotypic block.  Frobenius reciprocity is unchanged in the semisimple
fusion category `SU(2)_k`, so the finite statement requires no stability
or distance-from-wall condition.  Formula `(P23.11z5m)` is precisely
`(P23.11z5l)` with the fusion parity made explicit.  QED.

This chamber ends exactly when a proper support can carry `V_q`.
Coevaluation still embeds each such source block separately into the
empty-support target, but the images of different indexed blocks may
intersect.  Controlling those collisions is the unresolved unrestricted
Hall problem.

The first outer defect nevertheless has a complete two-import allocation.
It is the smallest chamber in which the single-source argument has genuinely
ended, so it gives a concrete unbounded extension of Proposition 23A9H.

**Proposition 23A9H0A (finite defect-one outer two-import collar).**  Let all
indexed labels `p_i` be positive, put `P=sum_i p_i`, and assume

```text
q=P-2>=1.                                             (P23.11z5m0aa)
```

Then the two-import graph of Target 23A9G2 has a full capacitated matching
ordinarily.  The same is true in every `SU(2)_k` whenever `q<=k`.
Equivalently, there is an injection

```text
K_q -> V_(q,x) tensor K_0.                            (P23.11z5m0ab)
```

**Proof.**  Let `U` be a source support and write `R=[n] minus U`.  If
`M_q(U)!=0`, the highest-weight bound gives

```text
sum_(i in R)p_i<=P-q=2.
```

Fusion parity makes this omitted total even.  Since every label is positive,
the only possibilities are

```text
R=empty,             R={i} with p_i=2,
R={i,j} with p_i=p_j=1.                              (P23.11z5m0ac)
```

For `R=empty`, the source is in the `a=0` block and has demand
`m_[n](q)`.  Send it to the empty target support, whose `a=0` capacity is
exactly `m_[n](q)` by rigidity.

For an indexed pair `R={i,j}` of label-one factors, the complementary
product has the unique top path to `V_q`.  Its source has one copy in each
of the `a=0` and `a=2` blocks.  Send both copies to the target support
`W=R`.  This is a two-import edge.  Since

```text
m_R(0)=1,                  m_(R^c)(q)=1,
q in 0 star q,             q in 2 star q,
```

the target has at least one slot in each corresponding `a` block.  The
supports `R` are indexed and distinct, so these images are disjoint.

It remains to route the sources with `R={i}` and `p_i=2`.  Each has one
copy in the `a=2` block.  Use the empty target support.  Its capacity is

```text
sum_(t in 2 star q)m_[n](t)
 >=m_[n](q)+m_[n](q+2)=(n-1)+1=n.                    (P23.11z5m0ad)
```

Here `m_[n](P)=1`, while `m_[n](P-2)=n-1`: in the top-weight expansion of
`product_i V_(p_i)`, the weights `P` and `P-2` have multiplicities `1` and
`n`, respectively.  There are at most `n` indexed label-two sources, so
this capacity suffices.  All maps used are permitted blocks of
`(P23.11z3b)`, and the target supports or the `a`-isotypic blocks separate
the stated images.  Thus their direct sum is injective.

For the finite statement, `q<=k` leaves only `P<=k`, `P=k+1`, and
`P=k+2`.  The first is the wall-free argument above.  Suppose first that
`P=k+1`, so `q=k-1`.  The pair routes remain valid because
`q in 2 star_k q`.  The empty `a=2` capacity for the singleton-label-two
sources is

```text
m_[n](k-3)+m_[n](k-1)
 =binom(n,2)+r-1>=c_2.                              (P23.11z5m0ae)
```

Here `r` is the number of labels at least two and `c_2` the number equal to
two.  Indeed the two displayed multiplicities agree with their ordinary
top-weight values: they are respectively
`binom(n,2)+r-n` and `n-1`; no reflected label can occur below total label
`P=k+1`.  Since `n>=2`, `(P23.11z5m0ae)` follows from `r>=c_2`.

It remains that `P=k+2`, so `q=k`.  At the top wall,

```text
2 star_k k={k-2},                                    (P23.11z5m0af)
```

and the `a=2` pair-of-ones sources can no longer use their own target
support.  If `n>=4`, route every such pair source to its own support in the
`a=0` block as before, but route its `a=2` copy there only through the
`k-2` channel: the complementary top product has
`m_(R^c)(k-2)=n-3>=1`.  Route all singleton-label-two sources to the empty
`a=2` target.  Its capacity is

```text
m_[n](k-2)=binom(n,2)+r-n>=c_2,                      (P23.11z5m0ag)
```

again by the ordinary top-weight count (the first reflected label is
`k+4>P`).

For `n=3`, the same empty capacity is `r`.  It pays all `a=2` sources
unless `(k;p_1,p_2,p_3)=(2;1,1,2)`.  In that exceptional word, send the
source omitting the label two to the all-three-factor invariant target and
send the pair-of-ones source to the empty target; both target blocks have
capacity one.  For `n=2`, only `[2,k]` (with `k>2`) can have a label-two
source, and the empty target has its unique `k-2` slot.  The remaining
case `[2,2]` at level two is resolved by sending one singleton source to
the empty target and the other to the all-factor invariant target.  Finally
at level one all labels are one, so only the `a=0` pair routes occur.
Every target used differs from its source by at most two imported indices.
This completes the finite allocation.  QED.

The next outer defect also closes on a nontrivial arbitrary-label subcone.
The restriction below removes the first competing pair supports, so its
proof isolates exactly the new collision caused by fundamental labels.

**Proposition 23A9H0B (defect-two collar without fundamental labels).**
Work ordinarily, or in `SU(2)_k` with `P<=k`.  Suppose

```text
p_i>=2,                 q=P-4>=4.                    (P23.11z5m0ah)
```

Then the two-import graph of Target 23A9G2 has a full capacitated matching,
and hence the boundary injection `(P23.11z5m0ab)` exists.

**Proof.**  As in Proposition 23A9H0A, if `M_q(U)!=0` and
`R=[n] minus U`, then the omitted label total is even and at most four.
Under `(P23.11z5m0ah)` the only possibilities are

```text
R=empty,             R={i} with p_i=2,
R={i} with p_i=4,    R={i,j} with p_i=p_j=2.           (P23.11z5m0ai)
```

The empty complement is routed to the empty `a=0` target exactly as before.
For an omitted pair of label-two factors, use that pair itself as target.
It is an invariant two-import support, and its complementary product has
the unique top `V_q` path.  Since `q>=4`, the channel `q` occurs in each of

```text
0 star q,            2 star q,            4 star q,
```

so its three source blocks `a=0,2,4`, each of dimension one, fit in the
