`M_0(W_j)` contains the scalar channel in `V_a tensor V_a`, and the simple
case of Lemma 23A9H2 sends the complete `C_j` source block to the `W_j`
target.  Pairwise disjointness and `r>=3` make the indexed unions `W_j`
distinct.  The direct sum of these maps is the required injection.  QED.

**Corollary 23A9H4 (simple-current co-doubleton family).**  In `SU(2)_k`,

```text
V_k tensor V_b=V_(k-b).                               (P23.11z5m16)
```

Hence any pairwise disjoint family of active two-index complements, each
consisting of one label `k` and one fixed label `b`, satisfies Corollary
23A9H3.  For three or more such complements, its complete source family is
paid by distinct four-index invariant supports, without using an empty or
two-index target support.

If `n>=3` and

```text
q>P-p_(1)-p_(2)-p_(3),                               (P23.11z5m17)
```

then these families belong to the first unresolved complement layer after
the full and co-singleton supports: every active source omits at most two
factors.

**Proof.**  The simple-current identity `(P23.11z5m16)` makes the object
on each displayed two-index complement the same self-dual simple
`V_(k-b)`.  Corollary 23A9H3 applies.  When the family has at least three
members, its cyclic targets are unions of two disjoint two-index
complements and therefore have four indices; this proves the target-support
claim.  Finally, a support omitting at least three indices has total label
at most `P-p_(1)-p_(2)-p_(3)<q`, so it cannot carry `V_q`, ordinarily or
after affine truncation.  QED.

Corollary 23A9H4 is a source-family closure, not a closure of every
co-doubleton type under `(P23.11z5m17)`.  Reducible complementary objects
must still satisfy the channel capacities `(P23.11z5m11)` or use additional
target supports.

The Hall cuts for a bounded-import graph admit an exact compression.  For
a set family `D subset 2^[n]`, define its `r`th upper shadow by

```text
D^(+r)={W: there is S in D with S subset W and |W minus S|<=r}.   (P23.11z5n)
```

**Lemma 23A9I (down-set Hall reduction).**  Fix `q,a` and give the support
graph the edge rule

```text
U -> W   if and only if   |W minus U|<=r.              (P23.11z5o)
```

With the exact indexed capacities `(P23.11z5c)--(P23.11z5d)`, this graph
has a full capacitated matching if and only if, for every down-set
`D subset 2^[n]`,

```text
sum_(U in D)d_U(a;q)
 <=sum_(W in D^(+r))c_W(a;q).                         (P23.11z5p)
```

Moreover `D^(+r)` is itself a down-set.  In particular, radius two is
equivalent to the weighted second-shadow inequalities `(P23.11z5p)`;
this is a reduction, not a proof of their positivity.

**Proof.**  Let `X` be an arbitrary family of source supports and put
`D=downarrow X`.  Its neighborhood is exactly `D^(+r)`.  Indeed, if
`U in X` reaches `W`, then `S=U intersection W` belongs to `D` and

```text
|W minus S|=|W minus U|<=r.
```

Conversely, if `S in D`, `S subset W`, and `|W minus S|<=r`, choose
`U in X` with `S subset U`.  Then
`W minus U subset W minus S`, so `U` reaches `W`.

Adding every source support in `D` to `X` leaves this neighborhood
unchanged and can only increase its nonnegative demand.  Hence the
strongest Hall inequality having down-closure `D` is precisely
`(P23.11z5p)`.  Every source family has such a down-closure, while taking
`X=D` proves the converse.  The capacitated Hall theorem now gives the
equivalence.

Finally, if `W in D^(+r)` and `T subset W`, choose a witnessing `S in D`
and put `S'=S intersection T`.  Downward closure gives `S' in D`, while

```text
|T minus S'|<=|W minus S|<=r.
```

Thus `T in D^(+r)`.  QED.

Taking `D=2^[n]` in `(P23.11z5p)` recovers the unrestricted boundary
multiplicity inequality itself.  Therefore the second-shadow formulation
does not evade the one-minus positivity problem; it isolates the additional
local-routing cuts which would have to be controlled after total
positivity.

Rigidity gives the useful invariant-network form

```text
d_U(a;q)=m_(U union {q})(0)m_(U^c union {a})(0),
c_W(a;q)=m_W(0)m_(W^c union {q,a})(0).                (P23.11z5q)
```

Here the braces denote new external indexed leaves, even when their labels
coincide with old ones.  Thus the radius-two inequality asks for a weighted
switching between two invariant spin networks: move the distinguished
`q` leaf from the first component to the component containing `a`, while
importing at most two old leaves into the first component.  Ordinary
polygon feasibility of such a switch would not prove `(P23.11z5p)`;
the required assertion preserves the full products of indexed path
multiplicities in `(P23.11z5q)`.

Literal standard-monomial switching does not preserve the fused blocks in
this formulation.  The obstruction already occurs on one four-vertex
Plucker face.  For ordered vertices `p<u<v<r`, put

```text
C=[uv]_[P][pr]_[N],       A=[pv]_[P][ur]_[N],
B=[pu]_[P][vr]_[N].                                  (P23.11z5r)
```

After forgetting the two colours, the Plucker relation is `C=A-B`.

**Lemma 23A9J (whole-block Plucker-switching obstruction).**  Let the four
vertices in `(P23.11z5r)` be fused blocks `V_delta`, with `delta>=2`.
Expanding them into `delta` fundamental occurrences and applying the
ordinary Plucker/jeu-de-taquin switch cannot be projected to a
multiplication-compatible triangular switch supported only on
whole-block cut tableaux, even when both active old blocks may change
colour.

More precisely, the two switched whole-block cuts on this face are
`A^delta` and `B^delta`, whereas

```text
C^delta
 =sum_(j=0)^delta (-1)^j binom(delta,j)
    A^(delta-j)B^j.                                  (P23.11z5s)
```

Every intermediate term `0<j<delta` splits both blocks `u` and `v`
between the two colours, and none of these terms can be eliminated by
further Plucker straightening inside the span of the two whole-block
cuts.

**Proof.**  In `A`, the block `v` belongs to colour `P` and `u` to colour
`N`; in `B` these assignments are reversed.  Hence
`A^(delta-j)B^j` gives positive degree in both colours at both `u` and
`v` when `0<j<delta`, so it is not a cut of the indexed `V_delta`
blocks.

The intermediate monomials in `(P23.11z5s)` are linearly independent.
Indeed, evaluate the four bracket vectors at

```text
v_p=(1,0),       v_r=(0,s),       v_u=(1,1),
v_v=(1,t).
```

Then

```text
A=st,                 B=s,                 C=s(t-1).
```

Thus a relation
`sum_j gamma_j A^(delta-j)B^j=0` would give
`s^delta sum_j gamma_j t^(delta-j)=0` for all `s,t`, forcing every
`gamma_j` to vanish.  Consequently `(P23.11z5s)` cannot be replaced by a
linear combination of only `A^delta` and `B^delta`.

At `delta=2` the obstruction is the explicit identity

```text
C^2=A^2-2AB+B^2.                                    (P23.11z5t)
```

Switching the first occurrence by `A` and the second by `B`, or vice
versa, produces the same symmetrized term `AB`.  This is the symbolic
collision: the occurrence tag is lost on projection to `V_2`, while the
nonzero middle term is indispensable by the preceding independence.
QED.

Lemma 23A9J rules out only multiplication-compatible whole-block
Plucker/JDT switching.  It does not obstruct the boundary injection
`(P23.11z3)`, nor a switch in a fused Temperley--Lieb/recoupling basis:
such a basis retains the intermediate channels which the cut projection
in `(P23.11z5s)` discards.  In particular, the radius-two Hall evidence
below cannot be promoted to a proof by applying ordinary jeu de taquin to
the fundamental occurrences and forgetting their occurrence tags.

The compressed OpenMP diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/search_su2_boundary_radius2_threaded.cpp` constructs
the exact source and target capacities, represents deletion followed by at
most two imports as a layered subset-lattice flow network, and computes its
full capacitated rank.  Its replay is
`certificates/su2_boundary_radius2_threaded.log`.  The recorded runs use 48
threads selected from the available CPU, RAM, and machine-load budget.
They found no radius-two Hall deficit through the declared randomized
finite-wall ranges, including words of length fifteen at level thirty.
This is diagnostic evidence only; it proves neither `(P23.11z5p)` nor the
boundary injection.

There is an exact fused-leaf recurrence which isolates what a
Temperley--Lieb recoupling induction would still have to control.  Let
`N_p` denote the ordinary fusion matrix, or the fusion matrix of
`SU(2)_k`, and let

```text
F(r,s)=[V_r box-times V_s]
       product_i((V_(p_i) box-times 1) direct-sum
                 (1 box-times V_(p_i))).
```

The table `F` is symmetric.  Define its boundary defect and its oriented
three-terminal transfer defect by

```text
B_F(q,a)=sum_(t in q star_k a)F(0,t)-F(q,a),

C_F(p,q;a)
 =sum_(t in q star_k a)F(p,t)
  -sum_(u in p star_k q)F(u,a).                       (P23.11z5y)
```

Adjoining one indexed plus leaf `p` replaces `F` by

```text
F^[p]=N_p F+F N_p.                                   (P23.11z5z)
```

**Lemma 23A9L (fused-leaf quadrilateral recurrence).**  Uniformly in the
ordinary and finite fusion rings,

```text
B_(F^[p])(q,a)
 =sum_(v in p star_k a)B_F(q,v)+C_F(p,q;a),           (P23.11z5za)

C_F(a,q;p)=-C_F(p,q;a).                              (P23.11z5zb)
```

Consequently the two opposite fused-leaf updates obey the paired identity

```text
B_(F^[p])(q,a)+B_(F^[a])(q,p)
 =2 sum_(v in p star_k a)B_F(q,v).                    (P23.11z5zc)
```

**Proof.**  Formula `(P23.11z5z)` gives

```text
F^[p](0,t)=F(p,t)+sum_v N_(p,t)^v F(0,v),
F^[p](q,a)=sum_u N_(p,q)^u F(u,a)
            +sum_v N_(p,a)^v F(q,v).
```

After summing the first line over `t in q star_k a`, fusion associativity
identifies

```text
sum_(t,v)N_(q,a)^t N_(p,t)^v F(0,v)
 =sum_v N_(p,a)^v sum_w N_(q,v)^w F(0,w).
```

Subtracting the second line gives `(P23.11z5za)`.  If

```text
T_F(p,q,a)=sum_t N_(q,a)^t F(p,t),
```

then `T_F` is symmetric in its last two arguments and

```text
C_F(p,q;a)=T_F(p,q,a)-T_F(a,p,q).
```

This proves `(P23.11z5zb)`; adding the two instances of
`(P23.11z5za)` proves `(P23.11z5zc)`.  QED.

There is an exact global current after summing over the choice of the
appended boundary leaf.  It is the first place in the one-minus problem
where the local antisymmetric remainder cancels without being assigned a
sign.

**Corollary 23A9L1 (leave-one-out boundary current).**  Let
`L=(p_1,...,p_n)` be an indexed plus list with `n>=2`, and write `F_L` for
its two-coordinate table.  For an external label `q`, put

```text
beta_i(L;q)=B_(F_(L minus {i}))(q,p_i).               (P23.11z5zc1)
```

Then, ordinarily and in every finite fusion ring `SU(2)_k`,

```text
(n-1) sum_i beta_i(L;q)
 =2 sum_(i<j) sum_(v in p_i star_k p_j)
       B_(F_(L minus {i,j}))(q,v).                    (P23.11z5zc2)
```

In particular, if every two-leaves-shorter boundary defect on the right is
nonnegative, then the complete leave-one-out current `sum_i beta_i(L;q)`
is nonnegative.

**Proof.**  Apply the paired identity `(P23.11z5zc)` with

```text
F=F_(L minus {i,j}),       p=p_i,       a=p_j.
```

Its left side is exactly

```text
B_(F_(L minus {j}))(q,p_j)+B_(F_(L minus {i}))(q,p_i)
=beta_j(L;q)+beta_i(L;q).
```

Sum this identity over all unordered indexed pairs `{i,j}`.  Each
`beta_i` occurs in exactly `n-1` pairs, which proves
`(P23.11z5zc2)`.  The final assertion is immediate because every finite
`SU(2)` fusion interval is multiplicity-free and all coefficients on the
right are nonnegative under its hypothesis.  QED.

Thus a negative one-minus boundary coefficient is never isolated once all
factor-deleted alternatives are retained: its complete indexed component
has a nonnegative current paid by two-leaves-shorter carriers.  This is a
genuine cumulative payment identity, but it does not yet prove the
individual inequality `beta_i>=0`; its other component vertices correspond
to different choices of the appended boundary leaf.

More sharply, under the same shorter-word hypothesis the paired identity
itself gives

```text
beta_i(L;q)+beta_j(L;q)>=0                 for every i!=j. (P23.11z5zc3)
```

Hence a deficit `beta_i=-d<0` forces every one of the other `n-1` vertices
to carry at least `d`, and therefore

```text
sum_j beta_j(L;q)>=(n-2)d.                            (P23.11z5zc4)
```

This is the quantitative pairwise-payment form of the current.  It makes
the obstruction to an individual proof precise: the available positive
reserve lives on different appended-leaf targets, so an additional
transport which returns that reserve to the original target is still
required.

The all-plus hypothesis in Corollary 23A9L1 is inessential for the current
identity.  What matters is only the exchange symmetry of the table before
the indexed plus leaves are adjoined.  This makes the same conservation law
available in every higher-minus packet after two minus positions have been
distinguished.

**Corollary 23A9L1A (even-background leave-one-out current).**  Let `E` be
an indexed signed background with an even number of minus positions, and
write its two-coordinate coefficient table as

```text
F_E(r,s)=[V_r box-times V_s]
 product_(e in E)(V_e box-times 1+epsilon_e 1 box-times V_e),
epsilon_e in {+1,-1}.                                (P23.11z5zc4a)
```

Let `L=(p_1,...,p_n)` be an indexed list of further plus leaves, with
`n>=2`, and set

```text
F_(E;L)=F_E^[p_1]...[p_n],
beta_i^E(L;q)=B_(F_(E;L minus {i}))(q,p_i).           (P23.11z5zc4b)
```

Then, in the ordinary ring and in every `SU(2)_k`,

```text
(n-1) sum_i beta_i^E(L;q)
 =2 sum_(i<j) sum_(v in p_i star_k p_j)
     B_(F_(E;L minus {i,j}))(q,v).                    (P23.11z5zc4c)
```

Moreover, `2 beta_i^E(L;q)` is the signed contraction obtained from the
background `E` by adjoining `q` and `p_i` as the two further minus leaves
and every leaf of `L minus {i}` as a plus leaf.  Thus `(P23.11z5zc4c)` is
an exact current conservation law inside every fixed even-minus background,
not merely in the two-minus chamber.

**Proof.**  Swapping the two coordinates in `(P23.11z5zc4a)` multiplies
the product by `product_(e in E) epsilon_e=1`.  Hence `F_E` is symmetric.
The plus updates `F -> F^[p]=N_pF+FN_p` commute, so for every pair `i!=j`
we may apply Lemma 23A9L to the symmetric base table

```text
F=F_(E;L minus {i,j}),       p=p_i,       a=p_j.
```

Its paired identity is

```text
beta_i^E(L;q)+beta_j^E(L;q)
 =2 sum_(v in p_i star_k p_j)
     B_(F_(E;L minus {i,j}))(q,v).
```

Summing over the unordered indexed pairs gives `(P23.11z5zc4c)`, since
each `beta_i^E` occurs `n-1` times.  Finally, expanding the two
distinguished differences
`(V_q box-times 1-1 box-times V_q)` and
`(V_(p_i) box-times 1-1 box-times V_(p_i))` against the symmetric table
in `(P23.11z5zc4b)` gives twice its boundary defect, exactly as in
`(P25.29e9)`.  This identifies `2 beta_i^E` with the stated contraction.
QED.

In particular, if every fused shorter defect on the right of
`(P23.11z5zc4c)` is nonnegative for this same background, then
`sum_i beta_i^E(L;q)>=0`; and a negative component vertex
`beta_i^E=-d` forces the other `n-1` vertices to carry at least `d` each.
This is the exact higher-minus cumulative reserve.  It still does not
produce the transport that returns this reserve to a prescribed `i`.

The strict C++ verifier
`character_ring_iter/verify_su2_even_background_current.cpp` constructs
the signed background table independently, checks its symmetry, verifies
`(P23.11z5zc4c)`, and separately expands both new minus differences to
check the factor-two contraction assertion.  It also exhausts the
two-bit fusion identity `(P23.11z5zc4ha)` over every even sign mask of
each tested indexed label word.  For words of at most twelve indexed
factors it now independently computes every subset invariant
`m_(A_T)(0)` by direct fusion and compares the full Fourier sum
`(P23.11z5zc4k)` against the signed contraction at every even sign set.
Thus this last audit shares neither the leave-one-out construction nor the
two-bit reduction.  A replay returns

```text
SU2_EVEN_BACKGROUND_CURRENT levels=2..5 labels<=3
background_factors<=1 leaves<=5 backgrounds=15
currents=13320 contractions=60504 hypercube_edges=1351062
invariant_split_fourier=101302 result=PASS.
```

The earlier medium exact replay returns

```text
SU2_EVEN_BACKGROUND_CURRENT levels=2..5 labels<=3
background_factors<=3 leaves<=3 backgrounds=433
currents=43152 contractions=118582 hypercube_edges=1351062 result=PASS.
```

The earlier current-only replay returns

```text
SU2_EVEN_BACKGROUND_CURRENT levels=2..6 labels<=4
background_factors<=3 leaves<=3 backgrounds=1052
currents=296352 contractions=828946 result=PASS.
```

These are implementation audits of the uniform symmetry proof and finite
fusion identities, including affine walls; they are not bounded substitutes
for either corollary.

The same statement can be written directly on the sign-placement graph.
This is the precise arbitrary-factor current supplied by the fused-leaf
identity.

**Corollary 23A9L1B (Johnson-star fused current).**  Let
`A=(a_1,...,a_N)` be an indexed label list, and for an even set of minus
positions `S` write

```text
J_A(S)=[1 box-times 1]
 product_(i in S)(V_(a_i) box-times 1-1 box-times V_(a_i))
 product_(i notin S)(V_(a_i) box-times 1+1 box-times V_(a_i)).
                                                        (P23.11z5zc4d)
```

This is the signed contraction of the word with minus set `S`.  Fix an
odd set `C` of positions and put `R=[N] minus C`, with `|R|>=2`.  For
distinct `i,j in R` and `v in a_i star_k a_j`, let `A_(ij:v)` be the
indexed list obtained by deleting positions `i,j` and adjoining one new
position `star` labelled `v`.  Then

```text
J_A(C union {i})+J_A(C union {j})
 =2 sum_(v in a_i star_k a_j)
    J_(A_(ij:v))(C union {star}),                    (P23.11z5zc4e)

(|R|-1) sum_(i in R)J_A(C union {i})
 =2 sum_(i<j, i,j in R) sum_(v in a_i star_k a_j)
    J_(A_(ij:v))(C union {star}).                    (P23.11z5zc4f)
```

Both formulas hold in the ordinary ring and in every `SU(2)_k`.  Hence if
all the one-factor-shorter contractions on the right of
`(P23.11z5zc4e)` are nonnegative, every pair sum in this Johnson star is
nonnegative; if those on the right of `(P23.11z5zc4f)` are nonnegative,
the complete star current is nonnegative.

**Proof.**  Choose any `q in C`, let `E=C minus {q}` carry its inherited
minus signs, and regard the positions in `R` as the plus list `L`.  The
background `E` has even minus parity, so Corollary 23A9L1A applies.  Its
`beta_i^E(L;q)` satisfies

```text
J_A(C union {i})=2 beta_i^E(L;q).                    (P23.11z5zc4g)
```

After fusing `i,j` to `v`, the same two-difference expansion gives

```text
J_(A_(ij:v))(C union {star})
 =2 B_(F_(E;L minus {i,j}))(q,v).                    (P23.11z5zc4h)
```

Multiply the pair identity and the leave-one-out identity of Corollary
23A9L1A by two and substitute `(P23.11z5zc4g)--(P23.11z5zc4h)`.  This is
exactly `(P23.11z5zc4e)--(P23.11z5zc4f)`.  Fusion is multiplicity-free in
`SU(2)_k`, and the identities retained the full fusion sums, so the finite
and ordinary statements are identical.  QED.

Corollary 23A9L1B is the corrected global-payment reduction available at
arbitrary factor number: finite certification of the fused shorter words
pays every Johnson-star current.  It is deliberately a component result.
The abstract assignment with one negative star vertex and all other
vertices carrying the opposite value satisfies both displayed conclusions,
so a separate overlap/transport theorem is still necessary to deduce
`J_A(S)>=0` for one prescribed sign set `S`.

The same two-factor calculation supplies the missing edges between distinct
minus layers.  It is useful to retain the full even hypercube rather than
only its fixed-layer Johnson subgraphs.

**Corollary 23A9L1B2 (two-bit fused hypercube relation).**  Let `S` be any
even subset of `[N]`, let `i!=j`, and put

```text
C=S minus {i,j},             epsilon=|S intersection {i,j}| mod 2.
```

For `v in a_i star_k a_j`, let `S_(ij:v)` be the sign set on
`A_(ij:v)` obtained from `C` by giving the new `star` position minus sign
exactly when `epsilon=1`.  Then

```text
J_A(S)+J_A(S triangle {i,j})
 =2 sum_(v in a_i star_k a_j) J_(A_(ij:v))(S_(ij:v)).  (P23.11z5zc4ha)
```

This holds ordinarily and in every `SU(2)_k`.  Therefore uniform
nonnegativity for the fused `(N-1)`-factor words gives

```text
J_A(S)+J_A(S triangle {i,j})>=0                    (P23.11z5zc4hb)
```

for every edge of the even sign hypercube.  The `epsilon=1` case is the
Johnson-star pair law `(P23.11z5zc4e)`; the `epsilon=0` case links the
layers `|S|` and `|S|+/-2`.

**Proof.**  Write `X_l=V_(a_l) box-times 1` and
`Y_l=1 box-times V_(a_l)`.  The two sign assignments at `i,j` have sum

```text
(X_i+Y_i)(X_j+Y_j)+(X_i-Y_i)(X_j-Y_j)
 =2(X_iX_j+Y_iY_j)                                  if epsilon=0,

(X_i-Y_i)(X_j+Y_j)+(X_i+Y_i)(X_j-Y_j)
 =2(X_iX_j-Y_iY_j)                                  if epsilon=1.
```

Fuse `X_iX_j` and `Y_iY_j` through every
`v in a_i star_k a_j`.  In the first line this creates a plus `star`
position and in the second a minus `star` position, giving
`(P23.11z5zc4ha)`.  The asserted inequality follows from the induction
hypothesis on each fused word.  QED.

Corollary 23A9L1B2 is a genuine overlap enlargement: it couples all even
minus layers, and the graph with edges `S--S triangle {i,j}` is connected.
It still cannot by itself establish an individual sign placement.  The
abstract value assignment `J(S_0)=-1` and `J(T)=1` for every other even
vertex satisfies every inequality `(P23.11z5zc4hb)`.  Hence any successful
transport must retain shared ticket capacity or a coherent Plucker/TL
resolution, rather than only nonnegative scalar combinations of these
edge relations.

Summing the Johnson-star law gives a literal global payment identity at
every even minus layer.

**Corollary 23A9L1C (global fixed-minus-layer current).**  Let `m` be even
with `2<=m<=N-1`.  In the notation of Corollary 23A9L1B,

```text
m(N-m) sum_(S subset [N], |S|=m) J_A(S)
 =2 sum_(C subset [N], |C|=m-1)
    sum_({i,j} subset [N] minus C)
    sum_(v in a_i star_k a_j)
       J_(A_(ij:v))(C union {star}).                 (P23.11z5zc4i)
```

Thus uniform nonnegativity of the fused `(N-1)`-factor words proves the
complete signed average over all `m`-minus placements at length `N`.

**Proof.**  Sum `(P23.11z5zc4f)` over all `(m-1)`-subsets `C`.  On the
left, a fixed `m`-subset `S` occurs once for each choice of the distinguished
position `i in S`, namely with `C=S minus {i}`.  It therefore occurs `m`
times, while `|[N] minus C|-1=N-m`.  This gives the left side of
`(P23.11z5zc4i)`, and the right side is the summed right side of
`(P23.11z5zc4f)`.  QED.

Formula `(P23.11z5zc4i)` is a global payment, not an individual-sign proof:
the all-layer average can be nonnegative with an isolated negative sign
placement.  The missing lemma must exploit overlap between the Johnson
stars (or the coherent Plucker/Temperley--Lieb ticket transport), rather
than only their scalar sums.

There is one further exact structure behind every Johnson current.  It is
stronger than an arbitrary scalar assignment, but still does not by itself
close the global payment.

**Lemma 23A9L1D (invariant-split Fourier form).**  For every subset
`T subset [N]`, put

```text
d_A(T)=m_(A_T)(0),
c_A(T)=d_A(T)d_A(T^c).                              (P23.11z5zc4j)
```

Then, for every even sign set `S`,

```text
J_A(S)=sum_(T subset [N])(-1)^|S intersection T| c_A(T).       (P23.11z5zc4k)
```

In particular, `J_A` is positive definite on the even Boolean subgroup,
its Fourier weights are nonnegative and complement-symmetric, and
`c_A(T)` has the displayed invariant-split factorization.

**Proof.**  In the product defining `(P23.11z5zc4d)`, choose the second
coordinate term exactly at the positions `T`.  The first coordinate then
has product `X_(A_(T^c))` and the second has `X_(A_T)`, so its
`V_0 box-times V_0` coefficient is precisely `(P23.11z5zc4j)`.  The sign
is `(-1)^|S intersection T|`.  Summing the expansion proves
`(P23.11z5zc4k)`.  Positivity and complement symmetry of the Fourier
weights are immediate.  QED.

The Fourier positivity, the singleton zeros forced by positive labels, and
all scalar two-bit inequalities are nevertheless still insufficient.  Thus
the missing ingredient is specifically the overlap compatibility of genuine
`A_1` invariant multiplicities.

**Proposition 23A9L1E (factorized Fourier-current obstruction).**  On the
even Boolean subgroup of four positions, there are nonnegative numbers
`d(T)=d(T^c)`, with `d(T)=0` for every singleton and co-singleton, such
that the factorized Fourier current

```text
J(S)=sum_T (-1)^|S intersection T| d(T)d(T^c)        (P23.11z5zc4l)
```

satisfies every scalar two-bit inequality

```text
J(S)+J(S triangle {i,j})>=0,                         (P23.11z5zc4m)
```

but has a negative value.

**Proof.**  Put

```text
d(empty)=d({1,2,3,4})=1,
d({1,3})=d({2,4})=d({1,4})=d({2,3})=1,               (P23.11z5zc4n)
```

and set every other `d(T)` to zero.  On even `S`, complementarity gives

```text
J(S)=2+2 chi_(13)(S)+2 chi_(14)(S),
chi_(ij)(S)=(-1)^|S intersection {i,j}|.             (P23.11z5zc4o)
```

At `S={1,2}`, both characters are `-1`, so `J(S)=-2`.  A flip of either
`{1,2}` or `{3,4}` reverses both characters, and its pair sum is `4`.
A flip of one of `{1,3},{2,4}` preserves `chi_(13)` and reverses
`chi_(14)`, giving pair sum `4+4chi_(13)`, which is `0` or `8`; the two
remaining flips are symmetric.  Hence every instance of `(P23.11z5zc4m)`
holds.

This model cannot arise from positive `SU(2)` labels: the four nonzero
two-factor invariants in `(P23.11z5zc4n)` force, successively,
`a_1=a_3=a_4=a_2`, which would also make `{1,2}` invariant.  It proves that
the global argument must use precisely these fused overlap constraints, not
only positive definiteness, complement symmetry, singleton vanishing, or
the factorization in `(P23.11z5zc4j)`.  QED.

The exact positive multiplicities are also essential; invariant feasibility
alone cannot supply the missing transport.

**Proposition 23A9L1F (invariant-support Fourier obstruction).**  In
`SU(2)_2`, take the indexed word

```text
A=(1,1,1,1,2)
```

and let `S={1,2}` be the first two fundamental positions.  Replace the
Fourier weight in `(P23.11z5zc4j)` by its support indicator

```text
c^supp_A(T)=indicator_(d_A(T)d_A(T^c)>0).
```

Then its even Fourier coefficient is negative:

```text
sum_T (-1)^|S intersection T|c^supp_A(T)=-2,          (P23.11z5zc4p)
```

whereas the genuine current is zero:

```text
J_A(S)=0.                                              (P23.11z5zc4q)
```

**Proof.**  Put `I={1,2,3,4}`.  Besides the empty and full cuts, the cuts
for which both sides carry an invariant are exactly the six two-subsets
`U subset I` and their six complements `U^c union {5}`.  Their invariant
multiplicities on both sides are one, whereas

```text
d_A(empty)=1,                 d_A({1,2,3,4,5})=2.
```

All other cuts have zero weight.  Hence
`c_A(empty)=c_A({1,2,3,4,5})=2`; every one of the other twelve nonzero cut
weights is one.  Among the six two-subsets the signed sum is `-2` (two have
even and four have odd intersection with `S`), and complementation gives
another `-2`.  Support weights therefore give `2-2-2=-2`, while the true
empty/full weights give `4-2-2=0`.

The strict C++ check

```text
verify_su2_even_background_current --support-fourier-nogo
```

returns

```text
INVARIANT_SUPPORT_FOURIER_NOGO level=2 labels=1,1,1,1,2
minus_mask=3 support_value=-2 exact_value=0 result=PASS.
```

QED.

This is a genuinely fused-channel statement: all intermediate labels of
the new `V_p` leaf have already been summed with their exact fusion
multiplicities, including affine-wall truncation.  It does not project a
divided-power Plucker switch back to whole-block cuts.  It also gives a
sharp no-go for a leafwise positivity induction.  The remainder
`C_F(p,q;a)` has no fixed sign.  Already for the one-leaf background

```text
F=(V_(1,x) direct-sum V_(1,y)),       (p,q,a)=(2,2,1)
```

in the ordinary ring, one has

```text
C_F(2,2;1)=-1.                                       (P23.11z5zd)
```

Indeed the first sum in `(P23.11z5y)` is zero, whereas the second contains
the unique channel `0 in 2 star 2` and `F(0,1)=1`.  The same calculation
works in `SU(2)_k` for every `k>=2`.  Thus a proof cannot make every local
fused remainder positive by a choice of `F`-move gauges or triangular
ordering: the opposite orientation has the negated remainder by
`(P23.11z5zb)`.  What recoupling does provide is the exact cancellation
`(P23.11z5zc)` across opposite updates.

**Corollary 23A9M (exact oscillation criterion and
minimal-counterexample restriction).**  Put

```text
R_F(p,q,a)=sum_(v in p star_k a)B_F(q,v).
```

If `R_F(p,q,a)>=0`, the two opposite updated boundary defects in
`(P23.11z5zc)` are both nonnegative if and only if

```text
|C_F(p,q;a)|
 <=R_F(p,q,a).                                        (P23.11z5ze)
```

Equivalently, put

```text
Theta_B(p,q,a)=sum_(u in p star_k q)B_F(u,a).
```

Then `(P23.11z5ze)` is exactly the fusion-triangle inequality

```text
|Theta_B(p,q,a)-Theta_B(q,a,p)|
 <=Theta_B(p,a,q).                                    (P23.11z5zf)
```

In particular, in a counterexample having the fewest indexed plus leaves,
neither external label `q` nor external label `a` can occur among the plus
labels.

**Proof.**  Equations `(P23.11z5za)--(P23.11z5zb)` identify the two
updated defects with `R_F+C_F` and `R_F-C_F`; for nonnegative `R_F`, both
are nonnegative exactly when `(P23.11z5ze)` holds.

For the triangle form, write `G(t)=F(0,t)`.  The boundary definition gives

```text
F(r,s)=sum_t N_(r,s)^t G(t)-B_F(r,s).
```

Substitution in `(P23.11z5y)` cancels the two `G` terms by fusion
associativity and leaves

```text
C_F(p,q;a)=Theta_B(p,q,a)-Theta_B(q,a,p),
R_F(p,q,a)=Theta_B(p,a,q).
```

This proves the equivalence with `(P23.11z5zf)`.

Now suppose a shortest counterexample contains a plus leaf `p=a`.  Its
shorter background has all boundary defects nonnegative, while
`C_F(a,q;a)=0` by `(P23.11z5zb)`.  Equation `(P23.11z5za)` makes the
claimed counterexample nonnegative, a contradiction.  Since
`F(q,a)=F(a,q)` and `q star_k a=a star_k q`, the definition
`(P23.11z5y)` gives `B_F(q,a)=B_F(a,q)`.  The same argument after
exchanging the two external labels excludes a plus leaf `p=q`.  QED.

The oriented remainder also has an exact determinant interpretation in the
fused `USp(4)` basis.  In the ordinary ring put

```text
P(x,y)=product_i[chi_(p_i)(x)+chi_(p_i)(y)],
dnu_1^norm=(1/2)(x-y)^2 dmu(x)dmu(y),

E_(p,a)(x,y)
 =[chi_p(x)chi_a(y)-chi_a(x)chi_p(y)]/(x-y).
```

**Lemma 23A9N (symplectic determinant factorization and sign no-go).**
For all `p,q,a`,

```text
C_F(p,q;a)
 =-integral D_q E_(p,a) P dnu_1^norm,                 (P23.11z5zg)
```

and

```text
E_(p,a)=
  Psi_(p-1,a),              p>a;
  0,                         p=a;
 -Psi_(a-1,p),              p<a.                     (P23.11z5zh)
```

Nevertheless the proposed orientation rule

```text
C_F(p,q;a)(p-a)<=0                                  (P23.11z5zi)
```

is false.  Its one-leaf counterexample is

```text
P=S_2,                  (p,q,a)=(2,1,1),             (P23.11z5zj)
```

for which `C_F(2,1;1)=1`.  The same fusion calculation is valid in every
`SU(2)_k`, `k>=2`.  Together with `(P23.11z5zd)`, where `p>a` but
`C_F=-1`, this shows that neither orientation can depend only on the sign
of `p-a`.

**Proof.**  Character orthogonality writes the two terms of
`(P23.11z5y)` as

```text
sum_(t in q star a)F(p,t)
 =integral chi_p(x)chi_q(y)chi_a(y)P(x,y)dmu(x)dmu(y),

sum_(u in p star q)F(u,a)
 =integral chi_p(x)chi_q(x)chi_a(y)P(x,y)dmu(x)dmu(y).
```

Since `P` is symmetric in `x,y`, antisymmetrizing the remaining factor
gives

```text
C_F(p,q;a)
 =-(1/2)integral [chi_q(x)-chi_q(y)]
   [chi_p(x)chi_a(y)-chi_a(x)chi_p(y)]P dmu(x)dmu(y).
```

Using

```text
D_q=[chi_q(x)-chi_q(y)]/(x-y)
```

proves `(P23.11z5zg)`.  Formula `(P23.11z5zh)` is the `USp(4)` Weyl
determinant formula for `Psi_(r,s)`, with the two rows exchanged when
`p<a`.

For `(P23.11z5zj)`, the only nonzero entries of the one-leaf table are

```text
F(2,0)=F(0,2)=1.
```

The first sum in `C_F(2,1;1)` runs over `1 star_k 1` and contains the
channel zero, so it equals one.  The second runs over `2 star_k 1` and
equals zero.  Thus `C_F=1` although `p-a=1`.  Equivalently,

```text
D_1=Psi_(0,0),        E_(2,1)=Psi_(1,1),
S_2=Psi_(2,0)-Psi_(1,1)+Psi_(0,0),
```

so `(P23.11z5zg)` gives `C_F=-(-1)=1` directly by `USp(4)`
orthogonality.  QED.

**Lemma 23A9Q (disjoint affine no-margin family).**  In `SU(2)_3`, let
`F_n` be the coefficient table of the plus background `S_2^n`.  For every
`n>=0`,

```text
R_(F_n)(2,1,1)-|C_(F_n)(2,1;1)|=1.                  (P23.11z5zj1)
```

For `n>=1` the denominator `R_(F_n)(2,1,1)` tends to infinity.  Hence

```text
|C_(F_n)(2,1;1)|/R_(F_n)(2,1,1) -> 1                (P23.11z5zj2)
```

strictly from below.  This family obeys the minimal-counterexample
restriction in Corollary 23A9M: the updated plus word contains only label
two, whereas `q=a=1`.  Thus no proof of `(P23.11z5ze)` can use a uniform
positive additive gap larger than the integral unit, or a uniform relative
gap away from one.

**Proof.**  Only the even labels `0,2` occur in `F_n`.  Write its even block
as

```text
F_n|_(0,2) = [[x_n,y_n],[y_n,z_n]].
```

On this block,

```text
N_2=[[0,1],[1,1]],
```

and the plus update `F_(n+1)=N_2F_n+F_nN_2` gives

```text
x_(n+1)=2y_n,
y_(n+1)=x_n+y_n+z_n,
z_(n+1)=2y_n+2z_n.                                  (P23.11z5zj3)
```

Since `(x_0,y_0,z_0)=(1,0,0)`, subtraction in `(P23.11z5zj3)` shows

```text
x_n+y_n-z_n=1                                       (P23.11z5zj4)
```

for every `n`.  At `(p,q,a)=(2,1,1)`, the `SU(2)_3` fusion rules give

```text
C_(F_n)(2,1;1)=y_n+z_n,
R_(F_n)(2,1,1)
 =B_(F_n)(1,1)+B_(F_n)(1,3)=x_n+2y_n.
```

Their difference is `(P23.11z5zj4)`.  Finally all three sequences are
nonnegative, and `(P23.11z5zj3)` gives
`y_(n+2)>=2y_n` once `y_1=1`; hence `R_(F_n)>=2y_n` is unbounded.  This
proves `(P23.11z5zj1)--(P23.11z5zj2)`.  QED.

The exact C++ diagnostic
`character_ring_iter/search_su2_boundary_oscillation.cpp` constructs every
actual plus-word table with arbitrary-precision integer arithmetic and
tests `(P23.11z5ze)`, the individual background defects, the disjoint
restriction, and the rejected sign rule `(P23.11z5zi)`.  Its finite replay
covered the complete rectangle `1<=k<=16`, background length `0<=n<=9`,
every multiset word with labels in `1,...,k`, every `1<=p,q<=k`, and every
`0<=a<=k`: `5,311,734` backgrounds and `18,132,703,200` exact triples.
No oscillation deficit or negative background defect occurred.  The
ordinary replay through label ten and length nine covered `101,615,800`
exact triples and likewise found no oscillation deficit.  The replay and
the disjoint extremal data are recorded in
`certificates/su2_boundary_oscillation_summary.log`.  These bounded searches
are diagnostic only; Lemma 23A9Q, not the search, proves the unbounded
no-margin statement.

The finite sine transform gives a sharp obstruction to inheriting the
boundary inequality term by term from a cyclic or dihedral character
inequality.  Put `N=k+2`,

```text
theta_j=(j+1)pi/N,                     0<=j<=k,
mu_j=(2/N)sin(theta_j)^2,
c_r(theta)=2cos(r theta).
```

Thus `mu` is the `SU(2)_k` spectral measure at `V_0`; it is the Weyl
`h^2` transform with `h(theta)=sin(theta)`.  Pointwise,

```text
c_1=chi_1,                    c_3=chi_3-chi_1.
```

**Lemma 23A9P (two-minus Weyl-transform no-go).**  For every `k>=3` and
every `1<=r<=k-2`, the uniform cyclic average on the `2N`th roots
satisfies

```text
E_cyc[(c_r(x)-c_r(y))(c_(r+2)(x)-c_(r+2)(y))]=0,     (P23.11z5zk)
```

whereas its Weyl `h^2` transform satisfies

```text
E_(mu tensor mu)[
 (c_r(x)-c_r(y))(c_(r+2)(x)-c_(r+2)(y))]=-2.         (P23.11z5zl)
```

Hence the Weyl/Doob transform does not preserve even the specific
two-minus cyclic GKS inequality.  In the smallest case, regrouping the
cyclic constituents into the complete `SU(2)` character restores
nonnegativity:

```text
chi_3=c_3+c_1,

E_(mu tensor mu)[
 (chi_1(x)-chi_1(y))(chi_3(x)-chi_3(y))]
 =-2+2=0.                                            (P23.11z5zm)
```

**Proof.**  On the cyclic group of order `2N>=10`, the bounds
`1<=r<=N-4` imply that `c_r,c_(r+2)` have zero means and are distinct
noninverse real characters.  They are therefore orthogonal.  The
elementary covariance identity

```text
E[(f(x)-f(y))(g(x)-g(y))]
 =2{E[fg]-E[f]E[g]}
```

therefore proves `(P23.11z5zk)`.

For the sine measure use, for every `r>=1`,

```text
c_r=chi_r-chi_(r-2),                 chi_s=0 for s<0.
```

Character orthogonality in `SU(2)_k` gives

```text
E_mu[c_r c_(r+2)]
 =tau_k[(chi_r-chi_(r-2))(chi_(r+2)-chi_r)]=-1.
```

Moreover `E_mu[c_r]=0` except at `r=2`, where it is `-1`, while
`E_mu[c_(r+2)]=0` throughout the stated range.  Hence

```text
Cov_mu(c_r,c_(r+2))=-1,
```

and the covariance identity proves `(P23.11z5zl)`.  For the regrouping
example `r=1`, the displayed identities specialize to

```text
E_mu[c_1]=E_mu[c_3]=0,
E_mu[c_1c_3]=tau_k[chi_1(chi_3-chi_1)]=-1.
```

Finally `E_mu[c_1^2]=1`, so the added diagonal term in
`chi_3=c_3+c_1` contributes two and proves `(P23.11z5zm)`.  QED.

The fusion-triangle criterion itself closes uniformly for the first three
updated plus leaves.  Write

```text
I(b_1,...,b_m)=dim Hom(1,V_(b_1) star_k ... star_k V_(b_m)),
```

with the ordinary tensor product in the stable ring.  All labels below are
nontrivial.

**Proposition 23A9R (two-leaf fusion-triangle base theorem).**  Let `F`
be the plus table of a background containing at most two indexed leaves,
adjoin a further leaf `p`, and assume that the two external labels satisfy

```text
q,a notin {all background labels,p}.                 (P23.11z5zn)
```

Then the fusion-triangle inequality `(P23.11z5zf)` holds, ordinarily and
in every `SU(2)_k` containing the displayed labels.  More precisely:

1.  For the empty background,

```text
C_F(p,q;a)=0,          R_F(p,q,a)=N_(p,q)^a.          (P23.11z5zo)
```

2.  For the one-leaf background `[r]`,

```text
C_F(p,q;a)=indicator_(q=a)indicator_(p=r),
R_F(p,q,a)=I(p,q,a,r).                               (P23.11z5zp)
```

3.  For the two-leaf background `[r,s]`,

```text
C_F(p,q;a)
 =indicator_(q=a)N_(r,s)^p
  +indicator_(p=s)N_(q,a)^r
  +indicator_(p=r)N_(q,a)^s,

R_F(p,q,a)
 =I(p,q,a,r,s)+indicator_(r=s)N_(p,a)^q.             (P23.11z5zq)
```

Thus equality in `(P23.11z5ze)` occurs exactly when the two quantities on
the corresponding right sides of `(P23.11z5zo)--(P23.11z5zq)` are equal.
In particular, in the one-leaf case it is equivalent to

```text
I(p,q,a,r)=indicator_(q=a)indicator_(p=r).            (P23.11z5zr)
```

If the indicator vanishes, this says exactly that the fusion intervals
`p star_k q` and `a star_k r` are disjoint.  If the indicator is one,
ordinary equality never occurs, while finite-level equality occurs exactly
when `p=k` or `q=k`.

**Proof.**  With no background leaves,

```text
B_F(u,v)=indicator_(u=v>0).
```

Therefore all three cyclic `Theta_B` values equal the symmetric fusion
coefficient `N_(p,q)^a`, proving `(P23.11z5zo)`.

For one background leaf, direct expansion of its two colour assignments
gives, for `v>0`,

```text
B_F(u,v)=N_(u,v)^r-indicator_(u=0)indicator_(v=r).
```

Consequently

```text
Theta_B(x,y,z)
 =I(x,y,z,r)-indicator_(x=y)indicator_(z=r).          (P23.11z5zs)
```

Apply `(P23.11z5zs)` to the three cyclic orders and use
`(P23.11z5zn)`.  This gives `(P23.11z5zp)`.  If its indicator is one,
pair the two copies of `q=a` and the two copies of `p=r` to obtain an
invariant path, so `I(p,q,a,r)>=1`.  Hence `C_F<=R_F`, and the equality
statement is immediate.  Since fusion is multiplicity-free,

```text
I(p,q,a,r)=|(p star_k q) intersection (a star_k r)|.
```

When `q=a,p=r`, this cardinality is

```text
min(p,q,k-p,k-q)+1
```

at finite level and `min(p,q)+1` ordinarily.  The labels are nontrivial,
which proves the refined equality assertions.

For two background leaves, their four indexed colour assignments give,
for `z>0`,

```text
B_F(u,z)
 =I(u,z,r,s)+indicator_(u=z)indicator_(r=s)
  -indicator_(u=0)N_(r,s)^z
  -indicator_(u=r)indicator_(z=s)
  -indicator_(u=s)indicator_(z=r).
```

Summing over `u in x star_k y` yields

```text
Theta_B(x,y,z)
 =I(x,y,z,r,s)+indicator_(r=s)N_(x,y)^z
  -indicator_(x=y)N_(r,s)^z
  -N_(x,y)^r indicator_(z=s)
  -N_(x,y)^s indicator_(z=r).                         (P23.11z5zt)
```

The common five-fold invariant term cancels from the oriented difference.
The symmetric fusion identity

```text
N_(p,q)^a=N_(q,a)^p
```

cancels the common `r=s` term.  Condition `(P23.11z5zn)` then turns the
three cyclic instances of `(P23.11z5zt)` into `(P23.11z5zq)`.

It remains to prove that the displayed `C_F` does not exceed `R_F`.
Use the exact path decomposition

```text
I(p,q,a,r,s)
 =sum_(t in q star_k a) sum_(u in r star_k s) N_(t,u)^p. (P23.11z5zu)
```

If `r!=s`, each nonzero term of `C_F` supplies a path in
`(P23.11z5zu)` with respectively

```text
t=0,                  t=r,                  t=s.
```

These channels are distinct.  For the second and third choices, existence
follows from the full symmetry
`N_(r,s)^u=N_(r,u)^s=N_(s,u)^r`; choose any
`u in r star_k s`.  Hence `I>=C_F`.

Suppose `r=s`.  The first contribution still uses the distinct channel
`t=0`.  If `p=r` and `N_(q,a)^r=1`, the last two contributions require
two paths over `t=r`.  There are

```text
|r star_k r|=min(r,k-r)+1
```

such paths at finite level, and `r+1` ordinarily.  This is at least two
unless `r=k`.  In the exceptional simple-current case `r=p=k`, the
five-fold invariant supplies one path, while fusion symmetry gives

```text
N_(p,a)^q=N_(q,a)^p=1;
```

the extra term in `R_F` supplies the second unit.  Thus `C_F<=R_F` in all
cases.  Since `C_F>=0`, equality in the absolute-value inequality is
exactly equality of the two explicit quantities in
`(P23.11z5zq)`.  QED.

The first layer not covered by the six-factor theorem has an exact
ten-cut form.  It removes all singleton and redundant colour assignments
before any straightening argument.  For an indexed set
`P={p_1,...,p_5}`, write `m(L)` for the invariant multiplicity of the
listed tensor product, ordinary or in `SU(2)_k`.  For `E subset P`, the
notation remembers the indices even when labels coincide.

**Proposition 23A9S (equivalent five-plus `3|4` inequality).**  Assume

```text
q,a notin {p_1,...,p_5}.                              (P23.11z5zv)
```

Define

```text
N=m(q,a,P),

P_eq=indicator_(q=a)m(P)
     +sum_(E subset P, |E|=2)
        indicator_(the two labels in E are equal)m(q,a,P minus E),

U=sum_(i=1)^5 m(q,a,p_i)m(P minus {p_i})
  +sum_(E subset P, |E|=2)m(q,a,E)m(P minus E),

T=sum_(E subset P, |E|=2){
     m(q,E)m(a,P minus E)+m(a,E)m(q,P minus E)}.      (P23.11z5zw)
```

Then the signed contraction with minus labels `q,a` and the five plus
labels is exactly

```text
(1/2) tau_k tensor tau_k{
 d_q d_a product_(i=1)^5 S_(p_i)}
 =N+P_eq+U-T.                                         (P23.11z5zx)
```

Consequently the complete seven-factor, two-minus layer is equivalent to
the single indexed inequality

```text
T<=N+P_eq+U.                                          (P23.11z5zy)
```

This equivalence is uniform at the affine wall.  If one plus leaf `p_i`
is designated as the last fused update and `F` is the table of the other
four leaves, the left side of `(P23.11z5zx)` is
`B_(F^[p_i])(q,a)=R_F(p_i,q,a)+C_F(p_i,q;a)`.
Thus `(P23.11z5zy)` is also the explicit `3|4` form of the first
unresolved fused-triangle orientation.

**Proof.**  Expand the five plus factors by an indexed subset `A subset P`
assigned to the first coordinate, and pair each complete colour assignment
with its coordinate reversal.  Retain the representative in which the
minus label `q` lies in the first coordinate.  If `a` lies there as well,
the contribution is

```text
m(q,a,A)m(P minus A);
```

if `a` lies in the second coordinate, it is

```text
-m(q,A)m(a,P minus A).                                (P23.11z5zz)
```

Their sum over all `A` is the left side of `(P23.11z5zx)`.

For the negative term, `|A|=0` or `5` leaves a nontrivial singleton
component.  If `|A|=1`, its first component is the pair `{q,p_i}`; if
`|A|=4`, its second component is `{a,p_i}`.  All four cases vanish by
`(P23.11z5zv)`.  The surviving sizes `2` and `3` pair by complementation
and give exactly `T`.

For the positive term, `|A|=4` leaves a nontrivial singleton and vanishes.
The cases `|A|=5` and `0` give respectively `N` and the first term of
`P_eq`.  Size one gives the first sum in `U`, and size two gives its second
sum.  At size three, the complementary two-label invariant is nonzero
exactly when its two labels are equal; these are precisely the remaining
terms of `P_eq`.  This proves `(P23.11z5zx)` and hence the equivalence with
`(P23.11z5zy)`.

Finally, the boundary definition identifies

```text
B_(F^[p_i])(q,a)
 =sum_(t in q star_k a)F^[p_i](0,t)-F^[p_i](q,a)
```

with the same retained-coordinate assignment sum `(P23.11z5zz)`.
Lemma 23A9L gives its fused `R_F+C_F` form.  No stability assumption enters
either calculation.  QED.

The same inequality has a symmetric allocation-correlation form for
arbitrary minus labels.  This is the nonfundamental analogue of the
specialized identity in Lemma 23A9U3.

**Lemma 23A9S1 (exact arbitrary-minus allocation form).**  Under the
hypotheses of Proposition 23A9S, for an indexed subset of plus positions
`E subset [5]` write

```text
m_r(E)=multiplicity of V_r in product_(i in E)V_(p_i),
c_P(r,s)=sum_(E subset [5])m_r(E)m_s(E^c).
```

Then

```text
T=c_P(q,a),
N+P_eq+U=sum_(t in q star_k a)c_P(t,0).             (P23.11z5zy1)
```

Consequently the complete finite seven-factor inequality is exactly

```text
c_P(q,a)<=sum_(t in q star_k a)c_P(t,0).            (P23.11z5zy2)
```

If the maximal active-cut rank is at most two, every nonzero summand on
the left of `(P23.11z5zy2)` is one or two.

**Proof.**  In `c_P(q,a)`, subset sizes zero and five vanish because
`q,a>0`.  Sizes one and four vanish by the disjoint-support hypothesis.
The size-two terms are

```text
m_q(E)m_a(E^c),
```

the first orientation in `T`.  Complementing each size-three subset
gives the second orientation.  Hence `T=c_P(q,a)`.

For the positive side, associativity and multiplicity-free binary fusion
give

```text
sum_(t in q star_k a)c_P(t,0)
 =sum_(E subset [5])m(q,a,E)m_0(E^c).              (P23.11z5zy3)
```

The size-five term is `N`.  The size-zero term is
`indicator_(q=a)m(P)`.  Sizes one and two are respectively the two sums
defining `U`.  At size three, the complementary two-label invariant is
nonzero exactly when those two indexed plus labels are equal; these are
the equal-plus terms in `P_eq`.  Size four vanishes because its complement
is a nontrivial singleton.  This proves both identities in
`(P23.11z5zy1)` and hence `(P23.11z5zy2)`.

Finally a two-label block has multiplicity at most one.  Thus every
active term in `c_P(q,a)` is its complementary four-label rank, which is
one or two in the stated chamber.  QED.

Fusion depth at least three forces a sharp endpoint dichotomy on every
rank-one or rank-two complement.

**Lemma 23A9S2 (small-overlap endpoint skeleton).**  Assume the
hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S1 and

```text
|q star_k a|>=3.
```

Choose an active oriented cut with invariant triple
`A={r,x,y}`, where `r` is one minus label, and write its four-label
complement as

```text
B={s,u,v,w},
```

where `s` is the other minus label.  Pair
`B=(s,u)|(v,w)`, put

```text
I=s star_k u,             J=v star_k w,
K=I intersection J,      d=|K|=m_0(B)<=2,
b_j=m_j(B).
```

Then `0 notin K`, and the following alternatives are exhaustive.

```text
d=1:  either B contains the plus label k, or b_2>=3;

d=2:  b_2>=3, b_4>=1, and either b_2>=4 or
      I=J=K and B contains at least two indexed plus labels
      in {1,k-1}.                                  (P23.11z5zy4)
```

Moreover the active triple has one of the two profiles

```text
k notin {x,y}:   (m_0(A),m_2(A),m_4(A))>=(1,2,1);

{x,y}={k,k-r}:   m_(2j)(A)=1
                  for 0<=j<=min(r,k-r),
                  and every other m_s(A)=0.         (P23.11z5zy5)
```

The second line is the only case in which the output-two lower bound in
the first line fails.  Hence orthogonality gives the raw lower bounds

```text
d=1, k notin B:       N>=7 if k notin A,  N>=4 if k in A;

d=2:                  N>=9 if k notin A,  N>=6 if k in A;
d=2, b_2>=4:          N>=11 if k notin A, N>=7 if k in A.
                                                               (P23.11z5zy6)
```

Thus the only branches which do not receive the strengthened neighboring
channel count are endpoint-rich: a rank-one complement may contain `k`,
while a rank-two unextended complement contains two labels from
`{1,k-1}`.

**Proof.**  The fusion depth hypothesis is

```text
min(q,a,k-q,k-a)>=2,
```

so both minus labels have cap at least three.  Since `u` is a plus label,
disjoint support gives `0 notin I`: output zero would force `u=s`.
Thus `0 notin K`.

Suppose `d=1`, say `K={z}`.  If either `I` or `J` is a singleton, one of
the two labels defining that fusion interval has cap one.  All labels are
positive, while the pair defining `I` contains the cap-three minus label
`s`; hence a plus label in `B` equals `k`.  If both intervals have at
least two entries, their singleton intersection is a common endpoint.
Because they are step-two intervals, after exchanging `I,J` they contain

```text
z-2,z in I,                    z,z+2 in J.
```

The three ordered pairs

```text
(z-2,z),                       (z,z),       (z,z+2)
```

all fuse to output two.  The existence of the displayed neighbors
handles both triangle walls, and `z>0`; hence `b_2>=3`.

Now let `d=2`, with `K={z,z+2}`.  The three pairs

```text
(z,z),                         (z,z+2),     (z+2,z)
```

give `b_2>=3`.  At least one of these or `(z+2,z+2)` gives output four:
for `z=1` use the two off-diagonal pairs, for `2<=z<=k-3` use either
off-diagonal pair, and for `z=k-2` use `(z,z)`.  Thus `b_4>=1`.

If one interval extends beyond `K`, its nearest new endpoint is `z-2`
or `z+4`.  Pairing it with the nearest endpoint of `K` in the other
interval gives a fourth, distinct output-two path.  Hence `b_2>=4`.
Otherwise `I=J=K`.  A finite binary fusion interval has cardinality

```text
min(cap_k(alpha),cap_k(beta)).
```

Since `cap_k(s)>=3`, the equality `|I|=2` forces
`u in {1,k-1}`.  The equality `|J|=2` forces at least one of `v,w` into
the same two-label set, proving `(P23.11z5zy4)`.

For the active triple put `L=x star_k y`.  Associativity and
multiplicity-free binary fusion give

```text
m_j(A)=|L intersection (r star_k j)|.               (P23.11z5zy4a)
```

Admissibility says `r in L`.  Because `cap_k(r)>=3`,

```text
r star_k 2={r-2,r,r+2},              r in r star_k 4.
```

The interval `L` is a contiguous step-two string.  If it has at least
two entries, one of its entries adjacent to `r` is therefore `r-2` or
`r+2`, and `(P23.11z5zy4a)` gives the first line of
`(P23.11z5zy5)`.

The exact interval cardinality is

```text
|x star_k y|=min(x,y,k-x,k-y)+1.
```

Since `x,y` are positive, `L` is a singleton if and only if one of
`x,y` is `k`.  The simple-current rule then makes its unique output
`k-y` or `k-x`.  As this output is `r`, the exceptional pair is exactly

```text
{x,y}={k,k-r}.
```

In this case canceling the simple current gives the complete profile

```text
V_k star_k V_(k-r) star_k V_r
 =V_r star_k V_r
 =V_0+V_2+...+V_(2min(r,k-r)),
```

proving the second line and its if-and-only-if assertion.  Finally

```text
N=sum_j m_j(A)b_j
```

and substitution of `(P23.11z5zy4)--(P23.11z5zy5)` gives every bound in
`(P23.11z5zy6)`.  QED.

Lemma 23A9S2 does not by itself prove the global width-three inequality.
Its local supplier-side obstruction is exact: possibly repeated active
cuts have plus pair `{k,k-r}`, and their fixed-cut images can intersect
at the affine wall.  Corollaries 23A9U2B--23A9U2F below resolve this
top-edge allocation without summing those images; the remaining global
problem concerns the nonexceptional cuts.

The preceding bounds give an exact active-count floor for a possible
fusion-depth-three raw deficit.

**Corollary 23A9S3 (depth-three small-cut residual).**  In the setting
of Lemma 23A9S2, let `c` be the number of active indexed oriented cuts
and choose the displayed cut with maximal rank `d`.  If `T>N+P_eq`,
then the following necessary conditions hold:

```text
d=1, k notin B:
       c>=8 if k notin A,       c>=5 if k in A;

d=2:
       c>=5 if k notin A,       c>=4 if k in A;

d=2, b_2>=4:
       c>=6 if k notin A,       c>=4 if k in A.     (P23.11z5zy7)
```

Thus below these active-count floors the fusion-depth lemma is proved
with `N` alone.  The simple-current complement `k in B` and the
unextended two-endpoint overlap in `(P23.11z5zy4)` require separate
endpoint analysis even before this comparison.

**Proof.**  Maximality gives `T<=cd`.  Combine this with the successive
lower bounds for `N` in `(P23.11z5zy6)` and use integrality.  Since
`P_eq>=0`, failure of `T<=N+P_eq` implies `cd>N`, producing precisely
the displayed floors.  QED.

The unextended rank-two exception in Lemma 23A9S2 has no hidden interior
parameters.

**Lemma 23A9S2A (unextended rank-two simple-current packet).**  Retain
the notation and hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2.  Suppose `d=2` and that the
two intervals used there have no extension beyond their intersection:

```text
I=J=K,                         |K|=2.
```

Then, after permuting the three plus labels in the complementary block,

```text
B={s,1,k-1,k-s}.                                  (P23.11z5zy7a)
```

In particular the three plus labels in `B` are distinct.  For a fixed
minus orientation, an unextended cut is therefore determined by an
indexed choice of the complementary packet

```text
C_s={1,k-1,k-s}.                                  (P23.11z5zy7b)
```

If two such indexed cuts differ only in the choice of one repeated label
`ell in C_s`, write their active pairs as `{ell,p}`.  The equal-plus
deletion of the two indexed copies of `ell` then has multiplicity at
least two:

```text
m(r,s,P minus {ell,ell})>=2.                       (P23.11z5zy7c)
```

Thus every collision between two unextended packets exposes a specific
nonzero summand of `P_eq`.  This lemma only identifies that allocation;
it does not by itself prove that the total `P_eq` supply pays all
unextended cuts.

**Proof.**  The cardinality of a finite binary fusion interval is

```text
|alpha star_k beta|=min(cap_k(alpha),cap_k(beta)).
```

Since `cap_k(s)>=3` and `|s star_k u|=2`, the plus label `u` has cap two:

```text
u in {1,k-1}.
```

Likewise one of `v,w`, say `v`, lies in `{1,k-1}`.  Put `J_0=V_k` and
write

```text
u=J_0^epsilon 1,              v=J_0^delta 1,
epsilon,delta in {0,1}.
```

The two length-two intervals are

```text
s star_k u=J_0^epsilon(s star_k 1),
v star_k w=J_0^delta(1 star_k w).
```

Their equality forces equality of their two centers, hence

```text
w=J_0^(epsilon+delta)s.
```

If `epsilon=delta`, this says `w=s`, contrary to disjoint sign support.
Therefore `epsilon!=delta`; the two cap-two plus labels are `1,k-1`
and `w=J_0s=k-s`.  This proves `(P23.11z5zy7a)`.  Since
`cap_k(s)>=3`, the label `k-s` is distinct from both `1` and `k-1`.

Now suppose two indexed choices of `(P23.11z5zy7b)` differ at a repeated
label `ell`.  Their active pairs contain respectively the other indexed
copy of `ell` and the same remaining label `p`; activity gives

```text
N_(ell,p)^r=1.
```

The rank-two complementary packet gives, by Frobenius reciprocity,

```text
m_ell(s,C_s minus {ell})=m_0(s,C_s)=2.
```

After deleting the two indexed copies of `ell`, fuse `r,p` through
`ell` and fuse `s,C_s minus {ell}` to the same output.  These two
independent complementary paths prove `(P23.11z5zy7c)`.  QED.

The two endpoint exceptions left by Lemma 23A9S2 therefore have stronger
profiles than its initial skeleton records.

**Corollary 23A9S2B (exact endpoint profiles and active-count floors).**
Retain the hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2, and let `c_act` be the number of
active indexed oriented cuts.

First suppose the selected rank-two cut is unextended, as in Lemma
23A9S2A, and put

```text
h=min(s,k-s)>=2.
```

Then its complementary block has the exact profile

```text
(b_0,b_2,b_4)=(2,4,3+indicator_(h>=3)).             (P23.11z5zy7d)
```

Consequently

```text
N>=13  if A is nonexceptional,
N>=9   if A={r,k,k-r}.                              (P23.11z5zy7e)
```

A raw deficit `T>N+P_eq` in these two branches therefore requires,
respectively,

```text
c_act>=7,                         c_act>=5.          (P23.11z5zy7f)
```

Second suppose the maximal active-cut rank is one and the selected cut
has a complementary block containing the simple current:

```text
B={s,k,u,v}.
```

Then

```text
(b_0,b_2,b_4)>=(1,2,1),                            (P23.11z5zy7g)
```

so

```text
N>=6  if A is nonexceptional,
N>=4  if A={r,k,k-r}.                              (P23.11z5zy7h)
```

A raw deficit in these branches requires respectively

```text
c_act>=7,                         c_act>=5.          (P23.11z5zy7i)
```

These floors sharpen the residual; they do not allocate the common
reservoir among all cuts and hence do not close the global width-three
inequality.

**Proof.**  Put `J_0=V_k`.  In the unextended case Lemma 23A9S2A and
two simultaneous simple-current cancellations give

```text
B=s star_k 1 star_k (J_0 1) star_k (J_0 s)
  =s star_k s star_k 1 star_k 1.
```

Now

```text
s star_k s=V_0+V_2+...+V_(2h),       1 star_k 1=V_0+V_2.
```

The coefficient of `V_0` is two.  Frobenius reciprocity gives

```text
b_2=1+|{0,2,...,2h} intersection (2 star_k 2)|=1+3=4,
b_4=1+|{0,2,...,2h} intersection (2 star_k 4)|
   =3+indicator_(h>=3).
```

This proves `(P23.11z5zy7d)`.  The apparent level-four truncation in the
second line cannot occur, because then `s=k-s`, contrary to the disjoint
occurrence of `k-s` as a plus label.

For a nonexceptional active triple, Lemma 23A9S2 gives
`(m_0,m_2,m_4)(A)>=(1,2,1)`.  Orthogonality across the selected cut
therefore gives

```text
N>=2+2*4+3=13.
```

For the exceptional triple its displayed profile is `(1,1,1)`, giving
`N>=2+4+3=9`.  Since maximality gives `T<=2c_act`, a raw deficit forces
`2c_act>N`, which is exactly `(P23.11z5zy7f)`.

Finally, if `B={s,k,u,v}`, canceling the simple current identifies its
profile with that of the positive invariant triple

```text
{k-s,u,v}.
```

Its singleton exception would require `{u,v}={k,s}`.  This is impossible
because disjoint sign support forbids the plus label `s`.  The
nonexceptional invariant-triple estimate therefore gives
`(P23.11z5zy7g)`.  Dotting it with the nonexceptional and exceptional
profiles `(1,2,1)` and `(1,1,1)` of `A` gives respectively `N>=6` and
`N>=4`.  Here `T<=c_act`, so `T>N+P_eq` forces the two floors in
`(P23.11z5zy7i)`.  QED.

The packet classification also pays all unextended rank-two cuts at
once.

**Corollary 23A9S2B1 (global unextended-packet payment).**  Retain the
hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2, and let `T_unext` be the total demand of all
oriented rank-two cuts whose two complementary intervals are equal to
their intersection.  Then

```text
q!=a:                  T_unext<=8<=N;
q=a:                   T_unext<=N+P_eq.              (P23.11z5zy7i1)
```

Thus the unextended cuts are paid as a complete family.  This statement
uses the common reservoir `N`; it does not license a second use of `N`
for the extended cuts.

**Proof.**  Lemma 23A9S2A says that an unextended cut in the `r`
orientation is an indexed choice of the three-label complementary packet

```text
C_s={1,k-1,k-s},
```

where `s` is the other minus label.  Its three labels are distinct.
Write `n_x` for the multiplicity of a label `x` in the five plus
positions.

Suppose first that `q!=a`.  If unextended cuts occur in both
orientations, their packets have union

```text
C_q union C_a={1,k-1,k-q,k-a}.
```

These four labels are distinct: the fusion-depth hypothesis separates
`k-q,k-a` from `1,k-1`, and `q!=a` separates them from each other.  The
total number of indexed unextended cuts is therefore

```text
n_1 n_(k-1){n_(k-q)+n_(k-a)}<=4,                   (P23.11z5zy7i2)
```

because the four positive multiplicity groups have total at most five.
Indeed, if `t=n_1+n_(k-1)` and
`w=n_(k-q)+n_(k-a)`, then `(t,w)` is either `(2,3)` or `(3,2)` at a
possible maximum, giving respectively at most `3` and `4`.

If only one orientation occurs, the count is

```text
n_1 n_(k-1)n_(k-s)<=4,                              (P23.11z5zy7i3)
```

since three positive integers with sum at most five have product at
most `2*2*1=4`.  Every cut has rank two, so
`T_unext<=8`.  Selecting any one of them in Corollary 23A9S2B gives
`N>=9`, proving the first line of `(P23.11z5zy7i1)`.

Now let `q=a`.  Put

```text
c=n_1 n_(k-1)n_(k-q).
```

There are `c` indexed complementary packets in either one of the two
identical minus orientations, so

```text
T_unext=4c,                       c<=4.              (P23.11z5zy7i4)
```

If `c<=2`, this is at most eight and again `N>=9`.  If `c=3`, the
three packet multiplicities must be a permutation of `(3,1,1)` and
already occupy all five positions.  Every active pair is therefore
nonexceptional, so Corollary 23A9S2B gives

```text
T_unext=12<=13<=N.
```

Finally `c=4` forces the multiplicities `(2,2,1)`.  Again the active
pair is nonexceptional and `N>=13`.  For each of the two repeated packet
labels, two indexed packet choices differ only in the copy of that
label.  Lemma 23A9S2A gives a multiplicity at least two to the
corresponding equal-plus deletion.  The two labels give distinct
summands of `P_eq`, and hence

```text
P_eq>=4,                  T_unext=16<=13+4<=N+P_eq.
```

This exhausts `c=0,1,2,3,4` and proves the corollary.  QED.

The smallest nonexceptional triple profile is itself rigid.

**Lemma 23A9S2B2 (minimal non-top supplier rigidity).**  Retain the
fusion-depth hypothesis of Lemma 23A9S2.  Let

```text
A={r,x,y}
```

be an active nonexceptional triple.  Then

```text
(m_0(A),m_2(A),m_4(A))=(1,2,1)                    (P23.11z5zy7i5)
```

if and only if one of the following holds:

```text
r=2,       {x,y}={1,1} or {k-1,k-1};
r=k-2,     {x,y}={1,k-1}.                         (P23.11z5zy7i6)
```

In particular every label in a minimal-profile active triple has cap at
most three.  Every other nonexceptional active triple has

```text
m_2(A)>=3             or             m_4(A)>=2.   (P23.11z5zy7i7)
```

**Proof.**  Put `I=x star_k y`.  As in Lemma 23A9S2,

```text
m_j(A)=|I intersection (r star_k j)|.
```

The nonexceptional hypothesis makes `I` a step-two interval of length at
least two containing `r`.  Equality `m_2(A)=2` therefore says that
exactly one of `r-2,r+2` belongs to `I`.  For the same adjacent entry not
to contribute to `m_4(A)`, the finite triangle rule forces respectively

```text
r=2                 or                 r=k-2.
```

Indeed `N_(r,r-2)^4=1` for `r>=3`, while
`N_(r,r+2)^4=1` for `r<=k-3`.

If `r=2`, equality in `(P23.11z5zy7i5)` forces
`I={0,2}`.  A binary fusion interval is `{0,2}` exactly when its two
labels are equal and have cap two, giving `{1,1}` or
`{k-1,k-1}`.  If `r=k-2`, it similarly forces
`I={k-2,k}`.  Containment of `k` makes the two labels simple-current
complements, while interval length two makes one of them have cap two;
hence their multiset is `{1,k-1}`.  Direct substitution proves the
converse in all three cases.  QED.

The remaining non-top cuts admit a useful five-vertex density sieve.
It separates a genuinely one-color residual from the mixed-color
configuration which carries the first half of a positive two-plus
allocation.

**Lemma 23A9S2C (non-top colored-graph density sieve).**  Retain the
hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2, and discard the exceptional active pairs

```text
{k,k-r}
```

for each minus orientation `r`; Corollaries 23A9U2B--23A9U2F below pay
every repeated family of that form.  On the five indexed plus positions
put a graph `G_r` of color `r`, joining `i,j` precisely when

```text
m(r,p_i,p_j)=1,             m(s,P minus {p_i,p_j})>0,             (P23.11z5zy7j)
```

where `s` is the other minus label.  Give this edge the second
multiplicity in `(P23.11z5zy7j)` as its weight.  Let `c` be the total
number of colored edges and `h` the number having weight two.  If the
maximal weight is at most two, then the remaining non-top demand is

```text
T_nt=c+h.                                             (P23.11z5zy7k)
```

The simple current has the following exact effect.

```text
P contains k at least twice:       c=0;
P contains k exactly once:         its indexed vertex is isolated
                                   in both colored graphs, and
                                   every remaining edge has
                                   weight one.                      (P23.11z5zy7l)
```

If `T_nt>N`, the following necessary density conditions hold:

```text
maximal weight one:
   k notin P:                       c>=8;
   k occurs once:                   c>=7;

maximal weight two:
   some weight-two cut unextended:  c+h>=14, hence c>=7;
   every weight-two cut extended:   c+h>=12, hence c>=6.            (P23.11z5zy7m)
```

Here ``extended'' has the meaning of Lemma 23A9S2: at least one of the
two complementary fusion intervals extends beyond their two-point
intersection.

If both colors occur and `c>=6`, there is a mixed wedge: after relabeling
positions,

```text
{i,j} in G_q,                  {i,l} in G_a,          j!=l.          (P23.11z5zy7n)
```

Write the other two positions as `u,v`.  This wedge has a canonical
candidate positive cut.  Namely

```text
m(q,a,p_j,p_l)>=1,                                      (P23.11z5zy7o)
```

and if

```text
m(p_i,p_u,p_v)>0,                                       (P23.11z5zy7p)
```

then the indexed pair `{j,l}` contributes at least one to `U_2`.
Consequently, in a residual with no positive `U_2` supplier, every
mixed wedge satisfies the explicit central-channel exclusion

```text
m(p_i,p_u,p_v)=0.                                       (P23.11z5zy7q)
```

There is an analogous one-color test.  If `G_q` contains a triangle on
positions `i,j,l`, and `u,v` are the other two positions, then

```text
m(q,a,p_i)>0,             m(q,p_u,p_v)>0              (P23.11z5zy7q1)
```

implies that the indexed singleton `i` contributes at least one to
`U_1`.  Thus, if the triangle has no `U_1` supplier and
`m(q,p_u,p_v)>0`, all three of its vertices obey

```text
m(q,a,p_i)=m(q,a,p_j)=m(q,a,p_l)=0.                  (P23.11z5zy7q2)
```

If instead a one-color six-edge graph is the triangle-free extremal
`K_(2,3)`, every vertex `i` in its three-vertex part has an invariant
four-plus complement: the remaining `K_(2,2)` contains a perfect
matching of two `q`-colored edges.  Hence

```text
m(q,a,p_i)>0                                        (P23.11z5zy7q3)
```

exposes the singleton-`i` summand of `U_1`.  With no such supplier, all
three labels in that part lie outside `q star_k a`.

In particular, if `k` occurs once, every raw deficit has a mixed wedge
and hence either exposes an indexed `U_2` term or obeys
`(P23.11z5zy7q)`.  If `k` is absent and only one color occurs, the
density alternatives in `(P23.11z5zy7m)` reduce to

```text
weight one:                       a graph with at least eight edges;
some unextended weight two:       a graph with at least seven edges;
all weight-two cuts extended:     a graph with at least six edges. (P23.11z5zy7s)
```

The first two graphs contain a triangle.  In the last line either there
is a triangle, or equality holds and the graph is `K_(2,3)`.

**Proof.**  A non-top active triple has multiplicity one, while its
complementary rank is one or two.  Summing its edge weights proves
`(P23.11z5zy7k)`.

No non-top active pair can contain `k`: activity would force its other
label to be `k-r`, which is precisely the discarded exceptional pair.
If two indexed copies of `k` occur, a pair avoiding both has a complement
of the form

```text
{s,k,k,x}.
```

The two simple currents cancel, so its invariant multiplicity is
`m(s,x)=0` by disjoint sign support.  A pair using a copy of `k` is
discarded or inactive.  If there is exactly one copy of `k`, every
non-top pair avoids it and its complementary rank has the form

```text
m(s,k,u,v)=m(k-s,u,v)<=1.
```

This proves all of `(P23.11z5zy7l)`.

When all weights are one, `(P23.11z5zy7k)` says `T_nt=c`.  If `k` is
absent, Lemma 23A9S2 gives `N>=7`; if it occurs once, Corollary
23A9S2B gives `N>=6`.  Integrality proves the first two lines of
`(P23.11z5zy7m)`.  If some weight-two cut is unextended, choose it as
the selected cut in Corollary 23A9S2B to obtain `N>=13`.  Otherwise
Lemma 23A9S2 gives `N>=11`.  Since `T_nt=c+h`, the last two lines
follow.

It remains to prove the graph and supplier assertions.  Two simple
colored graphs on five vertices with both colors nonempty and no mixed
wedge have at most five colored edges.  Indeed, if an edge has both
colors, neither endpoint can meet any other edge; deleting its two
vertices leaves at most three edges.  If there is no doubly colored
edge, the non-isolated vertex sets of the two colors are disjoint, and
the largest nontrivial partition `3+2` gives only

```text
binom(3,2)+binom(2,2)=4
```

edges.  Thus `c>=6` gives `(P23.11z5zy7n)`.

Activity and Frobenius reciprocity along that wedge give

```text
N_(q,p_j)^(p_i)=1,                  N_(a,p_l)^(p_i)=1.
```

Pairing through the common channel `p_i` proves
`(P23.11z5zy7o)`.  If `(P23.11z5zy7p)` also holds, the same indexed
channel contributes to the two factors

```text
m(q,a,p_j,p_l) m(p_i,p_u,p_v)
```

of the `{j,l}` summand of `U_2`.  This proves the supplier claim and
its contrapositive `(P23.11z5zy7q)`.

For the one-color assertion, the triangle edge `{j,l}` fuses through
`q`.  Under `(P23.11z5zy7q1)`, the remaining pair `{u,v}` also fuses
through `q`, so

```text
m(p_j,p_l,p_u,p_v)>=1.
```

Together with the first factor `m(q,a,p_i)>0`, this is exactly the
singleton-`i` summand of `U_1`.  Applying this argument at each vertex
of the triangle gives `(P23.11z5zy7q2)`.

For `K_(2,3)`, delete a vertex in the three-vertex part.  The remaining
four vertices contain two disjoint graph edges, and both plus pairs
fuse to `q`.  Fusing the resulting two copies of `q` to the unit proves
that four-plus multiplicity is positive.  Equation `(P23.11z5zy7q3)`
then supplies the other factor in the corresponding `U_1` summand.

When `k` occurs once, `(P23.11z5zy7l)` leaves four vertices and only
weight-one edges.  A raw deficit gives `c>=7`, while one color has at
most six edges.  Both colors therefore occur, so the mixed-wedge result
applies.  Finally a graph on five vertices with at least seven edges
contains a triangle by Mantel's bound.  A six-edge graph either contains
a triangle or is the extremal triangle-free graph `K_(2,3)`.  This
proves `(P23.11z5zy7s)`.  QED.

The lone-simple-current residual has an exact matching-channel
reduction.  It closes all generic minus pairs and verifies the proposed
opposite-pair supplier without an enumeration.

**Lemma 23A9S2D (lone-`J` matching reduction).**  Retain the non-top
setting of Lemma 23A9S2C and suppose

```text
P={J,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4},                    J=V_k.
```

For an edge `e={i,j}` of the four `x`-vertices, let `bar(e)` be its
opposite edge and put

```text
F_e=x_i star_k x_j,             Jr=k-r.
```

Then the colored activity conditions are exactly

```text
e in G_q  iff  q in F_e  and  Ja in F_(bar(e)),
e in G_a  iff  a in F_e  and  Jq in F_(bar(e)).      (P23.11z5zy7s1)
```

Let `c` count colored edges, as in Lemma 23A9S2C.

1.  If

```text
q!=a,                         q!=Ja,                 (P23.11z5zy7s2)
```

then

```text
c>=7  ==>  T_nt=c<=N.                               (P23.11z5zy7s3)
```

2.  If two of the four labels are simple-current complements, say

```text
x_2=Jx_1,
```

then every active colored edge exposes the indexed `U_2` supplier

```text
m(q,a,x_3,x_4)m(J,x_1,x_2)>=1,                     (P23.11z5zy7s4)
```

after relabeling the other two vertices as `3,4`.

Consequently a lone-`J` raw deficit with no positive `U_2` supplier is
confined to the exact residual

```text
a in {q,Jq},             x_j!=Jx_i for all i!=j.    (P23.11z5zy7s5)
```

The lemma makes no claim that the two collision columns in
`(P23.11z5zy7s5)` are already paid.

**Proof.**  A non-top active edge avoids the isolated `J` vertex.
Canceling `J` in its four-label complement gives

```text
m(a,J,x_u,x_v)=m(Ja,x_u,x_v),
```

which proves the first line of `(P23.11z5zy7s1)`; the second is the
same calculation with the minus orientations exchanged.  Lemma 23A9S2C
also shows that all these edges have weight one, so `T_nt=c`.

Fix one of the three perfect matchings `e|bar(e)` of the four vertices.
Canceling the external simple current and pairing first across this
matching gives the exact expansion

```text
N=m(q,Ja,x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4)
 =sum_(u in F_e)sum_(v in F_(bar(e)))m(q,Ja,u,v).
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7s6)
```

The four possible colored edges in this matching select respectively
the four ordered cells

```text
(q,Ja),                (Ja,q),                (a,Jq),                (Jq,a).
                                                               (P23.11z5zy7s7)
```

Every selected cell contributes exactly

```text
w=|q star_k a|>=3,                                (P23.11z5zy7s8)
```

because

```text
q star_k Ja=J(q star_k a)=a star_k Jq.
```

Under `(P23.11z5zy7s2)` the four ordered cells in
`(P23.11z5zy7s7)` are distinct.  If `r_M` is the number of colored
edges in this matching, `(P23.11z5zy7s6)` therefore gives

```text
N>=wr_M.
```

The three perfect matchings partition the colored edges.  Hence one has
`r_M>=ceil(c/3)`, and for `7<=c<=12`,

```text
N>=3ceil(c/3)>=c=T_nt.
```

This proves `(P23.11z5zy7s3)`.

Now suppose `x_2=Jx_1`.  The matching
`{1,2}|{3,4}` has no active colored edge: the first fusion interval is
the singleton `{J}`, while activity on the opposite edge would require
`Ja=J` or `Jq=J`, forcing a trivial minus label.  Thus every active edge
crosses this matching.  For example, a `q`-colored edge `{1,3}` gives

```text
q in x_1 star_k x_3,
Ja in x_2 star_k x_4=J(x_1 star_k x_4),
```

and hence `a in x_1 star_k x_4`.  Pairing both relations through the
common channel `x_1` proves

```text
m(q,a,x_3,x_4)>=1.
```

The other three crossing edges, and the other color, give the same
conclusion after using the common channel `x_1` or `x_2`.  Finally

```text
m(J,x_1,Jx_1)=1,
```

so the indexed pair `{x_3,x_4}` in the two-plus sum defining `U_2`
has the positive product `(P23.11z5zy7s4)`.  This proves the supplier
claim.  Combining it with the generic closure proves the residual
statement `(P23.11z5zy7s5)`.  QED.

The first collision-column margin is already cap-localized.

**Lemma 23A9S2D1 (lone-`J` eight-edge plus-cap localization).**  Retain the
setting of Lemma 23A9S2D, suppose

```text
c=T_nt=8,
```

and assume `T_nt>N+P_eq`.  Then all four labels `x_i` have cap at most
three.

**Proof.**  Suppose one label, say `z=x_1`, has cap at least four.
It has colored degree at least two, since otherwise its one edge and the
at most six colored edges on the other three vertices would give
`c<=7`.

Choose an incident edge of color `r`, and write `s` for the other minus
label.  Its active triple `A` is nonminimal by Lemma 23A9S2B2.  Its
four-label complement contains `J`; canceling the simple current gives
the positive invariant triple

```text
C={Js,x_u,x_v}
```

on the two vertices outside the edge.  Both `A` and `C` have profile at
least `(1,2,1)`.  If `C` were also nonminimal, Lemma 23A9S2B2 and
orthogonality would give `N>=8`.  The strict deficit with `T_nt=8`
therefore forces `C` to be minimal.  Consequently

```text
s in {2,k-2},                    x_u,x_v in {1,k-1}. (P23.11z5zy7s9)
```

Apply this to two distinct edges at `z`.  All three other `x`-labels
have cap two.  Both minus labels have cap three as well.  Indeed, if
only one minus label had cap three, all edges at `z` would have the
other color, while edges avoiding `z` could only have the cap-three
color.  The two color classes would then contain at most `3+3=6`
edges.

Thus the minus labels lie in `{2,k-2}`.  Fusing `z` with a label of cap
two to one of these two outputs, and using `cap_k(z)>=4`, forces

```text
z in {3,k-3}.                                      (P23.11z5zy7s10)
```

Assume first `k>=7`.  Write the four non-top plus labels as
`J^epsilon ell`, with low labels `ell=3` for `z` and `ell=1` for the
other three.  A pair supports color two exactly when its two exponents
agree, and color `k-2` exactly when they differ.  If the minus labels
are distinct, each unordered pair supports at most one color, so
`c<=binom(4,2)=6`.

If the minus labels coincide, the two orientations count each active
unordered pair twice.  Let `n_0+n_1=4` be the two exponent counts.
For color two the eligible-pair count is

```text
binom(n_0,2)+binom(n_1,2),
```

and for color `k-2` it is `n_0n_1`.  The complement has the same
simple-current parity for every eligible pair and is invariant only
when the total exponent sum is odd.  In that parity the eligible count
is at most three, again giving `c<=6`.

Finally let `k=6`, so `z=3` is fixed by `J`.  If `t` of the other three
labels are one and the rest five, all eligible pairs among those three
have active complement.  A pair `{3,u}` has active complement in color
two exactly when the other two labels are opposite, and in color four
exactly when they are equal.  For each `t=0,1,2,3`, these contributions
give three active unordered pairs for equal minus labels, hence six
colored edges after doubling the orientation.  For distinct minus
labels there are three colored edges among the cap-two vertices, while
the equal/opposite alternatives at `3` contribute three more.  Thus
again `c<=6`.

Every case contradicts `c=8`.  Hence no `x_i` has cap at least four.
QED.

**Corollary 23A9S2D2 (exact remaining lone-`J` depth columns).**  Under
the hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2D1, a raw deficit with a minus label of
cap at least four must satisfy

```text
x_i in {1,2,k-2,k-1}                 for every i,
a in {q,k-q},
q,a in {3,4,k-4,k-3}.                              (P23.11z5zy7s11)
```

Thus the only minus depths left by the eight-edge collision column are
four and five.

**Proof.**  Lemma 23A9S2D1 gives the first line.  Part 1 of Lemma
23A9S2D shows that a raw deficit must have `a=q` or `a=Jq`.
Every active pair of labels from `{1,2,J2,J1}` is, after removing its
common simple-current parity, one of

```text
1 star_k 1={0,2},       1 star_k 2={1,3},
2 star_k 2={0,2,4}.
```

Hence any minus label carried by an active edge has cap at most five.
The two minus labels have equal cap when they are equal or
simple-current complements.  Restricting to cap at least four gives
exactly the four displayed labels.  QED.

The finite endpoint columns left by Corollary 23A9S2D2 are already
raw-positive.

**Lemma 23A9S2D3 (lone-`J` collision endpoint closure).**  Retain the
hypotheses of Lemma 23A9S2D1.  Then

```text
T_nt<=N+P_eq.                                      (P23.11z5zy7s12)
```

Thus the two collision columns left open in Lemma 23A9S2D do not require
any additional positive-cut reservoir.

**Proof.**  Lemma 23A9S2D1 gives

