## Return to the full continuous cone through six factors

All six-factor actual-atom patterns now have proved suppliers. This
allows the original positive Fourier expansion and uniform approximation
to return an unrestricted statement about the full continuous central
cone at these lengths. The arbitrary-length objective remains unchanged.

**Independent double-check before the statement.** Listed all eleven
integer partitions of six and matched each to its whole-input theorem.
Checked trivial atoms and opposite-sign repeats before using a pattern
classification. Checked that paired atoms are included in every row,
and that the Fourier expansion is nonnegative in actual real atoms,
not a demand on complex constituent tuples. Finally recomputed the
uniform product difference bound on normalized product Haar measure.

**Theorem 48A (the full continuous central positive-definite cone at
lengths at most six).** For every compact connected target group `G`
with simple Lie algebra, normalized Haar measure `mu`, every
`0<=n<=6`, every list of real continuous central matrix-positive-definite
functions `f_1,...,f_n`, and all signs `epsilon_i in {+1,-1}`,

```text
integral_(G x G) product_(i=1)^n
   [f_i(g)+epsilon_i f_i(h)] dmu(g)dmu(h) >= 0.             (P48.1)
```

This includes arbitrary functions in the full cone, with no restriction
on their Fourier supports, their invariant multiplicities, or the
presence of non-self-dual irreducibles.

**Proof.**

1. Lengths at most five, including the empty tuple, are supplied
   by Theorem 41B. At length six, first take actual real atoms.
   A trivial minus factor kills the integral; a trivial plus
   factor contributes two and reduces the length. An
   opposite-sign repeat expands by `(P41.2)` as a finite
   nonnegative sum of at-most-five-factor inputs. Thus only
   six nontrivial atoms with disjoint sign supports require
   the pattern table.
2. Classify them by multiplicities of their actual dual-orbit
   types. The following list exhausts the partitions of six:

   ```text
   multiplicity pattern       whole-input supplier
   (1,1,1,1,1,1)              Theorem 42B
   (2,1,1,1,1)                Theorem 42B
   (2,2,1,1)                  Theorem 42B
   (3,1,1,1)                  Theorem 42B
   (2,2,2)                    Theorem 43D
   (3,2,1)                    Theorem 44D
   (4,1,1)                    Theorem 45D
   (3,3)                      Theorem 46C
   (5,1)                      Theorem 47C
   (4,2)                      Corollary 44E
   (6)                        Corollary 44E.              (P48.2)
   ```

   Every row supplies all target groups and every sign pattern
   for its entire actual tuple. Hence all six-factor atomic
   integrals are nonnegative.
3. For finite positive actual-atom expansions of each function,
   multilinearity expresses the integral as a finite sum of
   the proved atomic integrals with nonnegative coefficients.
   Lemma 28A gives, for each continuous full-cone function,
   finite nonnegative actual-atom expansions `p_i^(k)` converging
   uniformly to `f_i`. This is the actual positive real Fourier
   expansion; complex constituent functions are not required
   to satisfy the inequality separately.
4. Choose `M>=1` bounding all the functions and approximants
   in sup norm, and set `delta_i^(k)=||f_i-p_i^(k)||_infinity`.
   For fixed `g,h`, telescoping the product gives

   ```text
   |product_i [f_i(g)+epsilon_i f_i(h)]
     -product_i [p_i^(k)(g)+epsilon_i p_i^(k)(h)]|
       <=2(2M)^(n-1) sum_i delta_i^(k).                  (P48.3)
   ```

   For `n=6` this tends to zero uniformly. Normalized product
   Haar measure has mass one, so the same bound holds for
   the integral difference. The nonnegative approximating
   integrals converge to `(P48.1)`, proving the theorem.
   QED.

**Final independent check and exact original-target return.** Recounted
the eleven partitions in `(P48.2)`, including the two even-multiplicity
patterns that close by the original pointwise integrand. Inspected the
original RC source and target in each nontrivial supplier: sparse
relations use Theorem 34, injective merges use `Rel=0`, and determinant
or cup constructions use actual positive cut spaces with their outputs
packed inside one copy of each target. In the paired five-and-one
case, checked the orthogonal cup orientations and first-block isotypic
channels, including the linear unitary on agreeing-label source blocks.
Rechecked all trivial and opposite-sign reductions against the proved
shorter-length input.
Then replayed the actual uniform nonnegative Fourier approximation
into the original double integral, with the explicit bound `(P48.3)`.
Thus the full continuous-cone statement `(P48.1)` is proved for all
lengths through six, not merely for atoms or finite Fourier support.

The original objective quantifies over arbitrary finite lengths. Its
remaining input starts at length seven and still includes all groups,
all real continuous central positive-definite functions, and all sign
patterns. The source-to-target cup matching and the dual-volume
allocations above are established structural tools, but no theorem
supplies the entire arbitrary-length relation space. Therefore the
full-cone goal remains active and is not marked complete.

## Partial cup matching and a seven-factor whole-input supplier

The universal cup isometry can pay selected negative cuts while an
injective merge handles the unpaid cuts. Projection of the *whole*
relation space onto the paid source coordinates is then injective,
including relations coupling the two source families. This extends the
distinct-target supplier without requiring a match for every negative
cut. A seven-factor input supplies a concrete use: for `A^6,B`, fifteen
positive pair cuts pay fifteen negative cuts, and five balanced cuts
have an injective merge. The dimension-three boundary is handled by
an exact eight-cut factor-swap Gram calculation.

**Independent double-check before the statements.** Checked the kernel
of source-coordinate projection on the full `Rel`, rather than on
relations internal to the paid family. Checked Hall's condition for
every subset of fifteen chosen three-subsets of six positions. For
the eight-cut Gram, computed all single, double, and triple swap
compressions by reduced cross operators. Checked the standard and
trivial `S_3` multiplicity spaces separately, then each nonuniform
paired constituent word. Checked the small dimensions two and four
against their actual triple invariant spaces. Finally replayed all
seven-factor signs and the continuous seventh-function limit.

**Lemma 49A (partial matching pays the entire coupled relation space).**
Partition an atomic negative source into cut indices `I,J`. Suppose
`I` has the distinct positive pair assignment of Theorem 47B, and
the merge `F_J` is injective on the entire remaining source `O_J`.
Let `T_I:O_I -> E_prop` be the supplied whole-source isometry. Then

```text
L=T_I P_I|_Rel:Rel -> E_prop                              (P49.1)
```

is injective and supplies `(P28.2)` for the whole original input.
If `||F_J t||^2>=c||t||^2`, with `c>0`, its quantitative bound is

```text
||Lr||^2 >= [c/(c+|I|)] ||r||^2,  r in Rel.              (P49.2)
```

**Proof.**

1. If `r in Rel` and `P_I r=0`, then `r` lies in `O_J`
   and satisfies `F_J r=F r=0`. Injectivity of `F_J` gives
   `r=0`. Thus coordinate projection is injective on the
   entire `Rel`, irrespective of coupled relations between
   the two families. Composing it with `T_I` proves `(P49.1)`.
2. For the norm bound use `F_J r_J=-F_I r_I` and the
   elementary merge estimate `||F_I t||^2<=|I| ||t||^2`.
   Hence `||r_J||^2<=|I| ||r_I||^2/c`. The direct-source
   norm gives `||r||^2<= (1+|I|/c)||r_I||^2`, whereas
   `||Lr||=||r_I||`. This proves `(P49.2)`. Include the
   range in `H_free direct_sum E_prop`; Proposition 28
   consumes the injection on the original caller. QED.

For the next input label six distinguished positions by
`Aset={1,2,3,4,5,6}`, with a seventh position of distinct type `B`.
The negative triple cuts of the six-minus input have sides
`S` and `(Aset\S) union {B}`, where `|S|=3`. There are twenty.
Their positive same-type pair targets are the fifteen pairs of `Aset`.

**Lemma 49B (any fifteen triple sources admit distinct pair targets).**
Any family `I` of at most fifteen three-subsets `S` of `Aset` has
an injective assignment to pairs crossing `S`: one endpoint in `S`,
one outside it.

**Proof.** Form the finite bipartite eligibility graph and check Hall's
condition. For a nonempty `X subset I`, if its neighbor set contains
all fifteen pairs, then `|N(X)|=15>=|X|`. Otherwise some pair `{i,j}`
is never separated by any `S in X`. There are exactly

```text
binom(4,1)+binom(4,3)=8
```

three-subsets having either both or neither of these endpoints.
Thus `|X|<=8`. Any one three-subset has `3 times 3=9` crossing
pairs, so `|N(X)|>=9>|X|`. The empty subset also satisfies Hall.
An ordinary augmenting-path matching therefore supplies the assignment
on all of `I`. It is an actual assignment of cut indices, independent
of representation dimensions. QED.

Fix the three position pairs `(1,2),(3,4),(5,6)`. Let `C8` be the
eight triple cuts with exactly one distinguished position from each
pair on their side excluding `B`. Choose any five as `J`.

**Lemma 49C (five unpaid balanced cuts are uniformly independent).**
For every nontrivial actual atom `A`, every distinct nontrivial actual
atom `B`, and every target group, the merge of these five full actual
cut spaces satisfies

```text
||F_J t||^2 >=(1/6) ||t||^2.                             (P49.3)
```

In particular it is injective. The bound includes paired atoms and
all invariant multiplicities of the seventh factor.

**Proof.**

1. Let `d` be the dimension of an irreducible constituent of
   `A`; paired atoms have two dual constituents of this same
   dimension. For two different triple cuts, intersection of
   their three-subsets has size zero, one, or two. If zero,
   a refinement cell is empty and the opposite singleton is
   `B`, so their cut spaces are orthogonal by Lemma 29A.
   If one or two, a refinement cell is a singleton of type
   `A`; the common intersection is zero by Lemma 27A, and
   any shared irreducible label has dimension `d`. Thus
   every nonzero shared angle is at most `1/d`.
2. For `d>=5`, every five-cut merge consequently obeys

   ```text
   ||F_J t||^2 >=(1-4/d)||t||^2 >=(1/5)||t||^2.
   ```

   It remains to check dimensions two, three, and four.
   For `d=2`, Lemma 43A gives the `su(2)` defining module,
   whose triple has no invariant. Every source space is zero.
3. For `d=4`, again `(A^tensor3)^G=0`. Here is the small
   representation check, using the classified root systems
   and Weyl product of Etingof, [Lie Groups and Lie Algebras](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-755-lie-groups-and-lie-algebras-ii-spring-2024/mit18_755_s24_lec_full.pdf),
   Theorem 23.7 and Proposition 26.8. The differential embeds
   the simple Lie algebra in `su(4)`, with rank at most three
   and dimension at most fifteen. Only `A_1,A_2,B_2,G_2,A_3`
   occur at that bound. Type `A_2` has no dimension-four
   irreducible by Lemma 43A's dimension formula. Type `G_2`
   has dimension fourteen and cannot be a codimension-one
   subalgebra of compact simple `su(4)`: its orthogonal
   one-dimensional complement would be invariant and trivial,
   making it an ideal of `su(4)`. For `A_1`, the module is
   `V_3`, and the central element minus identity acts as minus
   identity, excluding triple invariants.

   For `B_2=C_2`, take positive roots `e_1-e_2,e_1+e_2,
   2e_1,2e_2`, fundamental weights `e_1,e_1+e_2`, and
   `rho=2e_1+e_2`. The Weyl product gives

   ```text
   dim V_(a,b)=(a+1)(b+1)(a+b+2)(a+2b+3)/6.
   ```

   Its only dimension-four label is `(1,0)`, the defining
   symplectic module, and its central minus identity again
   excludes triple invariants. These two modules are self-dual.
   For `A_3`, the differential image is all of `su(4)` on
   its four-dimensional defining space. The module is defining
   or dual, and its actual atom is their pair. The central
   charges of its triple words are `3,1,-1,-3`, none zero
   modulo four, so the actual triple invariant space vanishes.
   Invariants on any allowed central quotient equal those of
   the differential. This proves the claim for all `d=4`.
4. For `d=3`, Lemma 43A gives a self-dual irreducible with
   its unit determinant as its entire triple invariant space,
   or the defining `su(3)` module paired with its dual.
   In the latter case center charges exclude mixed triple
   words, and each pure triple invariant is its unit volume.
   First fix a uniform six-position constituent word `a^6`.
   In a reference balanced cut write

   ```text
   H_0=C epsilon tensor Q,
   Q=(a^tensor3 tensor B)^G.
   ```

   Let `S_1,S_2,S_3` swap the two positions in each fixed
   pair. They are commuting involutions, and their eight
   images of `H_0` are exactly this word's balanced cut
   spaces. On `Q`, let `P^-_(ij)` project to the minus
   parity of swapping its corresponding `a` factors.
5. The irreducible reduced cross operator of the unit volume
   on one factor is `Id/3`. On two factors it is
   `P_(wedge^2 a)/3`, because that exterior square has
   dimension three. Therefore the reference compressions are

   ```text
   P_0 S_i P_0=Id_Q/3,
   P_0 S_i S_j P_0=P^-_(ij)/3,
   P_0 S_1 S_2 S_3 P_0=0.                               (P49.4)
   ```

   The double-swap identity traces the two-factor reduced
   cross operator of `q` against the stated exterior-square
   projector, which is exactly its minus-parity matrix element.
   For the triple swap, projecting the three `a` factors of
   `q` onto the invariant volume leaves an invariant in `B`;
   `B^G=0`, giving the zero compression.
6. Fourier decomposition of the eight source copies uses
   characters `eta in {+1,-1}^3`. Its normalized source
   component at `g` is `eta(g) g z/sqrt(8)`, and its merge
   is `sqrt(8) Pi_eta z`, where
   `Pi_eta=(1/8) product_i (Id+eta_i S_i)`. Expanding this
   projector with `(P49.4)` gives the exact Gram on `Q`

   ```text
   G_eta=Id+(eta_1+eta_2+eta_3)Id/3
            +(1/3)sum_(i<j) eta_i eta_j P^-_(ij).         (P49.5)
   ```

   Different characters have orthogonal source and output
   spaces. This is an exact factor-permutation computation,
   without commuting the cut projections.
7. The internal `S_3` action on `Q` has no alternating part:
   it would be `(wedge^3 a tensor B)^G=B^G=0`.
   On its trivial part every `P^-` is zero, and the character
   coefficients in `(P49.5)` are `2,4/3,2/3,0` for zero,
   one, two, three minus character signs, respectively. The
   zero space consists exactly of the all-minus Fourier
   character tensored with this trivial part. Every such
   source vector has equal component norms on all eight cuts.
   A vector supported on five cuts has squared projection
   onto that zero space at most `5/8` of its squared norm.
   Thus its merge squared norm is at least
   `(2/3)(1-5/8)||t||^2=(1/4)||t||^2` in this part.
8. On a standard `S_3` component, its three transpositions
   sum to zero, so `sum_(i<j) P^-_(ij)=(3/2)Id`.
   In `(P49.5)` the all-plus and all-minus characters give
   `5Id/2` and `Id/2`. A character with one minus gives
   `5Id/6+(2/3)P^-` for the pair of plus indices. A
   character with two minuses gives `Id/6+(2/3)P^-` for
   the pair of minus indices. Every coefficient is therefore
   at least `Id/6`, including all multiplicity copies. The
   same bound holds on any five-source subspace.
9. It remains to check nonuniform words for a paired `A`.
   A balanced volume must select one label `a` in all three
   fixed position pairs. If two homogeneous pairs have opposite
   labels, there is no such source. Otherwise let `h` be
   the number of homogeneous pairs of label `a`, the other
   pairs being heterogeneous. Nonuniform words with `h>=1`
   have only that volume label, and `h<=2`. Their possible
   sources are exactly the `2^h` choices within homogeneous
   pairs. For `h=1`, the single-swap coefficient gives Gram
   `Id +/- Id/3`, with bound `2/3`.
10. For `h=2`, the same volume partial traces give two-character
    Gram

    ```text
    Id+(eta_1+eta_2)Id/3+eta_1 eta_2 P^-/3,
    ```

    where `P^-` is the minus projection on the two equal
    `a` factors in the second block. For equal plus signs
    the bound is `5/3`, for unequal signs `2/3`, and for
    equal minus signs `1/3`. If `h=0`, all three pairs
    are heterogeneous. There are at most two volume choices,
    one for each label; their triples are complementary
    subsets of the six positions. Their cut spaces are
    orthogonal by step 1, giving bound one. These account
    for every nonuniform word and all its multiplicities.
11. Word projections preserve the actual cut spaces, and their
    outputs are orthogonal. The bounds in steps 7--10 combine
    to `1/6` on the five chosen full cut copies. With
    steps 1--3 this proves `(P49.3)` for every actual atom.
    QED.

**Theorem 49D (six copies of one atom and an arbitrary seventh atom).**
For every target group, every two distinct nontrivial actual atom
types `A,B`, and every sign pattern, Q3 holds for `A,A,A,A,A,A,B`.
In the six-minus disjoint-support case, there is an explicit map on
the entire original relation space

```text
L:Rel -> E_prop,   ||Lr||^2 >=||r||^2/91.                (P49.6)
```

**Proof.**

1. Opposite-sign occurrences of `A` expand by `(P41.2)` into
   nonnegative sums of at-most-six-factor inputs, supplied
   by Theorem 48A. With disjoint supports the six copies
   have a common sign. If `B` is minus, the total minus
   parity is one or seven and gives zero. If all signs
   are plus, all cut coefficients are nonnegative. Only
   `A` minus six times and `B` plus needs a new source map.
2. In this case all singleton spaces vanish. A negative pair
   contains `A,B` of different actual types, so its space
   vanishes. Among the three-element sides, only the twenty
   subsets of three `A` positions are negative; two `A`
   positions and `B` have even minus parity. These twenty
   are therefore the entire nonzero negative family.
3. Choose any five balanced cuts as `J`, and let `I` be
   the other fifteen. Lemma 49C gives injective merge on
   all of `O_J`, with `c=1/6`. Lemma 49B assigns `I`
   injectively to the fifteen actual `A` pair cuts crossing
   their respective sources. These targets are proper and
   positive, since each contains two minus positions.
4. Theorem 47B supplies the whole-source isometry on `O_I`.
   Lemma 49A applies to the full coupled `Rel` and gives
   `L=T_I P_I`, using one actual copy of each assigned
   positive target. Equation `(P49.2)` with `|I|=15`
   and `c=1/6` gives `1/91`, exactly `(P49.6)`.
   Proposition 28 consumes this injection for the entire
   original seven-factor input. Together with step 1 it
   proves every sign pattern. QED.

**Corollary 49E (an arbitrary continuous seventh function).** Theorem
49D extends to six nonnegative multiples of one actual atom character
`R_A` and an arbitrary real continuous central positive-definite
seventh function, with all seven signs. There is no Fourier-support
restriction on that function.

**Proof.** Zero scalar multiples kill the product; other multiples
contribute their nonnegative scalar product. In a finite nonnegative
actual-atom expansion of the seventh function, distinct nontrivial
types use Theorem 49D. A trivial atom reduces to Theorem 48A or kills
a minus factor. The same type `A` gives seven copies of one type:
opposite signs reduce to six factors, all plus has nonnegative cut
coefficients, and all minus has odd parity. These supply every term.
Apply Lemma 28A's uniform positive approximation to the seventh
function. Since `|R_A|<=dim A`, its integral difference is at most
`2(2 dim A)^6` times the uniform approximation error. Passing to the
limit proves the claim. QED.

**Final independent check and original-consumer return.** Checked
that the partial projection kernel is exactly the unpaid merge kernel
when restricted to the full `Rel`; coupled relations have not been
discarded. Recomputed Hall's count eight and each triple's nine crossing
pairs. Checked the small-dimensional exclusions by the actual image
Lie algebra and its center, including the codimension-one argument
for `G_2`. Independently computed all eight Fourier Gram coefficients
from the volume's one-factor and two-factor density operators and
the zero triple compression. Rechecked the five-supported projection
bound `5/8`, the standard-component lower bound `1/6`, and every
heterogeneous-pair case. Finally replayed the twenty actual negative
cuts, their fifteen actual pair targets, and the same original `Rel`
into Proposition 28; the lower-bound denominator is `1+6 times 15=91`.
The continuous seventh-function passage uses the actual positive real
Fourier expansion and its stated uniform bound. This supplies whole
seven-factor inputs beyond Theorem 48A.

Arbitrary seven-factor inputs and arbitrary longer tuples remain in
the original full-cone objective. Partial matching is now supplied
with an exact coupled-relation map and an actual whole-input use.
No assertion has been made that every remaining family has an
injective unpaid merge or a sufficient distinct target assignment.
The full-cone goal remains active.


## Dual-channel agreement transport and a full-scope detector test

The selected demand is still the unrestricted actual relation injection
`(P28.2)`. The next construction puts both kinds of shared channel into
one actual positive agreement target. It includes non-self-dual
intermediate labels, and does not assume that the atom constituents
agree across the two source cuts. We then test a simultaneous allocation
to the single copy of each positive cut. A fixed bilinear Walsh choice
fails on an actual ten-factor input; a different coefficient choice
repairs that failure and all commuting inputs. The unrestricted
noncommuting allocation is not proved below.

**Lemma 50A (one positive target detects both other sides of a cut
triad).** Let `pi,sigma` be distinct negative cuts, and let
`tau=pi+sigma` be their proper positive agreement cut. All original
factors are actual real atoms. On `H_pi` put

```text
K_(pi,tau)=ran(Q_pi Q_sigma)+ran(Q_pi Q_tau).
```

There is an explicit complex-linear partial isometry

```text
T_(pi,tau):H_pi -> H_tau,
T_(pi,tau)^* T_(pi,tau)=P_(K_(pi,tau)),                  (P50.1)
```

with the two exact properties

```text
T_(pi,tau)x=0 iff Q_sigma x=Q_tau x=0,   x in H_pi,
T_(pi,tau)x=x,             x in H_pi intersection H_tau. (P50.2)
```

All cell multiplicities are included. In particular its kernel is
orthogonal to `H_sigma`. No lower bound on intermediate dimensions
or self-duality of intermediate irreducibles is assumed.

**Proof.**

1. Use the four common cells `A,B,C,D`, with cuts
   `pi=AB|CD`, `sigma=AC|BD`, `tau=AD|BC`. Each cell
   representation is a tensor product of actual real atoms,
   hence is self-dual. Write its unitary isotypic decomposition
   as `X=sum_lambda V_lambda tensor M_(X,lambda)`.
   Self-duality gives equal dimensions of `M_(X,lambda)`
   and `M_(X,lambda*)`. Fix a complex-linear unitary
   between these multiplicity spaces by choosing orthonormal
   bases. This does not identify inequivalent irreducible
   representations: it identifies their multiplicity spaces.
2. On a four-cell isotypic component, `H_pi` has a row
   singlet line precisely for labels `(lambda,lambda*,mu,mu*)`.
   Lemma 29A gives the following two kinds of its components
   in `K_(pi,tau)`:

   ```text
   shared with sigma: (lambda,lambda*,lambda*,lambda),
   shared with tau:   (lambda,lambda*,lambda,lambda*).     (P50.3)
   ```

   Each line is tensored with all four multiplicity spaces.
   The overlap `1/d_lambda` is nonzero, so the ranges in the
   definition of `K_(pi,tau)` include the entire indicated
   row component. The two kinds coincide exactly when
   `lambda=lambda*`; otherwise their cell supports are
   orthogonal. Different first-cell labels are also orthogonal.
3. On a component shared with `tau`, use
   `d_lambda Q_tau` restricted to its row line and
   multiplicity space. Lemma 29A makes this an isometry
   into the agreement singlet with the same four labels.
   This prescription includes every self-dual component
   shared with `sigma`, without counting it twice.
4. For non-self-dual `lambda`, map the component shared
   with `sigma` into the agreement component with labels

   ```text
   (lambda,lambda,lambda*,lambda*).                     (P50.4)
   ```

   Replace its unit row singlet by a fixed unit agreement
   singlet. On the multiplicity spaces, use the fixed
   unitaries

   ```text
   M_(B,lambda*) -> M_(B,lambda),
   M_(D,lambda)  -> M_(D,lambda*),
   ```

   and the identity on `A,C`. These are spaces in the
   original cell representations; both requested labels
   occur by self-duality. Their dimensions agree, so the
   line replacement tensored with these unitaries is an
   actual complex-linear isometry into `H_tau`.
5. For a fixed non-self-dual first-cell label `lambda`, the
   output of step 3 has `C` label `lambda`, whereas the
   output of step 4 has `C` label `lambda*`. They are
   orthogonal. Outputs with different first-cell labels are
   orthogonal as well. Thus all the component maps combine
   to one isometry from `K_(pi,tau)` into the single actual
   target `H_tau`. Extend it by zero on the orthogonal
   complement to obtain `(P50.1)`.
6. For `x in H_pi`, orthogonality to `ran(Q_pi Q_sigma)`
   is equivalent to `Q_sigma x=0`, by taking the adjoint;
   the corresponding assertion holds for `tau`. This proves
   the kernel statement in `(P50.2)`.
7. Lemma 27A identifies `H_pi intersection H_tau` with
   invariants independently on all four cells. This is
   exactly the trivial-label component of step 3, where
   `d_lambda=1` and `Q_tau` is the identity. Thus the map
   fixes that intersection. QED.

**Corollary 50B (distinct interacting agreements, with arbitrary
intermediate labels).** Suppose the positive agreements of all unordered
pairs of nonorthogonal negative cut spaces are distinct. Then

```text
r -> (T_(pi_i,pi_i+pi_j) r_i)_(i<j, Q_i Q_j!=0)        (P50.5)
```

is injective on the entire original `Rel`, and supplies Q3 on the
whole actual input. There is no cut-count or spectral-radius bound.

**Proof.** Each coordinate is an actual proper positive cut, counted
once. If every coordinate vanishes, `(P50.2)` gives
`<r_i,r_j>=0` for every interacting pair; the other pairs are already
orthogonal. Thus `0=||F r||^2=sum_i ||r_i||^2`, and `r=0`.
Include the target in `H_free direct_sum E_prop` and apply
Proposition 28. Unlike Theorem 29, this argument imposes no
non-self-dual overlap bound. QED.

The corollary is one successful consumption of the new map. The
unrestricted caller also includes collisions between agreement cuts.
For that caller use the whole coefficient family below, rather than
introducing multiple copies of a collided positive target.

Let `B=F_2^L/span{all-ones}` and let `ell=ell_M` for a nonempty even
minus set. Put `B^+=ker ell` and `N={pi:ell(pi)=1}`, including indices
whose spaces are zero. Choose one negative class `pi_0`. For each
proper positive `tau` and negative `pi`, set `sigma=pi+tau` and use
Lemma 50A. With arbitrary complex scalar coefficients define

```text
A_0(r)=F r,
A_tau(r)=sum_(pi in N) alpha_(tau,pi) T_(pi,tau) r_pi,
                            tau in B^+\{0}.             (P50.6)
```

Every output uses precisely one original positive target. If the
proper outputs are injective on `Rel`, they supply `(P28.2)`.
This is a sufficient full-scope construction attempt. It is stronger
than the original RC demand because it does not use `H_free`; failure
of this family would not by itself disprove Q3 or the original RC map.

**Proposition 50C (a fixed bilinear Walsh choice cannot be universal).**
Take ten positions and minus set `{1,3}`. For every bilinear form
`b:B^+ times B^+ -> F_2` fixed independently of the atom tuple, the
choice

```text
alpha_(tau,pi)=(-1)^b(tau,pi+pi_0)                       (P50.7)
```

fails to be injective on `Rel` for some actual `SU(2)` atom tuple
with this same position set and signs. This includes forms obtained
from any fixed linear isomorphism of `B^+` with its dual. The
counterexample concerns the proposed map, not the Q3 inequality.

**Proof.**

1. In `B^+`, let `C0` be the three-dimensional subspace
   spanned by the pair indicators `{5,6},{7,8},{9,10}`.
   These classes are independent modulo all-ones. On `C0`,
   the function `q(u)=b(u,u)` is a polynomial of degree
   at most two in three binary coordinates, with `q(0)=0`.
   The sum of its values over all eight vectors is zero
   modulo two: every degree-one or degree-two monomial
   is one an even number of times. Consequently `q` cannot
   be one on all seven nonzero vectors. Choose nonzero
   `tau in C0` with `b(tau,tau)=0`.
2. Represent this class by the union `Z` of its selected
   pairs, put `Y={3,4}`, and let `X` be the remaining
   positions. All three blocks have size at least two.
   Their minus counts are respectively one, one, and zero.
   Their block-union cut space has exactly two negative
   classes, `pi_X,pi_Y`, and one proper positive class,
   `tau=pi_Z=pi_X+pi_Y`.
3. Construct a unit invariant in each block that excludes
   every cut splitting that block. Here are explicit modules
   and the required simultaneous exclusion. Write `V_k` for
   the `SU(2)` irreducible of highest weight `k`. In a block
   of size `m`, assign `m-1` small modules `V_s` and one
   module `V_((m-1)s)`, where `s` is a positive integer.
   Couple the small modules through their unique Cartan
   component `V_((m-1)s)`, and take its unit invariant
   pairing with the large module. Call the resulting unit
   block invariant `v_block`.
4. If a proper subset of that block contains `a` small
   positions and does not contain the large one, its support
   in `v_block` is the Cartan component `V_(as)`.
   If the subset contains the large position, its support
   is dual to the Cartan component of the complementary
   small positions. Thus for every split block the selected
   factors of its invariant have a single nonzero highest
   weight between `s` and `(m-1)s`. This follows by factoring
   the unique highest component of the small tensor product,
   and then by Schur's lemma for the invariant pairing.
5. Let the sizes be `m_X,m_Y,m_Z`. Choose

   ```text
   s_X=1,
   s_Y=(m_X-1)s_X+1,
   s_Z=(m_X-1)s_X+(m_Y-1)s_Y+1.                         (P50.8)
   ```

   If a cut splits any blocks, choose the split block with
   largest scale. Its selected highest weight is strictly
   greater than the sum of the largest possible selected
   weights from the smaller-scale split blocks. Their tensor
   product has no invariant: the product of the smaller
   modules has highest weights at most their sum and hence
   cannot contain the dual of the larger module.
6. Put `v=v_X tensor v_Y tensor v_Z`, reordered into the
   original ten positions. Whole blocks remain invariant
   under either cut average. Step 5 proves

   ```text
   Q_pi v=v  if pi is a union of X,Y,Z,
   Q_pi v=0  otherwise.                                (P50.9)
   ```

   These are actual cut projections, including all other
   constituents and invariant channels of the ten modules.
   Every module is a nontrivial self-dual actual `SU(2)`
   atom; no added factors or external target spaces are used.
7. Define a nonzero full-source relation by

   ```text
   r_(pi_X)=v,   r_(pi_Y)=-v,   r_pi=0 otherwise.
   ```

   Its merge is zero. For a proper positive class other
   than `tau`, `(P50.9)` and `(P50.2)` give zero in
   `(P50.6)`: neither that class nor its sum with either
   source class fixes `v`. For `tau`, both partial
   isometries fix `v`, so the output is

   ```text
   [(-1)^b(tau,pi_X+pi_0)
     -(-1)^b(tau,pi_Y+pi_0)] v=0,                       (P50.10)
   ```

   because the ratio of the two signs is
   `(-1)^b(tau,pi_X+pi_Y)=(-1)^b(tau,tau)=1`.
   The pure output is also zero. This proves the stated
   map failure on a valid full-target tuple. QED.

This rules out only coefficients from a globally fixed bilinear
Walsh form. It does not rule out coefficients chosen from the actual
cut arrangement, or general scalar coefficients in `(P50.6)`.
The first natural replacement can be tested without changing the
source, target, or atom tuple.

**Proposition 50D (one universal coefficient choice repairs all
commuting arrangements).** Assign distinct positive real numbers
`t_pi` to all negative cut indices. Assign distinct nonnegative integer
exponents `k_tau` to all positive cut indices, with `k_0=0`. Use

```text
alpha_(tau,pi)=t_pi^k_tau.                              (P50.11)
```

If all negative cut projections commute, `(A_0,(A_tau)_(tau!=0))`
is injective on the entire `O`; its proper outputs give RC on `Rel`.
These same coefficients also detect the nonzero relation of
Proposition 50C, whether or not the other negative projections commute.

**Proof.**

1. First check that on a commuting arrangement the triadic
   maps reduce to common-intersection projections. Lemma 29A
   shows that a shared nontrivial four-cell channel between
   two commuting cuts is impossible: its two distinct singlet
   lines have overlap modulus `1/d` strictly between zero
   and one. Thus `ran(Q_pi Q_sigma)` is their common
   four-cell invariant space.
2. A nontrivial channel shared between `pi` and `tau`
   would also supply a nontrivial shared channel between
   `pi` and `sigma`: its multiplicity spaces have labels
   `(lambda,lambda*,lambda,lambda*)`, and self-duality of
   `C,D` supplies the alternative labels
   `(lambda,lambda*,lambda*,lambda)` with the same nonzero
   multiplicities. This would contradict step 1. Hence
   `K_(pi,tau)` is just the common invariant space, and
   Lemma 50A's map on it is the identity.
3. Decompose `H` into the joint zero/one spaces `K_J` of
   Theorem 30. For nonempty `J` with `K_J!=0`, that theorem's
   refinement argument gives `J=pi_J+C_J`, where `C_J`
   is the positive subspace of the binary span of `J`.
   For a source in its `K_J` component, step 2 makes the
   output at `tau` zero unless `tau in C_J`; if it is,
   the output lies in the same `K_J` and is

   ```text
   sum_(pi in J) t_pi^k_tau r_(pi,J),  tau in C_J.        (P50.12)
   ```

   This includes `tau=0`, which is the corresponding part
   of `F`. There are `|J|=|C_J|` source and target indices.
4. The square matrix `(t_pi^k_tau)_(tau in C_J,pi in J)`
   is invertible. To verify this without a determinant
   assumption, a nonzero real polynomial with `m` nonzero
   monomials has at most `m-1` distinct positive roots.
   Divide by its lowest power of `t`; differentiation leaves
   at most `m-1` monomials, and Rolle's theorem proves the
   assertion by induction. A linear dependence between the
   `m=|C_J|` rows would give such a polynomial vanishing
   at the `m` distinct positive numbers `t_pi`, which is
   impossible. The matrix is real, so this also proves its
   invertibility over the complex field and on `K_J`-valued
   coefficient vectors.
5. Different joint spaces are orthogonal. Step 3 makes every
   output preserve them, even where several joint spaces
   use the same actual positive target. Thus their output
   contributions cannot cancel. Step 4 proves injectivity
   on all of `O`, using one copy of each positive cut.
   On `Rel`, the zero output vanishes, leaving an injection
   into `E_prop`. Proposition 28 supplies the whole input.
6. On the explicit relation of Proposition 50C, the only
   possibly nonzero proper output is still at its `tau`.
   It is `(t_(pi_X)^k_tau-t_(pi_Y)^k_tau)v`, which is
   nonzero because the two nodes are distinct positive
   numbers and `k_tau>0`. Thus the replacement construction
   passes the exact instance that killed `(P50.7)`. QED.

**Proposition 50E (the same detector family contains the established
partial cup matching suppliers).** Suppose `I,J` and the distinct
positive crossing pair targets satisfy Lemma 49A. There are explicit
coefficients in `(P50.6)` making its proper outputs injective on the
entire coupled `Rel`. This includes the full seven-factor input
`A^6,B` of Theorem 49D, with the bound `1/91`.

**Proof.**

1. If a positive pair `tau={i,j}` crosses `pi` and has
   the same actual atom at its two positions, the two
   off-diagonal cells `B,C` are those single positions.
   For a self-dual atom their labels force every row
   component into `(P50.3)`. For a paired atom, the two
   single-position labels either agree, giving the first
   kind of `(P50.3)`, or are dual, giving the second.
   These are every row component, with arbitrary remaining
   cell multiplicities. Consequently `K_(pi,tau)=H_pi`
   and `T_(pi,tau)` is a whole-cut isometry.
2. For each paid `pi in I`, put `alpha_(tau_pi,pi)=1`;
   put all other coefficients equal to zero. Distinctness
   of the targets gives the whole-source isometry on `O_I`
   inside the actual positive direct sum. On `Rel`, its
   kernel is the unpaid merge kernel, which is zero by
   Lemma 49A. The same norm argument gives
   `c/(c+|I|)`, and hence `1/91` for Theorem 49D.
   This tests the new triadic maps on that entire original
   input, including paired atoms and all coupled relations.
   QED.

**Proposition 50F (positive-node determinants implement partial
matching, including a coupled noncommuting test).** In the setting of
Proposition 50E, the coefficients can also have the positive-node form
`(P50.11)`. There are orders of the nodes and exponents for which
`t_pi=t^a_pi`, with distinct positive integer `a_pi`, makes the
augmented map `(A_0,(A_tau))` injective for every sufficiently large
real `t`. This holds on the entire `O`, not only separately on the
paid and unpaid relation spaces.

For six `SU(2)` fundamental modules with minus positions `1,2`, one
explicit choice of orders works at `t=16!`. It detects the entire
eleven-dimensional `Rel` of this noncommuting input.

**Proof.**

1. Discard zero source spaces when forming a matrix; their
   indices can still receive distinct nodes. Order the
   unpaid source indices first, and then the paid indices
   `pi_1,...,pi_m`. Assign strictly increasing positive
   integer exponents `a_pi` in that order. Put `k_0=0`
   and `k_(tau_pi_j)=j`; give the unused positive targets
   any other distinct positive integer exponents.
2. Let `r_j=dim H_(pi_j)` and `D_J=dim O_J`.
   Injectivity of `F_J` supplies `D_J` independent coordinate
   functionals on `H` whose restriction to `F_J` is
   invertible. From each assigned `H_(tau_pi_j)` choose
   `r_j` independent coordinate functionals on the isometric
   image of `T_(pi_j,tau_pi_j)`. These select a square
   minor of the augmented map, of size
   `D=D_J+sum_j r_j=dim O`.
3. In a determinant term, each column from `H_pi` supplies
   the factor `t^a_pi k_tau` when assigned to a row of
   target `tau`. The `D_J` pure rows have exponent zero.
   The maximal exponent is attained only when every unpaid
   column goes to a pure row, and each paid source block
   goes to its assigned target row block. To check this,
   an inverted assignment of two unequal source exponents
   to two unequal target exponents increases its exponent
   after swapping, by the positive product of their two
   differences. Sorting gives the claimed assignment;
   the row-block sizes agree with the column-block sizes.
4. The coefficient at this maximal power is, up to the
   chosen determinant ordering, the nonzero determinant
   of the selected `F_J` minor times the determinants of
   the selected whole-cut isometries. All internal
   permutations within equally weighted blocks sum to
   exactly those determinants. Thus the selected minor
   is a nonzero polynomial in `t`. Its leading term
   dominates for all sufficiently large positive `t`.
   The entire augmented map is then injective. On `Rel`,
   its pure output is zero, so its proper outputs supply
   the original RC demand.
5. For the explicit six-factor instance, all eight negative
   sources are pairs `1x,2x` with `x in {3,4,5,6}`.
   Choose unpaid source `26` and the following seven
   paid assignments, in the stated order:

   ```text
   source pi_j       positive target tau_pi_j
   13                34
   14                45
   15                56
   16                36
   23                35
   24                46
   25                12.                               (P50.14)
   ```

   Each target has equal fundamental modules and crosses
   its source. All seven proper positive pair targets are
   used once. Proposition 50E makes their triadic maps
   whole-cut isometries. The unpaid merge is the single
   cut's isometric inclusion into `H`.
6. The fundamental fusion rule gives
   `dim Inv(V_1^tensor4)=2` and
   `dim Inv(V_1^tensor6)=5`. Every source and target
   pair-cut space has dimension two, so `dim O=16`.
   The merge is surjective: cup products span the
   six-fundamental invariant space, and a product using
   cup `12` is rewritten with either other cup `xy`
   by `epsilon_12 epsilon_xy=epsilon_1x epsilon_2y
   -epsilon_1y epsilon_2x`. Every resulting product
   belongs to a negative pair source. This is the same
   invariant-tensor spanning argument checked in Lemma 40A.
   Therefore `dim Rel=16-5=11`.
7. Set `a_26=1`, `a_(pi_j)=j+1` and
   `k_(tau_pi_j)=j` for `j=1,...,7`.
   Choose the two pure rows as inner products with an
   orthonormal basis of the unpaid image. Choose each
   target's orthonormal basis to be the image of its
   assigned source basis. The leading block matrices
   of step 4 are all identities. The selected
   sixteen-by-sixteen minor has leading coefficient one
   and degree

   ```text
   E=2 sum_(j=1)^7 j(j+1)=336.                          (P50.15)
   ```

   Every matrix entry before its monomial factor has
   modulus at most one: the pure maps are isometric
   inclusions and the triadic maps are contractions.
   The unique nonzero maximal-degree determinant term
   is the identity block assignment. Each of the at
   most `16!-1` other terms has degree at most `335`
   and coefficient modulus at most one. Consequently

   ```text
   |det A_minor(t)|
      >=t^336-(16!-1)t^335>0,   t>=16!.                 (P50.16)
   ```

   This gives the stated exact coefficient choice without
   a certificate search.
8. This is genuinely a noncommuting test. Negative cuts
   `13` and `14` have four cells of sizes `1,1,1,3`.
   Their shared fundamental channel has overlap modulus
   `1/2` on every vector of their two-dimensional cut
   spaces. Their projections therefore do not commute.
   Nevertheless the determinant construction is injective
   on all sixteen source dimensions and hence all eleven
   relation dimensions at once. Proposition 28 consumes
   this full actual input. QED.

**Final independent double-check and original-consumer replay.** Checked

For the non-self-dual transport, flipped the `B,D` multiplicity

For the commuting supplier, used actual cell self-duality to exclude

Every accepted supplier lands in the original proper positive cut
spaces. The finite-input step of Proposition 28 consumes each stated

for every 0!=r in Rel,
sum_(tau in B^+\{0})
